roles.name: guest
roles.description: A non-authenticated visitor who can browse public discussions and content but cannot participate, post, comment, or vote.

roles.name: member
roles.description: A registered user who can create posts, comment on discussions, vote, report inappropriate content, edit or delete their own contributions within certain time limits, and manage their own account settings.

roles.name: moderator
roles.description: A trusted community member or staff appointed to monitor discussions, review reports, edit or remove inappropriate content, suspend or ban users, and enforce community guidelines.

roles.name: admin
roles.description: The highest level role responsible for all system settings, user management (including moderator appointments and global bans), board structure, category definitions, policy configurations, and viewing analytical or audit logs.

# Table of Contents: Political/Economic Discussion Board Service Requirements

## Document Purpose and Use
This Table of Contents provides an authoritative overview of all business requirements and related documentation for the political/economic discussion board service (polEcoBoard). It functions both as a navigational aid and as the primary roadmap for backend developers and all stakeholders. The structure, order, and relationships of the requirements are clearly described so that readers can efficiently find and reference each aspect of the system. All document titles are provided as descriptive links for clarity.

## Document List and Navigation
Below is the complete list of requirements and specification documents prepared for polEcoBoard, presented in recommended reading and implementation order. Each document serves a unique function in defining the system's business context, user roles, functional flows, and operational expectations.

| Document Title | Description | Link |
|---------------|-------------|------|
| Service Overview and Business Rationale | Introduces the mission, core value proposition, target audience, and business logic of the entire discussion board. Establishes the vision for the project and outlines fundamental success metrics. | [Service Overview and Business Rationale](./01-service-overview.md) |
| Underlying Business Problems and User Needs | Analyzes market needs, user pain points, and concrete opportunities that justify the board's creation, with personas and data-driven rationale. | [Underlying Business Problems and User Needs](./02-problem-definition.md) |
| User Roles and Authentication Framework | Defines all user roles (guest, member, moderator, admin), permissions by role, authentication and session flows, and a detailed permission matrix. Specifies role boundaries and security requirements. | [User Roles and Authentication Framework](./03-user-roles-auth.md) |
| User Journey and Participation Processes | Maps the end-to-end user journey, from registration to ongoing interaction, with detailed business flows for all participation types (posting, commenting, account operations). | [User Journey and Participation Processes](./04-user-journey.md) |
| Functional Requirements Specification | States all business functions, rules, and workflows (posting, commenting, moderation, notifications, etc.) in EARS format and natural language, covering every business process. | [Functional Requirements Specification](./05-functional-requirements.md) |
| Non-functional Requirements (Performance, Privacy, Compliance) | Outlines backend-facing business goals for performance, scalability, reliability, usability, privacy/security, and regulatory compliance, in business terms. | [Non-functional Requirements (Performance, Privacy, Compliance)](./06-non-functional-requirements.md) |
| User Scenarios and Exception Handling | Presents exhaustive user scenarios (including normal, alternate, and error flows) to clarify required system behaviors and recovery paths for all user and role types. | [User Scenarios and Exception Handling](./07-user-scenarios.md) |
| Business Logic, Rules, and Validation Constraints | Captures business logic and validation requirements for participation, moderation, and content standards (post/comment length, eligibility, moderation escalation, etc.) with worked examples. | [Business Logic, Rules, and Validation Constraints](./08-business-rules.md) |
| Integrations and Conceptual Data Flows | Details the required third-party service integrations (analytics, anti-spam, notification, single sign-on, etc.) and provides conceptual data flow diagrams for business boundaries. | [Integrations and Conceptual Data Flows](./09-integrations-dataflow.md) |
| Operations, Event Monitoring, and Reporting | Defines requirements for ongoing service monitoring, administrative analytics, business event handling (moderation/reporting flow), and business/incident reporting. | [Operations, Event Monitoring, and Reporting](./10-operations-reporting.md) |

## Related Documentation
All documents in this collection are interconnected and jointly define the business requirements for polEcoBoard. This Table of Contents serves as the entry point and reference map for navigating the complete requirements set. Readers are encouraged to proceed in the order presented for maximum clarity, or to jump directly to functional or operational documents using the links above.

> *Developer Note: This document defines business requirements only. All technical implementations (architecture, APIs, database design, etc.) are at the discretion of the development team.*

# Service Overview: polEcoBoard

## Service Vision and Mission
polEcoBoard is designed around the mission of fostering informed, respectful, and impactful discussions about political and economic issues. The vision is to provide a modern, open, and trusted space for civil and fact-based discourse, empowering participants to share perspectives, debate meaningfully, and contribute to socially significant conversations. A primary business goal is to address fragmentation and polarization in digital discourse by emphasizing source-driven, transparent, and inclusive participation, governed by explicit community standards and robust moderation mechanisms.

- THE service SHALL empower informed dialogue by enabling structured, transparent, and equitable discussion environments.
- THE service SHALL always prioritize inclusive access across diverse backgrounds, expertise levels, and geographies, to facilitate global participation.
- THE service SHALL enforce community guidelines in all spaces to maintain civil discourse and safeguard participant well-being.

## Target Audience
Primary user segments include:
- Civically engaged citizens seeking to deliberate on political and economic matters
- Students, educators, and researchers in social sciences, policy, or economics
- Policy makers, NGO staff, and journalists conducting analysis or seeking informed views
- Community leaders and activists pursuing collaborative approaches to public issues
- The general public interested in nonpartisan, high-quality, and transparent debate

- WHEN onboarding new users from any of these segments, THE system SHALL provide pathways to discover relevant topics and communities aligned to their interests.
- THE system SHALL accommodate guests (read-only access), members (active participation), moderators (community standards enforcement), and admins (operations and policy management), as described in [User Roles, Authentication, and Permissions Overview](./03-user-roles-auth.md).

## Key Features
- Topic-based board and nested category organization covering core political and economic subjects
- Post creation with contextual, structured templates and clearly surfaced community guidelines
- Threaded comment and reply chains supporting in-depth, multi-layered discussions
- Voting mechanisms (upvote/downvote) that enhance visibility of valued content and provide transparent community feedback
- Robust reporting and moderation workflows to monitor and prevent misuse, ensuring fast response to flagged behavior
- Configurable notifications and personalized activity feeds for engagement and user awareness
- Gamification (badges, reputation, milestones) to incentivize positive, sustained participation
- Role-based access and permissions framework; explicit separation of guest, member, moderator, admin capabilities (full structure at [User Roles, Authentication, and Permissions Overview](./03-user-roles-auth.md))
- Privacy-centric account management and member settings, with transparent user data practices
- Integration readiness for analytics, fact-checking, or educational partners, supporting informed and evidence-based dialogue

- WHEN a user creates a post or comment, THE system SHALL validate input against content rules and enforce template completeness (see [Functional Requirements Document](./05-functional-requirements.md)).
- WHEN moderation is required, THE system SHALL provide workflows enabling efficient escalation, decision logging, and user notification to uphold transparent governance.
- THE permissions system SHALL guarantee that each user may only perform actions consistent with their assigned role (see [User Roles, Authentication, and Permissions Overview](./03-user-roles-auth.md)).

## Business Model

### Why This Service Exists
Digital forums for political/economic discussion often fall short due to polarization, misinformation, lack of constructive moderation, and failure to surface credible voices. Most platforms do not sufficiently support rigorous, nonpartisan, well-moderated debate—resulting in poor user trust and limited appeal to professionals or informed amateurs seeking more than sensational content. polEcoBoard fills this critical gap by:
- Establishing a high-integrity, transparent community built around clear, consistently enforced standards
- Prioritizing evidence-based contribution through structured workflows, fact validation, and community recognition
- Creating a trusted, differentiated engagement model for NGOs, researchers, and policy organizations seeking reliable digital forums
- Enabling regular users to become respected participants through measurable feedback (reputation, voting, moderation)

- THE existence of the service SHALL be justified by its unique enablement of trusted, structured, and constructive political/economic discourse online, with accountable moderation not found in legacy forums.

### Revenue Strategy
- Subscriptions: Premium tiers offer additional analytics, advanced badge displays, ad-free or more personalized experiences, early feature access, or exclusive event invitations.
- Sponsored Content: Carefully screened partnerships for promoted posts, policy Q&A, or expert panels—clear labels and non-intrusive display mandatory.
- Transactional Models: Events such as sponsored AMAs (Ask Me Anything), verified expert sessions, or content partnerships with educational consortia and NGOs.
- B2B/Institutional Packages: NGOs or advocacy groups can host branded sub-boards, access enhanced reporting, and implement custom moderation flows via paid service agreements.

- THE service revenue model SHALL avoid disruptive advertising, prioritizing member trust and integrity.
- WHEN generating revenue through partnerships or events, THE system SHALL maintain role-based content separation so no group can influence core discussion space unfairly.

### Growth Plan
- Word-of-mouth growth driven by user reputation systems and demonstrable quality of discourse (participation, voting, and reporting activity)
- Strategic partnerships with universities, think tanks, and research/education organizations for recruitment and community enrichment
- High-profile collaborative events including policy debates, expert Q&A, or co-hosted sessions with influential partners
- Continuous product evolution via regular user feedback cycles, A/B-tested feature rollouts, and transparent change logs
- Gamification strategies encouraging both new user retention and long-term engagement via milestone recognition, streak tracking, and standing in reputation/ranking lists

- WHEN onboarding new institutional partners, THE system SHALL support branded community spaces and optimized onboarding experiences to accelerate cohort engagement.
- THE service SHALL track user, post, and event growth rates and support scaling operations, via automatic moderation tools and engaged community stewards.

### Success Metrics
- Monthly Active Users (MAU), Daily Active Users (DAU), and average session duration tracked as core growth and engagement signals
- Engagement rates: posts, comments, and votes per active user (qualifies for business incentives or rewards)
- Community health metrics: ratio of positive to negative reports, average report resolution time, post/comment flagging rates
- User growth rates compared to registration churn and retention curves
- Partnership metrics: number, diversity, and visibility of NGOs, professionals, and institutions partnering or commissioning sub-boards
- Notable press mentions, research citations, and event participations reflecting external impact

- THE platform SHALL provide tracking and reporting for all above metrics to admins and authorized partners to guide business evolution.

## Market Positioning
Platforms addressing political/economic discussion span from broad social networks (Reddit, Quora) to specialist blogs or restricted professional bodies. polEcoBoard is set apart by:
- Transparent and enforceable community guidelines applied consistently and visibly—no ambiguity or hidden moderation decisions
- A business requirement for evidence-based, reasoned argument, with structural support for citing sources and integrating fact-checks (integration referenced in [Integrations and Dataflow](./09-integrations-dataflow.md))
- Role-based workflow and governance enforced at all business and operational layers—for example, moderators act under audit, admins appoint and oversee with documented policy (clear delineation found in [User Roles, Authentication, and Permissions Overview](./03-user-roles-auth.md), with escalation logic defined in [Functional Requirements Document](./05-functional-requirements.md))
- Dedicated, category-focused boards and sub-boards supporting nuanced, high-quality debate distinct from generalist platforms driven by ad volume or ideology
- Integration channels for NGOs, policy-makers, and research institutes to create branded collaboration spaces, supporting institutional trust and visibility

- WHEN compared to existing solutions, THE service SHALL emphasize measurable credibility, civility, and actionable insight—eschewing rapid, low-quality content churn—and providing robust audit trails and reputation signals for all participants.

## Success Metrics (Recap)
- Quantitative: active user growth (MAU, DAU), average session duration, engagement rate per user, moderation/response efficiency, number and status of partnerships
- Qualitative: Net Promoter Score (NPS), community health self-assessment, user trust and influence within policy or academic discourse, media reputation and incident resilience
- Platform robustness: time to flag abuse, incident response time, post-incident user retention

- THE monitoring and reporting of all metrics above SHALL be made available to authorized roles in the system (see [Operations and Reporting Specification](./10-operations-reporting.md)).

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["User Participation"] --> B["Reputation Growth"]
    B --> C["Event/Partner Opportunities"]
    C --> D["Community Impact & Trust"]
    A --> E["Voting/Moderation Workflow"]
    E --> F["Transparency & Audit Logs"]
    F --> D
    D --> G["Sustained Platform Growth"]
```

polEcoBoard is founded on the business requirement that measured, transparent, and role-based engagement provides a superior environment for political and economic conversation—with every process governed by explicit business logic, measurable community health outcomes, and regulatory-compliant, developer-autonomous implementation. All technical implementation details are determined by the development team; this specification defines what the service must achieve in business terms.

# Problem Definition for polEcoBoard

## Problem Statement

The digital environment for political and economic discourse is fragmented, frequently hostile, and inefficient by design and legacy assumptions. Users seeking to contribute to meaningful debate are routinely faced with platforms that encourage shallow engagement, tolerate or even incentivize uncivil behavior, and offer little to no recourse for abuse. Mainstream social spaces are typically not optimized for constructive, in-depth, or policy-centered discussion, and often lack mechanisms for fair and transparent moderation. There is a persistent, demonstrable gap for a dedicated system where users of all experience and expertise levels can take part in structured, civil, and fact-based discussion around complex policy and economics topics, with clear pathways for participation, moderation, and governance.

WHILE current discourse platforms continue to prioritize scale and sensational content, THE need for evidence-driven, trustworthy, and accountable digital discussion remains unmet. WHEN individuals with deep policy knowledge or contrary views try to participate, THE system currently SHALL not surface their contributions nor protect them from coordinated attacks. WHEN incoming users attempt to navigate communities, THE system SHALL not orient them effectively, leading to disengagement and exclusion. These system-level gaps perpetuate toxicity, groupthink, and underrepresentation of diverse expertise in political and economic dialogue. The absence of robust reporting, reputation, and role-based participation tools is a critical flaw across the sector.

## Pain Points

- WHEN users interested in policy and economics seek substantive debate, THE available communities SHALL often present high noise and limited signal, increasing user frustration and disengagement.
- WHEN trolling, ad hominem attacks, or personal abuse occurs, THE system SHALL rarely deliver rapid, transparent, or just moderation, causing repeated cycles of victimization and loss of trust.
- IF a participant operates anonymously, THEN THE system SHALL lack role granularity, which allows bad actors to evade accountability while discouraging expert and invested member participation.
- WHEN moderation is perceived as inconsistent or biased, THE system SHALL foster distrust and reduce overall engagement, often pushing marginalized or diverse voices out of discourse.
- WHEN thoughtful, high-quality contributions are uploaded, THE system SHALL frequently allow these to be eclipsed or drowned by clickbait, sensational content, or organized brigades.
- WHEN onboarding for new users is unclear or overwhelming—whether due to confusing navigation, opaque community rules, or weak onboarding workflows—THE system SHALL drive away potentially valuable participants before they meaningfully engage.
- IF reporting systems or voting mechanisms are poorly designed or hard to use, THEN THE system SHALL discourage constructive feedback and flagging of negative behaviors, letting problems fester.
- WHEN platforms fail to surface or signal reputation, THE system SHALL make it impossible for users to identify constructive contributors, experts, or recurring offenders, reducing trust in the community’s ability to self-manage.
- IF community governance is not participatory or lacks transparency, THEN the user base SHALL feel disenfranchised and less inclined to help moderate or improve the space.
- WHEN privacy, data protection, or advertising practices are unclear or overly intrusive, THE system SHALL drive privacy-conscious and professional users away, stunting the growth of a robust, trustworthy user base.
- WHEN moderation tooling is inadequate, THEN the burden on community volunteers and professional staff increases, resulting in burnout, inconsistent enforcement, or turnover, further eroding trust and continuity.
- WHEN escalation paths for severe abuse or systemic issues are not clear, THEN both members and moderators SHALL feel unsupported and at risk of exposure to harm.
- WHEN user interface and experience are outdated or lack expected modernical notification, navigation, or participation tools, THE system SHALL make it harder for users to stay engaged and for staff to efficiently maintain community health.
- WHEN platforms employ business models driven predominantly by advertising or virality, THE system SHALL often misalign incentives by optimizing for engagement instead of quality, thus perpetuating shallow or divisive discourse.

## Opportunities for Impact

- WHEN polEcoBoard enables evidence-driven, respectful, and thoughtful discussion, THE platform SHALL fulfill a critical need for high-quality political and economics communities disenfranchised by mainstream social products.
- WHEN role-based permissions are clearly established and enforced (guest, member, moderator, admin), THE system SHALL foster user confidence and create a sense of trust and safety.
- WHEN robust voting, reputation, and signaling mechanisms are built in, THE system SHALL consistently highlight, elevate, and circulate high-quality, expert, and constructive content.
- WHEN complaint and reporting flows are transparent, actionable, and responsive, THE platform SHALL demonstrate accountability and engage users as participants in community health.
- WHEN onboarding is thoughtfully designed to educate, orient, and connect new users, THE system SHALL reduce churn and foster inclusive engagement from across the ideological and experience spectrum.
- WHEN real-time, relevant notifications and accessible moderation tools are provided, THE system SHALL keep stakeholders informed, streamline action, and reward positive engagement across roles.
- WHEN privacy-first authentication and granular data management policies are prioritized, THE system SHALL attract professional, expert, and privacy-conscious contributors.
- WHEN integrations (with fact-checking tools, academic indices, or external certification) are established, THE platform SHALL further differentiate itself, promote evidence-based deliberation, and counter mis/disinformation.
- WHEN governance and policy are intentionally transparent, participatory, and communicable, THE system SHALL empower the community, drive adoption, and improve the legitimacy of both content and moderation outcomes.

WHILE most platforms primarily serve guests and loosely-defined members, polEcoBoard’s model of explicit role differentiation maps responsibilities and privileges, creating clear user journeys and a pathway for invested users to take on community stewardship and eventually administrative duties.

## Market Gaps

- WHEN mainstream networks such as Facebook, Reddit, and Twitter prioritize limitless scale, THE resulting discourse platforms SHALL often devolve into superficial, polarized engagement at the expense of thoughtful debate and policy-informed analysis.
- IF specialized forums or policy-focused communities exist, THEN these SHALL typically suffer from underinvestment in technical tooling, role-based access, transparency, and trust systems—failing to sustain civil or expert-driven conversations over time.
- WHEN examining leading platforms, THE majority SHALL not offer robust role separation or reputation-based signaling; new contributors and experts compete for attention on equal footing with trolls or coordinated brigades.
- WHEN current options provide anonymity for psychological safety but fail to enforce role accountability, THE system SHALL often create an environment ripe for abuse or coordinated disruption.
- WHEN new market research and user surveys are analyzed, THE evidence SHALL indicate widespread dissatisfaction with both the quality of discourse and the experience of dealing with anti-social behavior, especially in contentious subject areas like politics and economics.
- WHEN privacy, data, and advertising policies prioritize engagement or cross-promotion at the expense of protection, THE system SHALL decrease its attractiveness to sensitive contributors, policy professionals, and those seeking open but safe civic dialogue.
- IF transparent governance and workflows for moderation, content reporting, or escalation are missing, THEN platforms SHALL be unable to win user trust or create sustained community engagement among diverse, rigorous, or underrepresented user bases.
- WHEN adversarial actors and false information campaigns increase in volume and sophistication, THE existing options SHALL lack business logic or tooling for scalable detection, response, and community resilience—undermining trust in the entire ecosystem.
- WHEN looking at legacy discussion boards, THE absence of features like real-time feedback, granular notification, robust reporting, and claims verification means the industry standard is out of sync with today’s user needs for accountability, speed, and user empowerment.
- WHEN analyzing competitors, none explicitly support participatory, multi-role, transparent governance for complex domains like political discourse and economic policy, thereby missing a critical success factor for stakeholder trust and community longevity.

## User Personas

### Guest

- Description: A non-authenticated visitor who browses debates and discussions on polEcoBoard. Seeks to gauge the quality, depth, and civility of the community before deciding to join as a member.
- Pain Points:
    - WHEN browsing, THE guest SHALL find it difficult to assess credibility and tone due to limited visibility of reputation/reputation signals and community norms.
    - WHEN attempting to interact, THE system SHALL restrict engagement options, potentially making it hard for guests to understand the value of full participation.
    - WHEN abuse or polarization is visible in public discussions, THE guest SHALL form a negative first impression, discouraging sign-up.
    - WHEN onboarding flows or calls-to-action are unclear, THE system SHALL miss opportunities to convert guests to active members.
- Opportunity:
    - WHEN guests are presented with intuitive registration flows, prominent displays of community standards, and visible examples of positive engagement, THE likelihood of guest-to-member conversion SHALL rise.
    - WHEN evidence of transparent moderation, rapid abuse handling, and trust signals is available, THE guest SHALL be more inclined to join and participate over the long term.

### Member

- Description: A registered user who participates in substantive debate, contributes posts and comments, votes on content, and helps surface quality discourse through reporting or other participation mechanisms on polEcoBoard.
- Pain Points:
    - WHEN sharing non-mainstream or specialist views, THE member SHALL fear retribution or hostile engagement from others unless robust moderation and protection are visible and trustworthy.
    - WHEN their contributions are lost in the noise or receive less visibility than lower-quality, more sensational submissions, THE member SHALL feel discouraged from repeat participation.
    - IF onboarding for new members omits guidance on posting etiquette, moderation policies, or voting/reporting rules, THEN THE member SHALL experience confusion or unintentional rule infractions.
    - WHEN unclear boundaries exist for reporting, voting, or editing, THE member SHALL struggle to exercise agency in community governance or content curation.
    - WHEN lacking meaningful reward, recognition, or impact, THE member SHALL disengage, reducing overall content quality and civility.
- Opportunity:
    - WHEN robust onboarding, transparent community standards, and role-based escalation paths exist, THE member SHALL feel empowered to contribute, report problems, and aspire to advanced roles like moderator.
    - WHEN reputation systems accurately surface expertise, civility, and impact, THE member SHALL be incentivized to engage meaningfully and consistently.

### Moderator

- Description: A trusted community peer or staff member on polEcoBoard responsible for reviewing reports, adjudicating conflicts, removing abusive or noncompliant content, and enforcing community rules in accordance with clear policy.
- Pain Points:
    - WHEN faced with high volumes of reports, unclear enforcement guidelines, or inadequate tooling, THE moderator SHALL encounter high emotional labor, slow decision cycles, and risk of inconsistent action.
    - WHEN enforcement decisions are second-guessed, lack transparency, or are overturned by admins without communication, THE moderator SHALL face backlash and stress from members, increasing attrition.
    - WHEN moderation actions are time-consuming or lack audit trail, THE system SHALL fail to support accountability, exposing moderators to accusation of bias or arbitrary authority.
    - WHEN moderators must operate across broad topic areas or without contextual support, THE system SHALL increase the risk of error or unfair enforcement.
- Opportunity:
    - WHEN empowerment tools, clear escalation paths, and transparent status logs are available, THE moderator SHALL act with consistency and confidence, leading to effective and fair outcomes.
    - WHEN moderator decisions are supported by timely admin feedback, training, and automated alerts, THE system SHALL improve team well-being, reduce burnout, and foster long-term retention.

### Admin

- Description: The highest-authority system and policy administrator for polEcoBoard, charged with managing categories, configuring enforcement standards, setting up role structures, overseeing all security/compliance, and maintaining overall platform health.
- Pain Points:
    - WHEN manual processes are required for moderator appointment, systemic configuration, audit review, or user management, THE admin SHALL experience inefficiencies and risk of error.
    - WHEN analytics, reporting, or audit trails are absent or inadequately detailed, THE admin SHALL be unable to ensure system policy compliance or respond proactively to issues.
    - IF evolving business or policy needs are not quickly adaptable via configuration, THEN THE admin SHALL experience lag in enforcement, increased operational cost, or inability to meet stakeholder expectations.
    - WHEN abusive patterns, coordinated attacks, or privacy threats go undetected, THE admin SHALL be unable to uphold trust, risking reputational and regulatory harm.
- Opportunity:
    - WHEN polEcoBoard enables administrative dashboards, automation of repetitive tasks, comprehensive analytics, and click-through audit trails, THE admin SHALL maintain compliance, policy agility, and a positive reputation for the platform.
    - WHEN configuration is streamlined, transparent, and logged, THE admin SHALL reduce risk, support system longevity, and empower all roles to operate efficiently and securely.

## Evidence Supporting Need for the Service

- WHEN reviewing academic literature and independent surveys, THE data SHALL consistently demonstrate user dissatisfaction with the tenor, safety, and substance of current online politics and economics communities; accounts of declining engagement, harassment, and polarization are well-documented.
- WHEN examining decline in participation rates after periods of absent or inconsistent moderation, THE effect SHALL be significant and measurable: platforms see both loss of contributor diversity and lower content quality metrics.
- WHEN user interviews are conducted or feedback is solicited from target personas (e.g., students, professionals, community leaders), THE need for clear role structures, transparent reputation, participatory governance, and stronger protection is continually reiterated.
- WHEN new regulations mandate enhanced privacy, transparent handling of misinformation, or timely response to abuse/incidents (such as GDPR, CCPA, and DSA), THE platform SHALL be required to adopt innovation in design and process to maintain compliance and competitive appeal.
- WHEN comparative market and case studies are performed—analyzing competitors who failed to implement robust role systems, proper reporting, or participatory governance—THE resulting community health and retention outcomes SHALL lag far behind those seen in more advanced, user-centric offerings.

---

polEcoBoard’s approach, design, and business logic are explicitly and uniquely grounded in comprehensive real-world pain points and empirically documented gaps. Every subsequent business requirement, feature, workflow, and validation for polEcoBoard SHALL be informed by these realities, with a commitment to user trust, operational sustainability, and measurable positive impact.

# polEcoBoard User Roles and Authentication Requirements

The polEcoBoard service provides a community platform for high-integrity political and economic discussions. The system is governed by strict role-based access and security controls to ensure user safety, content quality, and regulatory compliance.

## 1. Authentication Flow Requirements
- THE registration process SHALL require a unique, valid email and password for each account.
- WHEN a user submits registration details, THE system SHALL validate email format and password strength before account creation.
- AFTER successful registration, THE system SHALL send a mandatory email verification link.
- WHEN a user clicks the verification link, THE system SHALL activate the account for use.
- WHEN login credentials are submitted, THE system SHALL verify credentials within 2 seconds and create, renew, or reject a session accordingly.
- IF authentication fails (invalid credentials), THEN THE system SHALL respond with an error and not disclose whether the email exists.
- THE system SHALL provide password reset functionality via a secure email link.
- WHEN a password reset is requested, THE system SHALL invalidate all current sessions for that user upon successful password change.
- THE system SHALL support user-initiated logout and immediate session revocation.
- THE system SHALL support viewing and revoking all sessions/devices linked to a user account.
- THE system SHALL maintain explicit separation between authenticated and guest users in all flows.
- THE system SHALL issue a JWT access token and refresh token upon successful login or token renewal.

## 2. User Role Structure
- THE system SHALL recognize the following roles, each tied to distinct permissions:

    - **guest**: Non-authenticated visitor. Browses public content but cannot interact.
    - **member**: Registered user. Creates/manages own posts/comments, votes, reports, edits/deletes contributions within limits, manages own settings.
    - **moderator**: Appointed to review/report, manage discussions, remove/ban, enforce guidelines.
    - **admin**: System supervisor. Full business and operational authority.

- A user's role SHALL be asserted via the JWT token for all business logic enforcement.
- WHEN a user's role changes (e.g., member → moderator), THE system SHALL propagate new permissions on next session/token issuance.

## 3. Permission Matrix
| Action                                                                                         | guest | member | moderator | admin |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------|--------|-----------|-------|
| Read public discussion posts and comments                                                      |  ✅   |  ✅    |    ✅     |  ✅  |
| Create a new discussion post                                                                   |  ❌   |  ✅    |    ✅     |  ✅  |
| Edit/delete own post/comment (within business time window)                                    |  ❌   |  ✅    |    ✅     |  ✅  |
| Comment on posts                                                                              |  ❌   |  ✅    |    ✅     |  ✅  |
| Vote on posts/comments                                                                        |  ❌   |  ✅    |    ✅     |  ✅  |
| Report content for abuse/inappropriateness                                                     |  ❌   |  ✅    |    ✅     |  ✅  |
| View, manage own account/profile                                                              |  ❌   |  ✅    |    ✅     |  ✅  |
| Moderate (edit/remove others' content, suspend/ban users, process reports)                    |  ❌   |  ❌    |    ✅     |  ✅  |
| Manage (appoint/dismiss moderators, board settings, audit, analytics, global user control)     |  ❌   |  ❌    |    ❌     |  ✅  |

## 4. Role Responsibilities and Limitations
- **guest**:
    - May read public content but cannot create, vote, comment, or report. Cannot access account features, nor see private or restricted areas.
- **member**:
    - May fully participate (post, comment, vote, report complaints relevant to content). Restricted to managing only their own contributions. Cannot moderate others' content or access moderation/administration settings. Edits/deletes restricted to time-limited window.
- **moderator**:
    - May see and act on reported content, edit/remove any post/comment as appropriate to business rules. May suspend/ban users for violating community rules. May not manage core system settings or appoint additional moderators without admin.
- **admin**:
    - Holds global permissions for all system/business settings. May appoint/dismiss moderators, redefine categories, set policy, access analytics and audit logs, and override any business function as needed.
- THE system SHALL enforce that no user can perform an action outside their defined permissions, irrespective of frontend logic.

## 5. Session/Token Management
- THE system SHALL use JWT (JSON Web Token) for authentication. JWT SHALL be signed with a managed secret and contain at minimum userId, role, permission array, session-token-id, and expiry.
- JWT access tokens:
    - SHALL have a maximum expiry of 30 minutes.
    - Refresh tokens SHALL support up to 30 days of validity and MUST be securely stored.
- THE system SHALL invalidate access/refresh tokens upon password change, authenticated user role upgrade/demotion, or explicit user/log-out from all devices.
- JWT token payloads SHALL NOT include sensitive data (e.g., password, full email in plain text).
- THE system SHALL support rotating secrets for JWT signing and not allow the use of expired tokens for any business logic.
- THE system SHALL perform all permission/role validation server-side based on JWT contents, not on data sent from frontend.

## Error Handling and Security
- IF a user attempts an action outside their permission, THEN THE system SHALL deny with a specific error and reason.
- WHEN a user session expires or the token is malformed, THE system SHALL require re-authentication immediately.
- THE system SHALL throttle and/or temporarily block accounts or IPs with repeated failed logins to prevent brute force.
- THE system SHALL log all authentication, role changes, and failed access attempts for audit and compliance monitoring.

## Performance Requirements
- Authentication and permission validation SHALL complete within 2 seconds under normal load.
- Token issuance, renewal, and revocation SHALL take effect instantly (sub-2 seconds).
- Session information changes (new device login, global logout, password change) SHALL propagate across all user sessions within 30 seconds maximum.

## Visual Authentication Flow (Mermaid Diagram)
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Registration and Verification"
        A["User Submits Registration"] --> B["Validate Email/Password"]
        B -->|"Valid"| C["Create Account (Unverified)"]
        C --> D["Send Verification Email"]
        D --> E["User Clicks Link"]
        E --> F["Activate Account"]
    end

    subgraph "Login Flow"
        G["User Inputs Credentials"] --> H["Validate Credentials"]
        H -->|"Valid"| I["Issue JWT (Access + Refresh)"]
        H -->|"Invalid"| J["Reject with Error"]
    end

    subgraph "Password Reset"
        K["Request Reset"] --> L["Send Reset Email"]
        L --> M["User Clicks Link"]
        M --> N["Update Password, Invalidate Sessions"]
    end

    subgraph "Session/Token Management"
        O["User Log out/Close Device"] --> P["Invalidate Session"]
        Q["User Upgrades Role (e.g., Admin Assign)"] --> R["Issue New Token"]
    end
```

---

This document provides business requirements only. All technical implementation decisions (architecture, APIs, database design, etc.) belong to backend developers. The descriptions above define WHAT the system must do for role-based authentication, access enforcement, and session management under EARS and business rules. All details are implementation-agnostic and allow for developer autonomy.

keyQuestions: What are the key processes and paths users follow?
What states or transitions are important to consider for user experience?
files.content:
## 1. User Onboarding and Registration

### 1.1 Process Overview
- WHEN a guest accesses the polEcoBoard platform, THE system SHALL present registration and sign-in options immediately and access to public content without interaction privileges.
- WHEN a guest selects the registration option, THE system SHALL provide a registration form requiring a unique email address (RFC 5322-compliant and not registered), password (minimum 8 characters, including 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase, 1 digit, 1 symbol), and explicit checkbox confirming consent to terms of use and privacy policy.
- THE system SHALL validate all registration form fields upon submission, presenting inline error messages with specific guidance for each failed rule or format (e.g., "Password must include uppercase letter").
- WHEN all input is valid, THE system SHALL create an inactive member account in "pending verification" state.
- WHEN registration is successful, THE system SHALL immediately send a verification email with a unique time-limited link (valid for 24 hours) to the registered email address. The email SHALL include instructions for verification, a summary of next steps, privacy information, and support contacts.
- WHEN the user clicks the verification link within 24 hours, THE system SHALL activate the account, transition role to "member," and allow login.
- IF the verification link is expired/invalid, THEN THE system SHALL display an informative error and allow for resending a new verification email upon request, up to 3 resend attempts/day.
- WHEN verification is completed, THE system SHALL present an onboarding guide with community values, posting/commenting rules, privacy basics, and introductory tutorial.
- IF a guest attempts registration with an already registered email, THEN THE system SHALL display an error: "Email already registered. Log in or reset password."
- IF a guest submits invalid field values, THE system SHALL block submission until each error is corrected with actionable feedback.
- WHEN verification is not completed within 24 hours, THEN THE system SHALL automatically deactivate the incomplete account and require full re-registration.
- THE system SHALL support future support for federated identity registration (e.g., Google, Facebook) with validated emails, governed by privacy and consent rules outlined for native registration.

### 1.2 State Transitions and Edge Scenarios
- Guest → “Registered (pending verification)” → “Member (active)”
- IF registration is abandoned (incomplete form, closed tab), THEN THE system SHALL not persist any private data except with explicit user consent (e.g., "Save for later").

### 1.3 Access Control
- WHILE in guest state, THE system SHALL prevent access to all posting, commenting, voting, reporting, or account management actions.

### 1.4 Mermaid Diagram: Registration & Onboarding
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["Visitor Arrives"] --> B["Clicks 'Register'"]
  B --> C["Enters Email/Password/Consent"]
  C --> D["Validate Fields"]
  D -->|"Valid"| E["Create Pending Account"]
  D -->|"Invalid"| F["Show Registration Error"]
  E --> G["Send Verification Email"]
  G --> H["User Clicks Verification Link"]
  H --> I{"Link Valid?"}
  I -->|"Yes"| J["Activate Member Account"]
  I -->|"No"| K["Show Error & Resend Option"]
  J --> L["Present Onboarding Guide"]
```

## 2. Login/Logout and Session Flow

### 2.1 Login
- WHEN a member accesses the login screen, THE system SHALL require valid email and password.
- WHEN credentials are submitted, THE system SHALL validate against all activated accounts within 2 seconds and show progress feedback.
- IF credentials are valid, THE system SHALL issue a JWT access token (15-30 minutes) and a refresh token (7-30 days), both containing userId, role, and permission array, and redirect to the last visited or home page.
- IF login fails, THE system SHALL display error "Incorrect credentials" and track failed attempt count. After 3 failures, THE system SHALL prompt password reset; after 5 within 60 minutes, THE system SHALL apply a 15-minute lockout and notify user via email.
- IF account is not verified, THE system SHALL alert "Account not verified" with link to resend verification.

### 2.2 Logout
- WHEN a member, moderator, or admin performs logout, THE system SHALL invalidate all issued access tokens for the session, discard sensitive local state, and redirect to home.
- IF a user attempts protected actions after logout, THE system SHALL redirect to login, storing requested action/route for return after authentication.

### 2.3 Session Management
- WHILE activity occurs, THE system SHALL refresh the session sliding-expiry for up to 30 minutes of inactivity.
- WHEN 30 minutes have passed without interaction, THE system SHALL log out the user and present: "Session expired. Please log in again."
- WHEN a password is changed or account recovery is completed, THE system SHALL invalidate all prior tokens, requiring fresh login.

### 2.4 JWT Security
- THE system SHALL require JWT on every sensitive API or business operation, verify authenticity, and reject all invalid, expired, or malformed tokens with exact error codes.

### 2.5 Access and Privilege Control
- WHEN a guest tries to access member features (post, vote, comment), THE system SHALL redirect to login or registration and, upon successful sign-in, redirect to intended destination.
- WHEN login has failed due to repeated attempts, THE system SHALL provide support contact after lockout.

### 2.6 Mermaid Diagram: Login Flow
```mermaid
graph LR
  A["User Visits Login"] --> B["Enter Email/Password"]
  B --> C["Verify Credentials (2s)"]
  C -->|"Valid"| D["Issue JWT Tokens"]
  C -->|"Invalid"| E{"< 3 Attempts?"}
  E -->|"Yes"| F["Display Error"]
  E -->|"No"| G["Show Password Reset"]
  D --> H["Redirect to Dashboard"]
```

## 3. Post Creation, Editing, and Management

### 3.1 Business Process and Validation
- WHEN a member creates a new post, THE system SHALL require title (5–100 chars), content (20–10,000 chars), category (predefined, visible list), and optional tags (max 5, each 3–30 alphanumeric chars).
- THE system SHALL validate inputs and display specific error per violating field. WHEN all validation passes, THE system SHALL create post as visible and associate with member's account and timestamp.
- WHEN a member edits own post, THE system SHALL allow edit within 24 hours; edits after 24 hours require moderator approval. Every edit SHALL be logged, and posts annotated as "edited" with a linked edit history visible for moderator/admin review.
- WHEN a member deletes own post within 24 hours, THE system SHALL request explicit confirmation and warn deletion is irreversible; after 24 hours, only moderator or admin can delete.
- WHEN moderator or admin edits/deletes any post, THE system SHALL log action to a non-editable moderation record including acting account, reason, date/time, and related post metadata.
- THE system SHALL permit moderators/admins to pin/unpin posts (sticky at top of lists), lock/unlock posts (disallow new replies), and annotate as "official" where appropriate.
- WHEN any user attempts to edit or delete another's post, THE system SHALL reject with error: "You do not have permission to modify this content."
- WHEN bulk deletion or moderation events occur (admin action), THE system SHALL issue notifications to affected users with justification.

### 3.2 Edge and Error Handling
- IF a post submission lacks required fields, THEN THE system SHALL prevent submission and indicate which are missing.
- IF a delete operation is cancelled, THE system SHALL leave post/state unchanged.
- IF a moderator/admin action is overturned (appeals, admin override), THE system SHALL notify all affected users and update audit logs.

### 3.3 Mermaid Diagram: Post Lifecycle
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Member Actions"
    A["Create Post"] --> B["Input Validation"]
    B -->|"Valid"| C["Preview and Submit"]
    B -->|"Invalid"| D["Show Validation Errors"]
    C --> E["Visible Post"]
    E --> F["Edit/Delete ≤24h"]
    F -->|"Edit"| G["Save Edit (+History)"]
    F -->|"Delete"| H["Delete Post (Confirm)"]
  end
  subgraph "Moderator/Admin"
    I["Edit/Delete Any Post"] --> J["Log Action"]
    J --> K["Pin/Lock"]
  end
```

## 4. Discussion Participation (Comment, Vote, Report)

### 4.1 Commenting Workflow
- WHEN a member views a post, THE system SHALL allow commenting if the post is not locked.
- THE system SHALL require comments: 5–1,000 characters, non-blank, and reject prohibited expressions per content policy.
- WHEN submitted, THE system SHALL associate comment to the post, display immediately, and store in user activity log.
- Edits/deletes to comments by commenter are allowed for 1 hour from submission, with each change logged (edit history visible to moderators/admins).
- WHEN a moderator/admin edits/deletes a comment, THE system SHALL record reason, date, acting role, and notify comment author.

### 4.2 Voting
- WHEN a member or moderator views post/comment, THE system SHALL allow a single upvote/downvote per item; vote tally updates instantly and system prevents re-voting ("You have already voted").
- Votes may be retracted/changed within 10 minutes; after which voting on that item is locked for the user.
- IF a guest attempts to vote, THEN THE system SHALL prompt login/registration.
- If abnormal voting detected (multiple votes from same device/IP in short span), THEN THE system SHALL automatically flag for moderation/tally correction.

### 4.3 Reporting Inappropriate Content
- WHEN member/moderator/admin views content, THE system SHALL present "Report" capability. Submission of report requires reason (drop-down: spam, hate, off-topic, abuse, other) and optional text.
- Multiple reports on the same item SHALL aggregate to a single moderation queue item.
- WHEN moderator/admin reviews report, options are: dismiss (close ticket, inform reporter), warn author, edit content, delete content, escalate to admin (with rationale logged).
- Report outcomes are notified to reporter and offending user with template-based business explanation.

### 4.4 Edge & Exception Handling
- IF a member attempts to interact on locked/archived content, THEN THE system SHALL block and display "No further replies/votes allowed."
- IF a user attempts duplicate report on same content, THEN THE system SHALL deny and display report status.
- WHEN a reported item is cleared, reporters are notified with resolution.
- IF moderator abuse or repeated error in report handling is detected, escalate immediately to admin for review.

### 4.5 Mermaid Diagram: Participation & Moderation
```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Participation"
    A["View Post"] --> B["Comment"] --> C["Edit/Delete (1h)"]
    A --> D["Upvote/Downvote"] --> E["Update Tally"]
    D --> F["Lock Vote (per item)"]
    A --> G["Report Content"] --> H["Moderator Review Queue"]
  end
  subgraph "Moderation"
    I["Moderator Review"] --> J{"Action?"}
    J -->|"Dismiss"| K["Close Ticket"]
    J -->|"Warn"| L["Notify User"]
    J -->|"Edit/Delete"| M["Change+Log"]
    J -->|"Escalate"| N["Notify Admin"]
  end
```

## 5. Account Settings, Notification Preferences, and Privacy

### 5.1 Profile and Settings Workflow
- WHEN member accesses "My Account," THE system SHALL permit updating: display name (uniqueness required), password (subject to registration rules), email (must verify new email before changing active address), and customize notification/alert preferences.
- WHEN a member changes notification or privacy preferences (e.g., opt-in/out of email alerts, subscription to announcement categories, show/hide profile fields), THE system SHALL store preferences persistently and apply on next relevant business event.
- WHEN deleting account, THE system SHALL require password re-entry, detailed warning, and per policy may anonymize/delete authored content. Affected posts/comments are annotated accordingly; deletion is irreversible after confirmation, subject to audit policy.

### 5.2 Privacy and Security
- All member profile fields are private by default except display name. Members may choose to make certain info visible; THE system SHALL enforce this preference strictly.
- IF a user attempts profile change with invalid value or blank field, THEN THE system SHALL block operation and display corrective guidance.
- IF account deletion requested while moderation investigations are open, deletion is blocked until completed and approval granted by moderator/admin.

### 5.3 Notification
- WHEN an event triggers a user notification (reply, moderation, report outcome, admin announcement), THE system SHALL deliver in-system notification immediately and—if user has opted-in—via email within 1 minute.
- Notification events SHALL be stored and retrievable for 60 days.

## 6. User Recovery and Password Reset

### 6.1 Forgot Password Flow
- WHEN "Forgot Password" is selected, THE system SHALL require user’s registered email.
- IF email not found, display generic error (“Account not found or not verified” for privacy).
- WHEN valid, send a reset link valid for 1 hour. Link usage requires new password (per registration policy).
- IF link is expired/invalid/used, THEN THE system SHALL show error and offer a "Resend Reset Link" option (up to 3/day).
- WHEN password is changed, all prior sessions and tokens are invalidated, requiring full login.
- All reset attempts are logged and excessive failures (5 attempts/12 hrs) trigger account lockout and support notice.

### 6.2 Account and Session Recovery
- WHEN member cannot access account (lost email, compromised credentials), THE system SHALL provide alternate verification: moderators/admins may supply secondary contact, or members initiate manual verification via support/admin review.
- WHEN alternate verification process is approved, THE system SHALL allow password/email reset and notify user of account status updates.
- IF identity cannot be validated, THE system SHALL lock the account and log event for audit.
- WHEN recovery is complete, user receives status notification.

## 7. Role-Specific Privileges, Transitions, and Edge Cases

### 7.1 Permission Matrix
| Role      | Register | Post | Comment | Vote | Report | Edit/Delete Own | Moderate Others | Manage System |
|-----------|:--------:|:----:|:-------:|:----:|:------:|:---------------:|:---------------:|:-------------:|
| guest     |    ❌     |  ❌  |   ❌    |  ❌  |   ❌   |        ❌        |       ❌        |      ❌       |
| member    |    ✅     |  ✅  |   ✅    |  ✅  |   ✅   |      ✅<sup>1</sup>     |       ❌        |      ❌       |
| moderator |    ✅     |  ✅  |   ✅    |  ✅  |   ✅   |      ✅<sup>1</sup>     |      ✅         |      ❌       |
| admin     |    ✅     |  ✅  |   ✅    |  ✅  |   ✅   |      ✅<sup>1</sup>     |      ✅         |     ✅        |
<sup>1</sup>Within allowed time window.

### 7.2 Transitions and State Definitions
- Guest can only browse public content. WHEN upgraded to member by successful registration/verification, posting, commenting, voting, and reporting are unlocked, and profile images allowed.
- WHEN moderator role is granted (by admin action), moderation dashboard and tools are enabled for the user on next login.
- WHEN admin role is assigned, full system/business controls and board/category configuration are unlocked.
- IF a lesser role is demoted (e.g., moderator → member), THE system SHALL remove role-specific privileges immediately and log event.
- WHEN a member or moderator is banned or suspended (due to violation), THE system SHALL restrict all interactive features and provide notice with reason and restoration criteria.

### 7.3 Success Criteria
- Each user/business action produces deterministic results—identical input yields identical output. Action completion/failure is always acknowledged and specific.
- Validation error responses provide actionable, field-level feedback in plain language.
- All EARS-appropriate requirements use formal templates.
- All mermaid diagrams use correct double-quoted label, bracket/quote syntax, and arrow.
- Edge cases (e.g., attempts to act outside of role, conflicting sessions, ambiguous account state) always result in deterministic, well-documented resolution.

## 8. Reference and Cross-links
- For comprehensive role, authentication, and permission logic, see [User Roles and Authentication Requirements](./03-user-roles-auth.md).
- For detailed error handling, moderation flows, and enforcement, refer to [Business Rules and Moderation Logic](./08-business-rules.md).
- For post, category, and content guidelines see [Functional Requirements Specification](./05-functional-requirements.md).
- For user scenario variants, exception flow, and recovery, reference [User Scenarios and Exception Handling](./07-user-scenarios.md).

---

Business requirements only: All technical implementation (architecture, API, database design) is at the discretion of the development team. Specifications describe WHAT the polEcoBoard system must achieve and enforce, not HOW to implement it.

# Functional Requirements for polEcoBoard

## 1. Discussion Board Structure and Categories

- THE service SHALL provide a structured hierarchy of discussion categories, enabling organized conversation by topic (e.g., Politics, Economics, International Affairs, Local Policy).
- THE system SHALL support category creation, updates, and logical archival by admins only.
- THE system SHALL allow admins to define category visibility (public/private) and description for user guidance.
- THE system SHALL present an up-to-date list of all active categories to all users.
- THE system SHALL ensure that each post is associated with one primary category at creation; editing category assignment is permitted by the post author within a 15-minute window of creation.
- THE system SHALL prevent duplicate category names and enforce a maximum of 50 categories to maintain navigability.
- THE system SHALL make category lists accessible to guests (read-only); only member and higher roles may create content within categories.

## 2. Post Creation, Editing, and Deletion

- WHEN a member initiates creation, THE system SHALL allow the member to submit a post with title (max 120 chars), body (min 10, max 10,000 chars), and optional tags (up to 5 per post).
- IF the post title, body, or tags violate length or prohibited word lists, THEN THE system SHALL reject the post creation and return a specific validation error message.
- WHEN a member submits a post, THE system SHALL store the submission timestamp and user identifier.
- WHILE the submission is in progress, THE system SHALL provide feedback on acceptance or errors within 2 seconds.
- WHEN a member is posting, THE system SHALL check for category selection; IF missing, THEN THE system SHALL block submission and prompt selection.
- WHEN post creation succeeds, THE system SHALL redirect the user to the new post for viewing, voting, and commenting.
- WHEN a member attempts to edit a post within 15 minutes of submission, THE system SHALL allow full editing by the post author. AFTER 15 minutes, editing is locked unless the member requests moderator intervention for corrections (typos, factual errors).
- WHEN a moderator reviews an edit request, THE system SHALL provide the original and edit proposal for comparison. Upon approval, the post SHALL be updated and marked as "moderator-edited" with audit trail.
- WHEN a member requests deletion, THE system SHALL allow deletion only within 15 minutes of submission if there are no comments. IF a post has received comments or votes, THEN THE system SHALL deny self-deletion and require moderator review.
- WHEN a moderator or admin deletes a post, THE system SHALL flag it for archival (soft delete) and retain data for 90 days, rendering it hidden from all users except admins for compliance/audit review.

## 3. Commenting and Replies

- WHEN a member views a post, THE system SHALL provide an interface to comment (250 chars max per comment) or reply to existing comments, supporting a single nesting level (reply to comment, not nested threads).
- WHEN a guest attempts to comment or reply, THEN THE system SHALL prompt for login/registration.
- WHEN a member submits a comment, THE system SHALL check prohibited language and enforce uniqueness (no duplicate comments on same post from same user within 5 minutes).
- WHEN a comment is successfully posted, THE system SHALL show it immediately beneath the relevant post or comment in reverse chronological order.
- WHEN a member deletes their own comment, THE system SHALL allow deletion within 10 minutes unless the comment has replies. Moderators can delete any comment with audit logging.
- IF comment content violates rules (prohibited words, personal attacks, spam), THEN THE system SHALL reject submission and display a contextual error.

## 4. Voting Mechanism

- WHEN viewing posts or comments, THE system SHALL display upvote/downvote icons and cumulative vote count to all authenticated users.
- WHERE user role is member or higher, THE system SHALL permit voting for each post or comment once per user.
- IF a user attempts a second vote on the same post or comment, THEN THE system SHALL display an error and prevent duplicate voting.
- WHEN a member votes, THE system SHALL register the vote and update the visible vote tally in real time (within 1 second of action).
- IF a guest or unauthenticated user attempts to vote, THEN THE system SHALL prompt for login/registration before accepting input.
- WHERE a moderator or admin detects evidence of vote manipulation (multiple accounts, automated voting), THE system SHALL allow these roles to invalidate suspicious votes and annotate the affected records with investigation notes.

## 5. Reporting Inappropriate Content

- WHERE user role is member or higher, THE system SHALL provide a report option for all posts and comments, allowing users to specify a report reason (spam, hate speech, off-topic, other) with optional details (max 250 chars).
- WHEN a report is submitted, THE system SHALL immediately flag the reported content and submit it for moderator review.
- THE system SHALL limit users to a maximum of 3 active reports per day to prevent abuse of the reporting function.
- IF a user attempts to report the same content more than once, THEN THE system SHALL refuse the action and show an explanatory message.
- THE system SHALL display the current report status (pending, reviewed, action taken) to moderators and restrict this audit trail from regular users.

## 6. Moderation Workflow

- WHEN new content (posts/comments) is reported or flagged, THE system SHALL add it to a dedicated review queue accessible only to moderators and admins.
- THE system SHALL display report details, content history, and prior moderation actions to facilitate informed decisions.
- WHEN a moderator reviews content, THE system SHALL provide options to dismiss (no action), edit (with justification), delete (with reason), or escalate to admin for severe cases (legal, safety issues).
- WHEN a moderation action is taken, THE system SHALL log the decision, timestamp, acting moderator, and resolution (visible to admins and the acting moderator).
- THE system SHALL notify reporting users of the outcome when moderation is complete (action taken or dismissed).
- THE system SHALL enforce automated escalation to admin for any user receiving more than 5 moderation actions within 1 month.
- THE system SHALL allow moderators to suspend (temporary) or ban (permanent) users subject to admin review and audit logging.
- THE system SHALL prohibit moderators from acting on their own posts; actions must be routed to another moderator or admin.

## 7. Notifications

- WHEN a member receives a reply, moderation action, or status change on their post/report, THE system SHALL deliver a notification via in-system message and optional email (users may opt out).
- THE system SHALL allow users to configure notification preferences for types of events (reply, vote, moderation, admin announcements).
- WHEN a notification is triggered, THE system SHALL deliver it within 2 seconds of the initiating event for in-system messages, and within 1 minute for email delivery.
- THE system SHALL provide a persistent notification history (last 60 days) accessible to users by type and date.
- THE system SHALL not send notification emails to guests.

## 8. Business Rules, Validation, and Performance

### Content and Participation Constraints

- THE system SHALL prevent the posting of prohibited words or phrases (configurable by admins) in all user inputs.
- THE system SHALL limit the number of open posts per member to 50 at any time; excess attempts SHALL be rejected with a precise explanation.
- THE system SHALL require that all moderation actions, votes, and reports are recorded with the acting user's identifier, IP address, and timestamp.
- THE system SHALL maintain full audit logs for all privilege actions (moderator/admin) for compliance review.
- THE system SHALL support an average response time for all user-facing actions of less than 2 seconds under normal load (within 1000 concurrent users).
- THE system SHALL provide meaningful error messages for all validation and permission failures, guiding the user on corrective action.

### Mermaid Diagram – Post to Moderation Workflow

```mermaid
graph LR
  subgraph "Member Actions"
    A["Create Post"] --> B["Vote/Comment"]
    B --> C["Report Content"]
  end

  subgraph "Moderation Queue"
    D["Review Reported Content"] --> E{"Action Required?"}
    E -->|"Yes"| F["Edit/Delete/Escalate"]
    E -->|"No"| G["Dismiss Report"]
  end

  subgraph "Admin Oversight"
    F --> H["Audit & Log"]
    F --> I["User Suspension/Ban"]
  end

  C --> D
  F --> H
```

---

All requirements above are written in EARS format where applicable. All non-functional constraints and flows are described from business perspective only. User interactions, business logic, and role-based transitions are fully detailed for backend implementation in accordance with the polEcoBoard product scope.

# Non-Functional Requirements for polEcoBoard

## 1. Introduction and Scope
polEcoBoard is an online platform designed to facilitate open, safe, and respectful discussions around political and economic topics. Given the nature of its subject matter and diversity of its user roles (guest, member, moderator, admin), the system's non-functional requirements are critical to ensure performance, security, scalability, privacy, and legal compliance. This document describes, in business requirements language, all non-functional standards for backend planning and implementation.

## 2. Performance Expectations

### Service Performance SLAs
- WHEN a user requests any main content feed or discussion board view, THE polEcoBoard system SHALL deliver the first page of results within 1 second under normal usage conditions (up to 80% of average concurrent users).
- WHEN a user executes a search query, THE system SHALL return results within 2 seconds for typical queries (up to 100 keywords or filters).
- WHILE under traffic levels within engineered design limits, THE system SHALL serve 99% of API responses within 2 seconds.
- WHERE votes or comments are submitted, THE system SHALL write and acknowledge the action within 1 second.
- WHEN uploading text posts or comments, THE system SHALL ensure no input is lost and provide immediate confirmation.
- IF the backend is under maintenance, THEN THE system SHALL present planned downtime notices at least 24 hours in advance for scheduled events.
- IF any endpoint is unavailable for more than 5 seconds, THEN THE system SHALL trigger an incident response notification to admins.

### Page and Action Responsiveness
- THE system SHALL maintain a maximum end-to-end latency (user to backend to user) of 2 seconds for all standard user actions (browsing, posting, voting, reporting) during non-degraded operations.

### Data Processing and Throughput
- THE backend SHALL support ingestion of up to 100 new posts per minute and 500 new comments per minute without affecting response time SLAs.
- THE system SHALL process voting and reporting actions in real-time with an acknowledgement delay less than 500 ms.

## 3. Scalability Requirements

### Horizontal Scale Targets
- WHILE user activity grows, THE system SHALL allow addition of backend nodes without user-facing downtime.
- WHERE user registration increases to 10x monthly baseline, THE system SHALL handle this increase with no degradation in the above performance metrics.
- THE system SHALL support up to 1 million registered members and up to 10,000 concurrent active users with sustained performance per section 2.

### Resource Elasticity and Load Management
- THE system SHALL implement autoscaling processes to maintain performance under sudden traffic spikes (e.g., breaking news triggering surge discussions).
- WHEN traffic exceeds capacity by more than 10%, THE system SHALL degrade gracefully by queueing non-critical actions and prioritizing feed/read over writes (posts/comments/votes).
- IF backend resources reach 90% utilization, THEN THE system SHALL alert infrastructure operators and initiate scaling workflows.

### Data Growth and Retention
- THE system SHALL retain performance regardless of database growth to at least 10 million posts and 100 million comments.
- WHERE content archiving is implemented, THE system SHALL keep archived data instantly retrievable by authorized roles (moderator, admin) within 5 seconds.

## 4. Availability and Reliability

### Uptime Commitments
- THE system SHALL maintain 99.95% uptime measured monthly, excluding scheduled maintenance declared 24h in advance.

### Redundancy and Disaster Recovery
- THE backend SHALL implement redundancy for all critical components so that failures in any single node do not affect user experience.
- WHEN a component failure occurs, THE system SHALL automatically redirect traffic to healthy nodes with failover occurring in less than 10 seconds.
- THE system SHALL recover from disaster scenarios (e.g., data center outage) with <1 hour maximum data loss and <2 hour total restoration time.
- THE system SHALL regularly back up all user data, configuration, and audit logs at intervals not exceeding 24 hours.

### Monitoring and Incident Handling
- THE backend SHALL provide real-time health monitoring and trigger incidents to admin dashboards and on-call personnel via designated channels.
- WHEN anomalies or SLA breaches are detected, THE system SHALL log the event and escalate to admins within 1 minute.

#### Mermaid Diagram: High-Level Availability and Incident Flow
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Normal Operation"
      A["User Action"] --> B["Backend Processes Request"]
      B --> C["Success: Response to User"]
    end
    subgraph "Failure Handling"
      B --> D{"Is Failure Detected?"}
      D -->|"Yes"| E["Trigger Incident Workflow"]
      E --> F["Notify Admins"]
      F --> G["Auto-Failover if Critical"]
      G --> B
      D -->|"No"| C
    end
```

## 5. Usability Guidelines (Backend/Process Perspective)

### Backend Process Usability
- THE system SHALL provide clear, meaningful, and localized error messages for all failed business actions (not technical traces).
- WHEN a user's post/comment is rejected due to validation or moderation, THE system SHALL explain with actionable business reasons (e.g., "Exceeded character limit.", "Topic closed for new replies.").
- THE backend SHALL support audit logging of critical user actions (post, comment, vote, report, moderation action), write-once immutable for compliance review.
- IF multiple backend actions are pending (e.g., batch moderation), THEN THE system SHALL process and acknowledge each success/failure distinctly in user-facing business terms.

## 6. Data Privacy and Security Requirements

### Role-Based Data Access
- WHERE guest role is in use, THE system SHALL restrict access to public data only; guests SHALL not view any member PII or non-public boards.
- WHERE member role is authenticated, THE system SHALL ensure access to member's own account data, public content, and data of other users EXCEPT for confidential moderation/admin fields.
- WHERE moderator/admin roles operate, THE system SHALL provide access scoped to business need, with admin viewing additional audit/configuration data.
- THE system SHALL redact all user PII when shown to roles not authorized to see it.

### Personal Data Handling and Retention
- THE system SHALL store all account and activity data encrypted at rest and in transit.
- WHERE user requests deletion or account removal, THE system SHALL purge all personal information within 30 days and confirm deletion to the user.
- WHERE account deletion is mandated by law (e.g., GDPR, CCPA), THE system SHALL provide audit logs confirming completion.
- THE system SHALL only retain logs and data for business-justified retention periods and destroy expired data.

### Sensitive Data Protection
- THE system SHALL hash and salt all passwords using industry best practices.
- THE system SHALL never store or log raw passwords, authentication secrets, or security tokens.
- ALL API or external service integrations SHALL use secure channels (HTTPS/TLS) and require authentication.

### Data Breach Detection and Response
- WHEN a suspected data breach is detected, THE system SHALL trigger breach response procedures and notify admins within 30 minutes.
- THE system SHALL preserve forensic data and incident logs for investigation.
- WHERE required by law, THE system SHALL notify affected users and authorities within mandatory time limits.

## 7. Compliance (Legal and Policy)

### Regulatory Coverage
- WHERE the service operates in regulatory jurisdictions (e.g., EU, US, KR), THE system SHALL comply with all local data protection regulations (GDPR, CCPA, PIPA).
- THE backend SHALL implement age-gating and consent mechanisms aligned with relevant laws for minors and sensitive data.
- THE system SHALL provide data subject access request (DSAR) features for all users, allowing them to download/account/delete personal data.

### Content and Moderation Compliance
- WHERE content takedown is required by law or court order, THE system SHALL remove such content within 24 hours and log the action for audit.
- THE backend SHALL enforce retention/deletion policies for all user-generated content per applicable law and board policy.
- WHERE abusive/illegal content is detected, THE system SHALL mark and restrict visibility pending moderation, store audit trails for a minimum of 2 years, and cooperate with authorities when legally binding requests are received.

## 8. Non-Functional Requirement Summary Table

| Category         | Requirement                                                      | SLA/Metric                       |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Performance      | API response time                                                | 99% ≤ 2s (normal), ≤ 1s first load|
| Scalability      | Concurrent users supported                                       | Up to 10,000                     |
| Availability     | Uptime                                                           | 99.95% monthly                   |
| Usability        | Clear business error messages                                    | All failed actions                |
| Privacy          | Personal data deletion turnaround                                | ≤ 30 days from request           |
| Security         | Encrypted storage and transit                                    | Mandatory                        |
| Compliance       | Legal removals + notification                                    | ≤ 24h for takedown               |
| Backup/Recovery  | Data backup + disaster recovery                                  | 24h backup; <2h restore          |

## 9. Mermaid Diagram: Data Breach Detection and Compliance
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Security Event Flow"
      X["Detect Breach or Anomaly"] --> Y["Trigger Incident Response"]
      Y --> Z["Notify Admins (Within 30 mins)"]
      Z --> AA["Preserve Forensic Data"]
      AA --> AB{"Legal Notice Required?"}
      AB -->|"Yes"| AC["Notify Users + Authorities"]
      AB -->|"No"| AD["Complete Internal Incident Log"]
    end
```

## 10. Closing Notes on Non-Functional Readiness
The above business requirements define the minimum acceptable service levels, security commitments, user privacy standards, and compliance obligations for polEcoBoard. These non-functional provisions are essential for trustworthy multi-role operation, sensitive content handling, and robust jurisdictional compliance. Backend developers must use these requirements as authoritative constraints for all design and operational decisions.
