files.content:
# User Scenario Requirements Analysis Report for polEcoBoard

## Introduction
Political and economic discussions on the polEcoBoard platform require clear, testable, and role-based requirements for system behavior. All scenarios—regular, alternate, edge, and exception—are exhaustively modeled for every user role (guest, member, moderator, admin) using EARS-compliant syntax and explicit business language. Expectations for authentication, session management, error recovery, permission enforcement, audit trails, and performance are described so that backend developers can implement every business need directly from this scenario analysis.

## Primary Use Scenarios

### 1. Board, Category, and Post Viewing
- WHEN a guest accesses the board homepage, THE system SHALL instantly display an up-to-date list of public categories and the 20 most recent posts ordered by latest activity.
- WHERE a member is authenticated, THE system SHALL additionally highlight threads the member has posted in or is following within all visible categories.
- WHERE any user (guest or member) selects a board category, THE system SHALL present all active posts in that category ranked by most recent reply within 1 second.
- WHEN a user views a post, THE system SHALL present the full post content, metadata (author, timestamp, votes, view count), and all visible first-level comments ordered newest-first; loading MUST complete within 1 second for 95% of requests.
- IF a post or category has been restricted or archived, THEN THE system SHALL display a clear status explaining visibility limitation.

### 2. Post Creation and Drafting (Member)
- WHEN a member selects "New Post", THE system SHALL present all available categories, required post fields (title, content), and optional tag fields (max 5 tags, unique, 3-30 chars each).
- WHEN post title is entered, THE system SHALL validate length (10–100 chars), allow only permitted characters, and block prohibited terms.
- WHEN submission is attempted, THE system SHALL verify that all required fields are present and within business validation constraints; missing/invalid entries SHALL be immediately identified and the user notified with corrective guidance.
- WHEN validation passes, THE system SHALL create the post, associate it to the member, log creation with timestamp, and display confirmation plus a view of the new post.
- WHILE a post is in draft, THE system SHALL allow editing/discarding by the author; drafts are autosaved every 30 seconds and persist for 7 days unless published or deleted.
- IF a member is muted, suspended, or banned, THEN THE system SHALL block post submission and display specific restriction and duration with escalation link to request admin/mod review.
- WHEN a post is created, THE system SHALL update board/category lists in real time and, where moderation is required, notify appropriate moderators within 3 seconds.

### 3. Commenting and Replies (Member)
- WHEN a member views an active post, THE system SHALL show the comment form with input length restrictions (5–1,000 chars; no prohibited language; 1,000 unicode chars max).
- WHEN submitting a comment, THE system SHALL validate user status, content, duplication (no same user duplicate comments on same post within 10 minutes), and input restrictions.
- IF validation fails, THEN THE system SHALL reject and present a highlighted explanation of every business rule violated.
- WHEN successful, THE system SHALL store the comment, link it to post/member, increment comment count, and notify post author if notification preferences permit.
- WHERE a comment was made by a member, edit/delete are allowed for 15 minutes post-submission, tracked with full audit log; edits after 15 minutes (or to comments with replies) REQUIRE moderator review and explicit justification.

### 4. Voting Interactions
- WHEN a member views posts or comments, THE system SHALL display voting icons; IF the user is the author, voting icon is disabled.
- WHEN a vote is initiated, THE system SHALL validate that the user has not previously voted and is eligible (not suspended/banned, within daily quota of votes).
- WHEN accepted, THE system SHALL record the vote, update the tally instantly, and prevent further voting by this user on the same item within 24 hours.
- IF duplicate voting or voting on own content is attempted, THEN THE system SHALL reject with an explanatory error and log occurrence.
- IF all voting quotas are exhausted for the day (default: 200 per member), THEN THE system SHALL block further votes and prompt user.

### 5. Reporting Inappropriate Content
- WHEN a member clicks "Report" on a post/comment, THE system SHALL provide a required reason dropdown (configured by admin), and allow up to 400 characters of free-text description.
- WHEN report is submitted, THE system SHALL validate the submission (reason present, description valid), store the report, notify the moderator team immediately, and prevent further reports of the same item by the submitting member.
- IF content is already under review or actioned, THEN THE system SHALL inform reporting user of current case status.
- IF a member uses the report function excessively (more than 10 in 24 hours or repeated invalid reports), THEN THE system SHALL suspend reporting rights and notify moderators with an audit trigger.

### 6. Moderation Workflow (Moderator)
- WHEN a moderator logs in, THE system SHALL show a dashboard with pending reports, flagged content, recent moderation actions, and assigned categories.
- WHEN reviewing, THE system SHALL present content summary, aggregated report reasons, user history, prior decisions, available actions (dismiss, edit, remove, warn, suspend, escalate).
- WHEN an action is taken, THE system SHALL enforce business/process permissions, log the rationale, update content/audit records, and notify the affected user (member or moderator).
- IF the action is outside moderator authority (e.g., permanent bans, core settings), THEN THE system SHALL block and optionally alert admin.
- WHERE a moderator is uncertain or polarity of decisions is high, escalation to admin SHALL be available with summarized case package.
- WHERE a moderator attempts to alter own prior actions, dual review/approval by another moderator is required.

### 7. Administrative Management (Admin)
- WHEN an admin accesses the admin panel, THE system SHALL allow review/configuration of: user accounts; board/category structures; moderation policy/rules; analytical and audit logs; and moderator assignments.
- WHEN appointing/removing moderators, THE system SHALL require dual confirmation, log event, and notify both the promoted/demoted user and current moderators.
- WHEN reviewing escalated/moderation cases, THE system SHALL provide override authority and require specific justification for all critical/irreversible actions.
- WHEN changing policy/roles/category structures, THE system SHALL log before/after, require action description, and alert all potentially affected users/roles.

## Alternative and Edge Case Flows

### 1. Validation, Limits, and Permissions
- IF any post or comment includes prohibited language, exceeds min/max length, lacks required fields, or breaches uniqueness, THEN THE system SHALL reject input, explicitly indicate rules breached, and allow user to correct and resubmit instantly.
- IF a user’s session token, JWT, or authentication is missing, expired, or tampered, THEN THE system SHALL prompt for login, preserve in-progress data for up to 10 minutes, and advise the user how to recover unfinished work.
- IF draft is corrupted/lost during save, THEN THE system SHALL prompt user to re-edit or recover from the last autosave copy.

### 2. Role Transitions, Restrictions, and Escalations
- IF a member is suspended, THEN THE system SHALL immediately restrict posting, commenting, voting, reporting, and provide banner alerts explaining status, reason, and duration; links to appeal SHALL be prominently displayed.
- IF moderator error occurs (e.g., action taken without required evidence, outside role, or with insufficient review), THEN THE system SHALL require admin confirmation before action takes effect and send alerts to operational admins.
- IF a moderator attempts to alter user roles or board configurations, THEN THE system SHALL deny and log all attempts and trigger admin notification if repeated.
- IF role transitions occur due to system integration, ban appeal, or admin override, prior and new permissions SHALL take effect on next issued session/JWT, and session log SHALL record the event.

### 3. Voting/Reporting Edge Cases
- IF a member attempts to vote after the target content has been archived, deleted, or locked, THEN THE system SHALL reject the action and display a historical state notice.
- IF a member attempts to exceed allowed upvote/downvote counts per day (default 200), THEN THE system SHALL block and clearly explain the quota policy.
- IF a user reports the same content multiple times, or the maximum report quota is reached, THEN THE system SHALL restrict new reports, provide feedback on quota status, and surface outstanding open cases in user dashboard.

### 4. Moderator/Admin Escalation & Emergency Action
- IF a moderator faces repeated, ambiguous, or high-impact moderation (e.g., multiple escalations, suspected coordinated abuse), THEN THE system SHALL facilitate escalation workflows, package cases with evidence for admin review, and require at least two admin confirmations for irreversible or highly impactful actions (e.g., permanent bans, mass deletions).
- IF multiple moderator abuses or extraordinary admin actions are detected within a short interval (system default: 1 hour), THEN THE system SHALL trigger internal audit alerts, temporarily suspend automated processing, and require system audit log review and formal completion of review before resuming normal moderator/admin system operations.

### 5. Automated Safeguards for System Integrity
- WHEN error rates spike or backend slowdowns impact user actions beyond performance thresholds, THE system SHALL display status banners, initiate auto-retry for failed submissions, save in-progress data, and redirect users to a status/help page if necessary.

## Error and Recovery Paths

### 1. Authentication Errors
- IF a guest/member attempts to access or perform actions not permitted by their role, THEN THE system SHALL deny access, present a business-friendly error message, and provide the authorized path for next steps (e.g., "Please log in" or "Admin access required").
- IF JWT/session token is invalid, expired, or suspicious, THEN THE system SHALL require immediate re-authentication and record an audit log event with user and IP.
- IF account/password reset is initiated but the token is outdated or compromised, THEN THE system SHALL deny access, prompt secure account recovery, and invalidate associated tokens.

### 2. Submission and Network Failures
- IF post/comment/report/moderation submission fails due to server/network errors, THEN THE system SHALL save unsent data locally (where allowed), inform the user of failure, and provide options to retry or discard.
- IF confirmation of critical actions (deletion, ban, configuration change) does not reach user within 3 seconds, THE system SHALL auto-retry twice and inform the user of pending status with warnings against repeat submissions.
- IF submission is irrecoverable, THE system SHALL surface error codes and contact/help options, and ensure in-progress data is preserved for at least 10 minutes for user retrieval/retry.

### 3. Data Consistency and Integrity
- IF any action attempts to reference stale/deleted/changed resources (e.g., already deleted post, moved/invalid board/category), THEN THE system SHALL provide user with a detailed error and a link to board/category home.
- WHEN backend detects content inconsistencies, THE system SHALL display a global alert for users in affected flows, restrict further input, and trigger admin system diagnostics and incident reporting.

### 4. System-wide Exception Paths
- IF multiple errors/uncaught exceptions occur rapidly for a single user or session (threshold: 3 or more in 60 seconds), THEN THE system SHALL lock input, display a "Service temporarily limited" warning, and activate internal error logging and rollback/retry protocols.
- IF scheduled maintenance is ongoing, or an internal service is degraded, THEN THE system SHALL display banners, block affected business features/business logic rolls as required, and log configuration for compliance traceability.

## Role-Based Experiences and Permissions

### Guest
- CAN view all public boards/categories/posts
- IF attempting to post, comment, vote, or report, THEN THE system SHALL prompt for registration/login, block action, and highlight member benefits.
- CAN register as a member; registration flows override viewing if initiated.

### Member
- CAN create, edit (with limits), and delete (with limits) own posts/comments; cannot modify others' content.
- CAN vote, comment, report, as per quota and business validation.
- CANNOT perform moderation, view sensitive moderation/audit data, or access admin functions.

### Moderator
- Inherits all member rights plus: CAN access dashboard for pending reports/flagged content; CAN take moderation action in authorized categories; CAN warn, suspend, remove offending content, view and add to audit logs; CANNOT change admin configurations, appoint others, or bypass dual approvals for key actions.

### Admin
- All system privileges: CAN manage users, roles, boards, moderation policy, global bans/suspensions, analytics/audits; CAN override all moderation actions, but irreversible actions REQUIRE dual confirmation and reason.

| Role      | View | Post | Comment | Vote | Report | Moderate | Admin Ops |
|-----------|------|------|---------|------|--------|----------|-----------|
| Guest     | ✅   | ❌   | ❌      | ❌   | ❌     | ❌       | ❌        |
| Member    | ✅   | ✅   | ✅      | ✅   | ✅     | ❌       | ❌        |
| Moderator | ✅   | ✅   | ✅      | ✅   | ✅     | ✅       | ❌        |
| Admin     | ✅   | ✅   | ✅      | ✅   | ✅     | ✅       | ✅        |

## Response Time and Performance Requirements
- THE system SHALL serve homepage, board, and post view screens within 1 second 95% of the time; all post/comment/report submissions SHALL respond in under 2 seconds under normal load.
- IF any confirmation does not reach user within 2 seconds for regular actions or 3 seconds for admin/mod actions, THEN THE system SHALL display a temporary status warning and auto-retry.
- Critical moderation/admin changes SHALL propagate system-wide (authorization, permissions, session invalidation) within 30 seconds.

## Scenario Flow Diagram

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Posting and Moderation Flow"
        A["Create Post"] --> B["Validate Post Input"]
        B -->|"Valid"| C["Save Post"]
        C --> D["Update Board & Notify Moderators"]
        B -->|"Invalid"| E["Show Error & Allow Edit"]
        D --> F["Moderator Review"]
        F -->|"Approve"| G["Post Visible to All"]
        F -->|"Edit/Remove"| H["Notify Author, Log Action"]
        F -->|"Escalate"| I["Admin Escalation"]
    end
```

## Success Criteria
- THE system SHALL fulfill all above scenarios and requirements in business terms, handle normal, alternative, edge, and error cases as specified, and provide complete audit trails/logging for each permissioned/sensitive action, ensuring testability and implementation-readiness for backend.

## End of Document

How are moderation actions governed and enforced?
files.content:
# Business Rules and Validation Requirements for polEcoBoard

## 1. Content Validation Rules (Post/Comment Limits, Language)

### General Validation
- WHEN a user submits a post or comment, THE system SHALL require non-empty content (after trimming whitespace).
- THE system SHALL enforce a maximum content length of 5,000 characters per post and 1,000 characters per comment; IF these limits are exceeded, THEN THE system SHALL reject the submission and display a precise error message indicating the offending field and allowed maximum.
- THE system SHALL only allow content in supported languages: English (default; additional locales may be approved by admin). IF an unsupported language is detected, THEN THE system SHALL reject and inform the user of supported options.
- IF submitted content (post or comment) is blank or contains only whitespace, THEN THE system SHALL reject submission with a specific error code and message.
- WHEN a post or comment is received, THE system SHALL sanitize the content to remove prohibited HTML, scripts, and unsupported markup, and SHALL escape any potentially unsafe characters.
- WHEN a user includes code snippets in their post or comment, THE system SHALL allow only supported syntax-highlighting tags in pre-defined safe formats; all other embedded code SHALL be rejected or neutralized.

### Attachment Rules
- WHEN a user adds attachments to a post, THE system SHALL verify that only permitted file types (jpeg, png, gif, pdf, docx) are included and SHALL limit the total number of attachments to 3 per post, with a strict maximum file size of 10MB per file and a total of 20MB per post.
- IF an unsupported file type is uploaded or a file is oversized, THEN THE system SHALL reject the attached file(s) and inform the user about the violation in clear business language.
- WHEN an attachment is rejected, THE system SHALL provide a specific reason, supporting affected users with actionable guidance for correction.
- WHEN a post is deleted, THE system SHALL schedule all associated attachments for deletion according to content retention rules.

### Prohibited Content and Expression
- IF a post or comment contains hate speech, personal attacks, explicit or veiled threats, discriminatory/inflammatory language, doxing, advertising/spam, or references to off-platform illegal activity, THEN THE system SHALL block content submission, provide a direct message specifying policy breach, and log the violation for moderator review.
- WHEN a user attempts to submit content flagged as prohibited, THE system SHALL capture an audit event (timestamp, user ID, partial content or hash as privacy allows).
- WHERE a pattern of policy-violating attempts (3 or more in 24 hours) is detected, THE system SHALL escalate for automated or manual review and apply progressive sanctions.

### Language Moderation and User Protection
- THE system SHALL maintain a living blacklist of prohibited words/phrases (including but not limited to profanity, slurs, and targeted abuse), updatable by moderators and admins.
- IF a user submits content matching blacklist terms, THEN THE system SHALL reject the submission with an immediate explanation specifying the category of violation (without echoing term itself).
- WHERE repeated rejections for blacklist violations exceed three occurrences in a rolling 24-hour window, THE system SHALL impose an automated posting cooldown (30 minutes) and notify the user of the sanction, including appeal instructions.
- WHEN automated filters catch borderline or context-dependent content (e.g., potentially harassing but ambiguous phrasing), THE system SHALL flag the item for moderation review and limit public visibility until resolved.

### Validation Error Handling
- WHEN a submission fails validation (length, blank, prohibited terms, file type/size), THE system SHALL return a detailed error message with corrective instructions, maintain the unsaved user entry (so user does not lose work), and allow retry after correction.
- IF validation fails repeatedly for the same cause (e.g., reusing excess length), THEN THE system SHALL provide progressively clearer, more actionable feedback and, after 5 failed attempts, recommend resource links or community guidelines.

## 2. Participation Rules

### Role-based Content Contribution
- WHERE user has the guest role, THE system SHALL strictly prohibit creation, editing, or deletion of posts/comments and display a prompt to register/login.
- WHERE user has the member role, THE system SHALL permit posts, comments, and votes on eligible boards/categories. WHEN a member creates content, THE system SHALL attribute authorship and timestamp, and enforce all content rules at submission.
- WHEN a member edits or deletes own posts/comments, THE system SHALL allow this for up to 30 minutes after submission or until the first reply, vote, or report (whichever comes first). IF this period has expired or content has received interaction, THEN THE system SHALL block further edits/deletions and notify the member, suggesting escalation to moderators if legitimate corrections are needed.
- WHERE moderator or admin role is present, THE system SHALL allow editing/deletion of any content as per moderation workflow, with mandatory audit logging and notification to the original author.
- WHEN editing occurs, THE system SHALL create and securely store an edit history, available to admins for audit trail purposes.

### Voting Rules
- WHERE user is a member, moderator, or admin, THE system SHALL allow one upvote or downvote per post or comment per user. IF duplicate voting is attempted, THEN THE system SHALL reject and inform the user why.
- Members and above SHALL not be able to vote on their own content. IF attempted, THEN THE system SHALL reject with a clear error.
- Members can retract or change their vote within 10 minutes of casting the initial vote; after this, votes are locked. Changing votes is audit-logged for moderators.
- Voting results (counts, ratios) are visible to all users, but voting identities are confidential except to admins for audit or abuse tracing.

### Reporting and Appeal
- WHERE user is a member or higher, THE system SHALL enable reporting of any post or comment for abuse, with mandatory functional reason (dropdown from report types: spam, hate speech, off-topic, privacy, other) and optional, bounded free-text field (max 500 chars).
- WHEN a report is submitted, THE system SHALL generate a unique case, maintain reporter anonymity (except to admins), and set initial status to pending review.
- Guests attempting to report are blocked and instructed to register or login.
- A user may only report a given content item once; duplicate or frivolous reporting attempts are rejected.
- IF a user files excessive invalid reports (more than 5 rejected complaints within 7 days), THEN THE system SHALL flag for possible sanction (report function suspension), reviewed by moderators.

### Participation Limitations and Sanctions
- WHEN repeated content policy or reporting abuse occurs (by member), THE system SHALL escalate consequences: warning, posting privilege temporary suspension (1–14 days), and if severe, permanent account or IP ban (subject to admin review).
- Account bans must be defensible with audit trail and are subject to appeal as a core user right.
- WHEN appealed, THE system SHALL record all actions, communications, and case material for compliance, transparency, and reporting to the user.
- IF a sanctioned user attempts to circumvent measures (e.g., new account, proxy use), THEN THE system SHALL implement and log adaptive response mechanisms (IP/device matching, further sanctions, admin notification).

## 3. Moderation and Escalation Rules

### Moderator Responsibilities
- WHERE user has moderator role, THE system SHALL grant powers to view reported/flagged content and all associated prior moderation events within assigned categories.
- WHEN content is reported, flagged, or shows automated risk triggers, THE system SHALL move it to a review queue, visible to all eligible moderators (with timestamp, content snapshot, report details, and contributor/user audit info).
- WHEN a moderator takes action (edit, removal, warning, escalation, close as NFA), THE system SHALL prompt for mandatory contextual reason and store the action, associated metadata, and time in an immutable audit log.
- Content review by moderators must occur within 12 hours of staging or sooner if business or compliance rules require; breach of SLA triggers a system escalation to admins.
- Moderators can restrict participation, lock threads, hide posts from public view, or anonymize content as needed.
- Complex/escalated violations (severe threats, legal issues, coordinated abuse, policy gray area) SHALL be referred to admin with all evidence and recommended disposition attached.

### Admin Authority and Escalation
- WHERE user has admin role, THE system SHALL grant unrestricted control over moderation review, action, audit access, and all appeal/case logs.
- Admin can override moderator decisions, but all override events are logged with rationale and must be visible to oversight functions.
- WHEN a user (or associated account/IP) accumulates 5 or more valid reports or 3+ moderator actions within 30 days, THE system SHALL automatically flag account for admin review, generate a risk assessment case, and restrict certain privileges pending review.
- IP/Device-based circumvention attempts (linked to sanctioned user) are detected, correlated, and escalated to admin for advanced action.

### Enforcement Actions
- WHERE content is found in violation, THE system SHALL permit removal, edit, hiding, locking, or anonymization as contextually appropriate. Severity, context, and user history determine which actions are available and require manual justification.
- Multiple levels of sanction are supported: warning, timed suspension (from 1 to 30 days), permanent ban. Members must be notified with reasons, duration, and appeal instructions.
- WHEN law or public safety is involved (e.g., imminent threat, evidence preservation), THE system SHALL flag and restrict content, notify admin immediately, and trigger a legal hold on account and associated material.

### Auditability and Tracking
- ALL moderator and admin actions affecting member participation/content SHALL be time-stamped, attributed to acting staff, and visible in an audit trail accessible to authorized roles only.
- THE system SHALL maintain and display a compliance dashboard for moderators and admins showing time-to-resolution, reports per moderator, reversal rates, and outstanding escalation cases.
- Users must be able, via account dashboard, to view (in summary) the status of reports made, sanctions on their account, and the right to request explanation.

## 4. Content Visibility and Retention

### Visibility Rules
- Publicly visible content must meet all business and moderation standards, with real-time updates to reflect any status change (flagged, hidden, locked, deleted).
- WHERE content is flagged for review, THE system SHALL remove visibility from guest and member views (except author), and include banners indicating review status to the author.
- Removed or deleted content is immediately excluded from public and member (non-author) views, but remains accessible to moderators and admins for 60 days.
- Locked content is read-only and cannot receive new interactions; all users see a clear indication of lock reason/status.
- WHEN content is resolved (reviewed and deemed permissible or impermissible), THE system SHALL restore/hide with persistent notice as required by policy.

### Retention and Purge Policy
- Soft deleted content (via self-delete or moderator/admin removal) is maintained in system for minimum 60 days for audit and compliance before permanent purge, except when legal hold is applied.
- Members may request removal of authored content; request triggers review and, if approved, applies redaction policy (content replaced with marker, details retained for audit).
- Admins can place legal or investigation hold on deleted content, preventing purge until external release/auth approval.
- All scheduled purges are logged and subject to reversal pending admin action.

### User Requests and Data Subject Rights
- WHEN a user requests compliance deletion under law (e.g., GDPR/CCPA), THE system SHALL expedite removal of all personal and authored content, with audit logged.
- THE system SHALL provide summary of removed vs. retained (audit) data to the requesting party.

### Special Content Cases
- Attachments and embedded media follow the same visibility and retention guidelines as textual content.
- External references/links may be anonymized or redacted upon review where policy or law requires.

## 5. Examples and Edge Cases

### Example: Post Submission with Excessive Length
- WHEN a member submits a post exceeding 5,000 characters, THE system SHALL reject it, display a precise error citing the length limit, and allow trimming/resubmission.

### Example: Comment with Forbidden Word
- WHEN a member posts a comment containing a blacklisted term, THE system SHALL block submission, display the violation category (e.g., hate speech, profanity), and highlight user options (edit, cancel, appeal if applicable); repeated offenses trigger cooldown automatically.

### Example: Multiple Attachment Violation
- WHEN a post is submitted with 4 files attached (above allowed 3), THE system SHALL reject, list files by name exceeding policy, and permit user to adjust selection before retrying action.

### Example: Guest Attempts to Vote on Post
- WHEN a guest or unauthenticated user tries to upvote or downvote content, THE system SHALL prompt registration/login, preserving intended action (vote will be applied if/when authentication completes).

### Example: Concurrent Edit Attempt
- WHEN two members submit edits to the same post concurrently, THE system SHALL apply last-write-wins logic, record both edit histories, notify both editors of overwrite/collision, and flag for moderator review if disputed.

### Example: Moderator Removes Content after Edit Window
- WHEN a member attempts to delete own comment after edit/delete window passes, THE system SHALL block with a timed-out message and suggest moderator escalation; WHEN moderator acts for a business rule violation, THE system SHALL log action with context and retain for 60 days post-event.

### Example: Repeated Bad Report Filing
- WHEN a member files six unsupported (rejected) abuse reports in seven days, THE system SHALL suspend reporting privileges for that user for 48 hours and notify both user and moderators of action, including right to appeal.

### Example: Escalated User Ban Due to Multiple Incidents
- WHEN a user accumulates five or more valid abuse reports or three moderator interventions in 30 days, THE system SHALL auto-flag for admin review, restrict posting, and notify the user of impending action and appeal process.

### Example: Data Retention Hold for Legal Investigation
- WHEN law enforcement, judicial authority, or company counsel requests retention of deleted materials, THE system SHALL exclude affected data from scheduled purge, document the legal hold request, and maintain records securely until official release.

### Example: Attachment Deletion with Post Purge
- WHEN a post is permanently purged after 60 days, THE system SHALL ensure all associated file attachments are also deleted irreversibly, and log the action in purge report.

---

All requirements are actionable, measurable, and role-based, using EARS format per section wherever applicable. Cross-references to [Functional Requirements Specification](./05-functional-requirements.md), [User Roles and Authentication Framework](./03-user-roles-auth.md), and [User Scenarios and Exception Handling](./07-user-scenarios.md) for integration and further detail.

files.content:
# External Integrations and Data Flow Requirements for polEcoBoard

## 1. Introduction
polEcoBoard relies on various external services to deliver a secure, compliant, and scalable discussion experience. External integrations—covering authentication, analytics, anti-spam, notification, and consent management—must be designed with clear business rules and workflows. This specification details the necessary business logic, user journeys, error handling, and integration boundaries for all required third-party services, ensuring actionable requirements for backend implementation while avoiding technical or API-specific content. All requirements are given in EARS format or equivalently precise business language for direct execution by the backend team.

## 2. Third-party Service Requirements

### 2.1 Authentication and Identity Providers
- WHEN a user selects a third-party authentication option (e.g., Google, Facebook, Apple ID), THE system SHALL initiate the provider-specific flow and, upon receiving successful verification, SHALL create or update the user's polEcoBoard profile—storing verified email, display name, and consented metadata.
- IF a user denies authentication consent or closes the third-party login, THEN THE system SHALL return the user to the login/signup page and present a business error: "Authentication was canceled by the user. No account changes were made."
- WHERE third-party authentication data delivers an already verified email, THE system SHALL accept the verified status for email and forgo additional email verification steps.
- IF provider does not confirm verified email, THEN THE system SHALL require independent email verification following primary polEcoBoard workflows.
- WHERE third-party authentication conflicts with existing accounts (e.g., duplicate emails), THE system SHALL allow account linking or error the operation with a specific message: "An account with this email already exists. Please link or choose a different provider."
- THE system SHALL support sign-in and sign-up via standard, SSO, and federated identity providers according to user opt-in preferences.

### 2.2 Analytics and Insights Services
- WHEN users interact with the platform (view, post, comment, vote, report, login, session), THE system SHALL generate an anonymized, non-personal analytics event for each action and transmit it to the analytics provider(s).
- WHERE users opt out of analytics collection, THE system SHALL not transmit analytics for those sessions or actions, regardless of role.
- WHEN a guest user interacts, THE system SHALL report only non-identifying session metrics (browser, device, location to region/country-level, no cookies or tracking without explicit consent).
- THE system SHALL only transmit analytics events containing: action type, user role (non-PII), timestamp, session context, and anonymized identifiers consistent with privacy regulations.
- WHEN a user requests analytics erasure under privacy law, THE system SHALL signal to analytics providers to remove or anonymize records within the mandated business period.

### 2.3 Anti-spam, Abuse Prevention, and Moderation Tools
- WHEN a user submits content (post, comment), THE system SHALL transmit the relevant text, user role, content metadata (category, submission rate, language, IP region), to one or more anti-spam verification providers before making the content visible.
- IF anti-spam provider returns a high-probability or confirmed violation, THEN THE system SHALL prevent content publication and display a business message such as: "Your submission was flagged by automated review and was not published. You may appeal this decision."
- THE system SHALL provide users with an appeal workflow for false positive anti-spam returns: WHEN a member requests an appeal, THE system SHALL flag submission for manual moderator review and notify the user of the appeal status.
- WHERE the anti-spam provider is unavailable or slow beyond 5 seconds, THE system SHALL queue submissions for re-validation, inform the user: "We are experiencing review delays. Your content will be published after successful review."
- WHEN system degradation occurs, THE system SHALL store pending submissions securely until recovery and provide status updates via notification.
- Moderators and admins SHALL have an audit trail of all anti-spam actions for review and dispute, accessible via the moderation dashboard.

### 2.4 Notification and Messaging Services
- WHEN a trigger event (reply, mention, moderation action, account update, system notice, report status) occurs, THE system SHALL assemble a notification event containing relevant business metadata (user, role, channel, timestamp, urgency).
- THE system SHALL route notification to the user's preferred channel (email, push, in-app, or SMS) based on their configured preferences and opt-in status.
- WHERE delivery of a notification fails (provider/network outage detected by callback or error), THE system SHALL queue the notification for up to 24 hours with retry policies set in business rules. AFTER three consecutive failures, THE system SHALL generate an in-system alert and provide error context in the user's notification history.
- WHERE users choose to opt out of specific notification channels, THE system SHALL respect their preferences and route only to allowed channels.
- WHEN required by law, THE system SHALL default critical notifications (e.g., account compromise, policy update) to at least one channel still enabled, and inform the user of mandatory contact policies.

### 2.5 Consent, Privacy, and Data Residency
- WHEN any integration action requires sharing PII or non-anonymized data with an external provider, THE system SHALL seek explicit, revocable user consent and record consent status for audit.
- IF a user revokes consent for any integration (analytics, identity, notification), THEN THE system SHALL halt all data transmission to the relevant provider and confirm the change via the user's allowed notification channel within 24 hours.
- WHERE data residency rules restrict cross-border processing, THE system SHALL use a regionally-appropriate provider, or present explicit legal language informing the user, and require updated consent before transmitting data out-of-region.
- WHEN privacy rule changes (e.g., new GDPR or equivalent update) affect integration, THE system SHALL suspend outbound integrations for affected users until updated consent is received.
- Administrative and moderator access to provider integration logs SHALL be limited to business-justified, role-controlled dashboards, with audit trails of who accessed what integration and when.

## 3. Conceptual Data Flow

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "User Interaction"
        A["User Registration/Login"]
        B["User Post Submission"]
        C["User Comment/Vote/Report"]
        D["User Receives Notification"]
    end
    subgraph "Core System Logic"
        E["Account Management"]
        F["Content Validation"]
        G["Analytics Event Queue"]
        H["Notification Dispatch"]
    end
    subgraph "External Integrations"
        I["Third-party Authentication"]
        J["Anti-spam Service"]
        K["Analytics Platform"]
        L["Notification Provider"]
    end
    A --> E
    E -->|"Third-party login"| I
    B --> F
    F --> J
    C --> G
    G --> K
    B --> G
    F --> H
    H --> L
    L --> D
```

### 3.1 Data Flow Scenarios by User Role
- WHEN a guest browses public content, THE system SHALL not trigger authentication or privileged data integrations. Analytics events (view, browse) SHALL be anonymized.
- WHEN a member logs in via SSO, THE system SHALL initiate the provider handshake and update internal sessions only after email verification/consent steps are confirmed.
- WHEN a moderator/admin takes moderation action, THE system SHALL log event to analytics (with non-PII fields), trigger notification for relevant users, and, where workflow requires, interact with anti-spam provider (escalation flag).

### 3.2 Error and Privacy Flows
- IF any integration fails (e.g., analytics, notification, anti-spam) due to third-party issues, THE system SHALL provide immediate business explanation to the user, queue or re-attempt data exchange per the business policy, and retain full audit log of each event, result, and retry/failure resolution.
- WHEN a user exercises privacy rights (delete account, erase analytics record, revoke notification consent), THE system SHALL coordinate a full stop/erasure across all active integrations and confirm completion for audit/compliance.

## 4. Interaction Points with Third-party Services

### 4.1 Authentication Integration
- WHEN initiating third-party login, THE system SHALL validate provider is enabled and recognized for current locale/user region, and, if blocked or unsupported, inform the user: "This provider is not supported for your region."
- Admins SHALL be able to configure (enable/disable) third-party providers per business, legal, and operational needs. WHEN a provider is disabled, THE system SHALL present clear explanation on login screens.

### 4.2 Analytics Integration
- WHEN tracked actions are performed, THE system SHALL submit analytics events in batches where possible to reduce API overhead, except where real-time reporting is required by business rules (e.g., incident/event, moderator action).
- Members, moderators, and admins SHALL have configurable analytics opt-in/out (where privacy policy allows). Guests SHALL always operate under default anonymized analytics.

### 4.3 Anti-Spam Integration
- WHEN content is flagged as 'potential abuse' by internal rule or user report, THE system SHALL re-send to external anti-spam provider with additional business context for escalation and investigation.
- WHEN third-party review is completed, THE system SHALL update content status (approved, held, rejected), notify moderators and affected users, and require manual review for ambiguous or unresolved scores.
- Moderators SHALL receive special notification for content quarantined by integration, with workflow to release, escalate, or permanently remove.

### 4.4 Notification Service Integration
- WHEN a business event matches user notification rules, THE system SHALL compose and dispatch notification respecting all user, role, and region-specific settings—audit logging event content, delivery attempts, and user-level feedback (open/read/delete).
- IF repeated notification failures indicate persistent provider outage, THE system SHALL alert admins and allow switching to backup notification providers per business continuity plan.

### 4.5 Consent, Privacy, and Compliance Integration
- WHEN user privacy/consent status changes, THE system SHALL retrieve, store, and update provider-side preferences in real time, logging audit results for compliance.
- IF compliance conflict exists (e.g., data residency region mismatch), THEN THE system SHALL restrict all outbound traffic for the affected user until legal standing is resolved.

## 5. Business Logic for Integrations

### 5.1 Role-Based Integration Access
- WHERE user role implies restricted integration use (e.g., only moderators/admins may use audit/analytics dashboards, anti-spam override/retry tools, or advanced notification settings), THE system SHALL block unauthorized attempts and present a business explanation in the interface.
- All privileged actions via integrations SHALL be logged with user, timestamp, operation, and outcome for compliance.

### 5.2 Opt-in/Opt-out and Consent Handling
- WHEN presenting integration options (analytics, SSO, notifications), THE system SHALL default all non-essential integrations to explicit opt-in, with granular per-user and per-integration settings retained in the account profile.
- WHEN user status changes (revocation, opt-out, account closure), THE system SHALL update all provider-side status, remove PII, and present audit summary to the user within 24 hours.

### 5.3 Error Handling and Fallbacks
- IF an external integration (identity, analytics, anti-spam, notification) fails, THEN THE system SHALL log the incident, inform users of delay/impact, and, where function is business-critical, fall back to a manual or backup flow (e.g., manual moderation, in-app alert, batch re-send) until normal integration resumes.
- IF multiple integrations simultaneously fail (major provider incident), THEN THE system SHALL enter a "degraded mode," limiting new postings and account actions, communicating restrictions via alert banners and status notifications to all users, and ensuring incident status is visible to moderation and admin teams throughout.

### 5.4 Compliance and Region Constraints
- WHERE residency or compliance law restricts integration, THE system SHALL ensure only compliant providers are used, and shall record user consent and jurisdiction for every transmitted event. WHEN a change occurs, THE system SHALL trigger review by compliance administrators and require re-confirmed consent before re-enabling integrations for those users/accounts.

### 5.5 Scalability, Continuity, and Business Monitoring
- WHEN integration throughput approaches business or provider limits (API rate limits, quota ceilings), THE system SHALL monitor usage, implement per-provider business-logic backoff and notification, and inform impacted users and admins of degraded features in business language (e.g., delayed updates, retry windows).
- THE system SHALL support provider switching for critical functions (e.g., backup analytics, alternate notification provider) and require all integrations have business continuity plans executable by admins without technical intervention.
- All integration logs, consent modifications, opt-in/out events, and error/failure incidents SHALL be available to admins via audit dashboards for review and reporting as part of business compliance measures.

## 6. Reference to Related Documents
For detail on user permissions and authentication, see the [User Roles and Authentication Requirements](./03-user-roles-auth.md). Business logic for participation, moderation, and user workflows is specified in the [Functional Requirements Document](./05-functional-requirements.md) and [Business Rules and Validation](./08-business-rules.md). Service mission, business value, and compliance metrics appear in the [Service Overview and Business Model](./01-service-overview.md). Operational monitoring and analytics are covered in the [Operations and Reporting Specification](./10-operations-reporting.md).

## 7. Success Criteria and Constraints
- THE system SHALL provide comprehensive opt-in/out, audit, and notification flows for every integration and user role.
- All integrations SHALL operate within documented consent, privacy, business, and compliance boundaries at all times.
- THE system SHALL ensure at least one backup provider or manual fallback for every critical integration. No single provider SHALL constitute a single point of failure for a core system function.
- Role-based permissions, region, and consent status SHALL be enforced at integration boundary with real-time auditability (logs, dashboards) for moderators and admins.
- Integration failures SHALL never result in silent data loss or privilege escalation—instead, all flow interruptions SHALL be communicated instantly in actionable business terms to users and staff.
- Where legislative or compliance requirements change, THE system SHALL pause affected integrations and require explicit new consent from users to resume affected flows.
- All integration business requirements, error flows, role restrictions, and compliance scenarios described herein are enforceable measures for backend implementation.

## 8. Expanded Glossary
- **Integration**: Business-governed transfer or sharing of data with external service providers (not technical contacts/APIs).
- **Consent**: Active, revocable agreement by the user to share specific data for specific integrations, with record-traceable audit.
- **Third-party Provider**: Any approved external service trusted by polEcoBoard for non-core functions (auth, analytics, notifications, anti-spam, compliance).
- **Business Boundary**: The logical perimeter at which polEcoBoard delegates process or decision to an external party, triggering business process completion or waiting for response.
- **Degraded Mode**: Temporary statewide restriction of features pending restoration of essential external integrations; communicated in business language platform-wide.
- **Audit Trail**: Immutable business record of integration actions, consent changes, error incidents, and privileged access for compliance review.
- **PII (Personally Identifiable Information)**: Any data that can identify a user directly or indirectly—treated with explicit consent and residency compliance.
- **Manual Fallback**: Human (moderator/admin) process used to maintain business process continuity when automation or integration is impaired.
- **Role-based Access**: Principle limiting integration use to users with permission (e.g., only admins can review logs, only moderators can override anti-spam decisions, etc.).
- **Provider Switching**: Business process to change between approved providers in case of outage, regional restriction, or compliance need.
- **Region and Residency**: Data locality jurisdiction governing what providers and flows are permissible; requires per-event compliance and auditability.

---

All requirements, scenarios, and flows specified are business-facing only. All technical implementation decisions (architecture, APIs, schemas) are solely within developer discretion. This document specifies WHAT business operations and requirements all polEcoBoard external integrations must support and enforce.

# Operations and Reporting Requirements for polEcoBoard

## 1. System Operation and Monitoring

### 1.1 Service Health and Uptime Monitoring
- THE system SHALL provide real-time health indicators covering API responsiveness, database connectivity, major background services, and external third-party integrations.
- WHEN any monitored subsystem (API, DB, service, integration) becomes unresponsive for more than 30 seconds, THE system SHALL trigger a service alert visible to admins.
- WHEN system-wide error rates exceed 1% within a rolling 5-minute window, THE system SHALL log this as an operational event and notify admins immediately.
- THE system SHALL support summary dashboards aggregating service uptime, latency, error frequencies, content publishing rates, and login activity.
- WHERE system monitoring is degraded or data sources are missing, THE system SHALL mark the impacted metrics as unavailable and raise an admin-only warning event.

### 1.2 Operational Dashboards
- THE system SHALL allow admins to view dashboards summarizing current and historical stats for user sign-ups, posts, comments, votes, abuse reports, suspensions/bans, and system errors.
- THE system SHALL allow moderators access to dashboards specific to their moderation areas (e.g., content queue length, flagged posts, review status).
- WHERE a member accesses operational dashboards, THE system SHALL restrict access to only their own contribution summaries and exclude system-wide metrics.
- THE system SHALL automatically refresh dashboard data at intervals no longer than 60 seconds.

### 1.3 Alerting and Proactive Notification
- WHEN system performance degrades (e.g., 95th percentile response time exceeds 2 seconds or job queues exceed thresholds), THE system SHALL generate operational alerts for admins.
- WHEN the number of unresolved abuse reports exceeds the configured threshold, THE system SHALL alert moderators responsible for that content category.
- WHEN a scheduled maintenance window is upcoming (within 24 hours), THE system SHALL notify all moderators and admins with the expected downtime, scope, and recovery plan.

### 1.4 Data Retention and Compliance Operations
- THE system SHALL allow admins to configure data retention periods for business audit data, error logs, abuse reports, and user activity based on policy and compliance requirements.
- WHEN retention limits are reached, THE system SHALL perform automated purging consistent with policy and audit requirements, with full event records prior to erasure.
- IF retention policies are changed, THEN THE system SHALL log and report such changes to admins for review.


## 2. Business Event Processing (Moderation, Reports, User Actions)

### 2.1 Event Tracking and Auditing
- THE system SHALL record detailed audit trails for all moderator and admin actions, including content deletion/restoration, user suspensions, policy changes, and configuration updates.
- WHEN a moderator or admin changes any policy or configuration, THE system SHALL require an action description and reason for the audit log.
- WHEN a user (member, guest) is subjected to a moderation action (warning, suspension, ban, content edit/deletion), THE system SHALL record the event, responsible staff, and user notification status.

### 2.2 Notification and Escalation Flows
- WHEN content is reported by users, THE system SHALL queue it for moderator review, recording timestamps for report, assignment, review, and resolution.
- IF reported content is not reviewed within the business-defined SLA (e.g., 24 hours), THEN THE system SHALL escalate the event to admins with priority notification.
- WHEN moderators close abuse reports, THE system SHALL notify the reporting member of the decision with a status code (accepted, rejected, action taken, no action).

### 2.3 Event-Based Automation
- WHEN content thresholds are reached (e.g., post receives >N reports or downvotes in M minutes), THE system SHALL temporarily hide the content pending moderator review, notify all affected parties, and log the action.
- WHEN a user’s privileges are automatically restricted due to behavioral triggers (e.g., repeated abuse, excessive spam, failed login attempts), THE system SHALL notify the user, responsible moderator, and log the reason and evidence.
- WHERE admins designate an event as sensitive (e.g., election interference, major legal risk), THE system SHALL enable enhanced tracking, limiting event data access strictly to moderators and admins assigned to that review.

### 2.4 Example: Moderation Lifecycle (Mermaid)
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Business Event Processing"
        A["Content Reported by Member"] --> B["Event Queued for Moderator Review"]
        B --> C{"Is SLA Breached?"}
        C -->|"No"| D["Moderator Reviews Report"]
        D --> E{"Action Needed?"}
        E -->|"Yes"| F["Content Modified/Removed"]
        E -->|"No"| G["No Action Taken"]
        F --> H["Reporter Notified - Action Taken"]
        G --> I["Reporter Notified - No Action"]
        C -->|"Yes"| J["Escalated to Admin"]
    end
```


## 3. Administrative Analytics and Reporting Needs

### 3.1 Core Business Metrics
- THE system SHALL support reports and data exports for admins covering:
    - User growth and activity trends (DAU, WAU, MAU)
    - Content creation rates, engagement volumes
    - Moderation workload (reviewed/closed reports per period, time-to-resolution, decision types)
    - Abuse report response rates, outcomes, and escalation frequency
    - User retention, suspensions, bans, and appeals statistics
    - Popular discussion topics, trending tags, and top contributors
    - Audit log summaries by staff and event type
    - Data subject access requests and deletion requests (compliance)
- WHERE moderators access analytics, THE system SHALL filter results to only their assigned categories/content areas.
- WHERE members access analytics, THE system SHALL restrict visibility to their own activity (contributions, reports, bans/suspensions received).

### 3.2 Custom and Scheduled Reports
- THE system SHALL allow admins (and authorized moderators) to configure scheduled recurring reports (daily/weekly/monthly) for key operational and business metrics, delivered via secure notification.
- WHEN ad-hoc reporting is requested, THE system SHALL provide selectable criteria for content type, user cohort, time range, and moderation event types.
- WHEN a report is generated, THE system SHALL log the report request, creator, and delivery status for auditability.
- WHERE regulatory or compliance reports are required (e.g., data export of banned users), THE system SHALL provide compliant data exports and audit their issuance.

### 3.3 Notification and Data Access Permissions
- THE system SHALL enforce strict role-based access for all analytics—billing/usage, moderation, user growth, and compliance—with visibility set by the permission matrix (see [User Roles and Authentication Business Requirement Document](./03-user-roles-auth.md)).
- WHERE an analytics/reporting function is attempted by an unauthorized role, THE system SHALL deny access and record the attempt.


## 4. Incident and Change Management

### 4.1 Service Incident Tracking
- THE system SHALL record all significant service disruptions including downtime, major errors, failed integrations, or degraded performance as separate incident events.
- WHEN an incident reaches business-defined thresholds (e.g., >5 mins outage, critical error), THE system SHALL initiate a formal incident record with timestamps, nature of disruption, responsible staff, communication sequence, and resolution details.
- THE system SHALL provide admins with a timeline view of incident occurrence, investigation, mitigation, and recovery.
- WHEN an incident is resolved, THE system SHALL require a resolution summary and optionally attach follow-up tasks or business process reviews.

### 4.2 Audit Trails for Change Management
- WHEN any business policy, role permission, configuration, or notification template is changed, THE system SHALL log the before/after state, user, timestamp, and reason for change.
- THE system SHALL allow admins to search and filter all change records by time, actor, and area of impact.
- WHERE any unauthorized attempt to change protected settings is made, THE system SHALL block the attempt, notify admins, and log the event for escalation.

### 4.3 Example: Incident Management Flow (Mermaid)
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Incident Lifecycle"
        A["Service Incident Detected"] --> B["Incident Record Created"]
        B --> C["Staff Assignment and Acknowledgement"]
        C --> D["Investigation Ongoing"]
        D --> E{"Mitigated?"}
        E -->|"Yes"| F["Normal Operations Restored"]
        E -->|"No"| G["Escalate to Admin/External Support"]
        F --> H["Resolution Summary Logged"]
        G --> H
    end
```


## 5. Role-Based Permission Matrix for Operations/Reporting

| Action/Feature                                               | Guest | Member | Moderator | Admin |
|--------------------------------------------------------------|:-----:|:------:|:---------:|:-----:|
| View operational dashboards (overall/system-wide)            |  ❌   |   ❌   |   ❌      |  ✅  |
| View own activity dashboard                                  |  ❌   |   ✅   |   ✅      |  ✅  |
| View moderation queue / category dashboards                  |  ❌   |   ❌   |   ✅      |  ✅  |
| Access error/service health monitoring                       |  ❌   |   ❌   |   ❌      |  ✅  |
| Audit logs (actions, policy/config changes)                  |  ❌   |   ❌   |   ✅      |  ✅  |
| Business analytics (overall)                                 |  ❌   |   ❌   |   ❌      |  ✅  |
| Analytics (category-specific)                                |  ❌   |   ❌   |   ✅      |  ✅  |
| Analytics (own contributions)                                |  ❌   |   ✅   |   ✅      |  ✅  |
| Receive system incident/maintenance alerts                   |  ❌   |   ❌   |   ✅      |  ✅  |
| Change management / config updates                           |  ❌   |   ❌   |   ❌      |  ✅  |
| Request/receive scheduled/adhoc reports                      |  ❌   |   ❌   |   ✅      |  ✅  |
| Export compliance/legal data (users, abuse, audit, etc.)     |  ❌   |   ❌   |   ❌      |  ✅  |


## 6. Error and Exception Handling for Operation Events
- IF any reporting, audit, or analytics function fails due to data retrieval errors, access denial, or policy mismatch, THEN THE system SHALL notify the user with a specific error code and log the incident for review.
- IF a scheduled or generated report cannot be delivered to the intended recipient, THEN THE system SHALL provide delivery status with guidance on re-issue or escalation.
- IF retention or compliance policy conflicts are detected during a purge, THEN THE system SHALL halt the operation, notify admins, and require business input/info before proceeding.
- WHEN operational alerts are triggered but no designated staff acknowledges within SLA, THE system SHALL escalate and record the event.


## 7. Performance and Responsiveness
- WHEN operational dashboards or reports are accessed by authorized users, THE system SHALL load data and visualizations within 3 seconds under normal operating loads.
- WHEN event or incident data is recorded, THE system SHALL ensure the audit or incident entry is available for review within 5 seconds of event completion.


## 8. Visual Summary: System Operation & Event Monitoring Overview
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Service Operation Monitoring"
        A["System Health Signals"] --> B["Dashboards/Alerts"]
        B --> C["Admin/Maintenance Review"]
    end
    subgraph "Business Event Tracing"
        D["Content/Member Events (Post, Report, Ban, etc.)"] --> E["Audit/Event Logging"]
        E --> F["Analytics & Reports"]
        F --> G["Admin Review & Compliance"]
    end
    A --> D
```


## 9. Data Retention and Privacy
- THE system SHALL allow admins to configure, review, and update retention settings for all operational, audit, and analytics data in line with current legal and policy requirements.
- WHERE data is marked for deletion, THE system SHALL provide a preview, approval path, and full audit record of action taken.
- THE system SHALL ensure only authorized roles may access, export, or purge operational/analytics/audit data; all actions require explicit logging.


## 10. Success Metrics and KPIs
- THE system SHALL support extraction and reporting of key operational KPIs, including response time compliance, mean time to acknowledge/resolve incidents, moderation efficiency, business event volumes, and data access audit rates.
- THE system SHALL allow admins to define additional custom metrics in future without code changes required for each new metric.


---

This document provides business requirements only. All technical implementation decisions (including architecture, API structure, storage, and external service selection) are at the sole discretion of backend developers. The document describes WHAT the system must enable for operations and reporting, not HOW to build it.
