### `pol_eco_board_board_statuses`

Tracks the dynamic status of each board (such as open, locked, archived,
visible, or hidden) for business logic and audit trail purposes. Each
record represents a status change event for a single board, with
effective time, responsible actor, and rationale for the change. Supports
reporting and compliance tracking of board accessibility and moderation
actions. Links to the target board, relevant actor (admin or moderator),
and includes fields for status type, effective timestamp, and status
detail.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `pol_eco_board_board_id`: Board's [pol_eco_board_boards.id](#pol_eco_board_boards) to which this status applies.
- `actor_moderator_id`
  > Moderator's [pol_eco_board_moderators.id](#pol_eco_board_moderators) responsible for this
  > status change (if set by a moderator).
- `actor_admin_id`
  > Admin's [pol_eco_board_admins.id](#pol_eco_board_admins) responsible for this status
  > change (if set by an admin).
- `status_type`
  > Type of board status (e.g., open, locked, archived, visible, hidden,
  > merging, splitting, etc). Used for operational logic and reporting;
  > business logic dictates permissible values.
- `effective_at`: Date and time the status became effective.
- `reason`
  > Business rationale or free-text explanation for status change (e.g.,
  > moderation reason, admin action, scheduled maintenance).
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last update to this record.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when this record was soft-deleted (if applicable).

### `pol_eco_board_board_histories`

Preserves historical records of board assignments and organizational
changes. Each record represents a structural or ownership change, such as
moving a board between categories, reassigning responsibility, or other
changes impacting board lineage and reporting. Supports full auditability
of board organizational structure and facilitates operations reporting.
References the relevant board, previous and new category, and the acting
admin or moderator.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `pol_eco_board_board_id`: Board's [pol_eco_board_boards.id](#pol_eco_board_boards) related to this history change.
- `previous_category_id`
  > The [pol_eco_board_categories.id](#pol_eco_board_categories) the board was previously assigned
  > to (null if first assignment).
- `new_category_id`
  > The [pol_eco_board_categories.id](#pol_eco_board_categories) the board is assigned to after
  > the change.
- `actor_admin_id`
  > The [pol_eco_board_admins.id](#pol_eco_board_admins) admin who performed the change (if by
  > admin).
- `actor_moderator_id`
  > The [pol_eco_board_moderators.id](#pol_eco_board_moderators) moderator who performed the
  > change (if by moderator).
- `change_type`
  > Type of change (e.g., reassignment, merge, split, archive, ownership
  > transfer). Business logic constrains allowed values, tracked for audit
  > and reporting.
- `change_reason`
  > Business rationale or description for the change (optional), supporting
  > audit trails and operational reporting.
- `changed_at`: Timestamp when the change occurred.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of the last update to this record.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when this record was soft-deleted (if applicable).

### `pol_eco_board_moderator_board_assignments`

Junction table linking moderators to boards, representing operational
moderation assignments. Supports many-to-many mapping of which moderators
are actively assigned to which boards. Tracks assignment start, end (if
expired/removed), role transfer log, and assignment rationale. Enables
runtime dashboards, compliance, and audit trails of moderator coverage
for every board or sub-board. References boards and moderators from
existing tables.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `pol_eco_board_moderator_id`: Moderator's [pol_eco_board_moderators.id](#pol_eco_board_moderators) assigned to this board.
- `pol_eco_board_board_id`: Board's [pol_eco_board_boards.id](#pol_eco_board_boards) for which this assignment applies.
- `assigned_by_admin_id`

  > (nullable if self-assignment/automatic).
- `assigned_at`
  > Timestamp the assignment began (i.e. when the moderator was linked to the
  > board).
- `ended_at`: Timestamp the assignment ended (null if currently active).
- `role_transfer_log`

  > audit. Useful for documenting manual overrides or special cases.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for this assignment record.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when this record was soft-deleted (if applicable).

### `pol_eco_board_posts`

Primary business table for user-authored discussion posts. Each post
represents an authored topic or thread under a specific category/board
(referenced externally). Records immutable author, timestamps, and core
data needed for content management, moderation, audit, and retention.
Supports tagging, voting, comment chains, and moderation/reporting via
separate tables. Stores only raw post data—no calculated aggregates.
Historical edits captured in pol_eco_board_post_edits. Soft delete is
enabled for retention/audit.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `author_member_id`
  > Belonged author's [pol_eco_board_members.id](#pol_eco_board_members). Immutable creator
  > reference for traceability.
- `category_id`
  > Category's [pol_eco_board_categories.id](#pol_eco_board_categories) for post organization and
  > visibility. Immutable after creation.
- `title`
  > Post title, required, business-validated length (10-120 chars), may not
  > contain prohibited terms. Used for display, search, and navigation.
- `body`
  > Main body of the post content. Min: 10, Max: 10000 chars. Allows markdown
  > or limited markup. Sanitized and validated on submission.
- `comment_count`
  > Number of first-level comments. Updated by triggers for performance but
  > not denormalized with business aggregates outside this table.
- `view_count`
  > Number of times the post has been viewed. Used for engagement tracking.
  > Not business critical but monitored for analytics.
- `flagged`
  > True if post is flagged for moderation/review. Set by reporting/voting
  > business rules or moderation actions.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp for post creation. Used for ordering and retention policies.
  > Immutable.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp of last edit or business update. Updated only by allowed
  > business flows. Used by audit logic.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete marker. Set when deleted by user or moderator. Retained for
  > audit period, NULL if active.

### `pol_eco_board_post_edits`

Edit history and audit trail for all edits to pol_eco_board_posts. Each
row is a snapshot of post content at a given edit. Used for moderation,
accountability, and viewing edit history. Links to post, editor, and
stores previous state. Not a materialized view—every revision is
immutable. Permanent part of audit trail (no user deletions).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: Original post's [pol_eco_board_posts.id](#pol_eco_board_posts) being edited.
- `editor_member_id`: Member's [pol_eco_board_members.id](#pol_eco_board_members) who performed the edit.
- `edit_body`
  > Body content for edit snapshot. Full state of post body at the time of
  > edit. Used for rollback and audit.
- `edit_reason`
  > Reason for edit, supplied by editor or system. Required for moderation,
  > optional for self-edits.
- `created_at`: Timestamp for edit operation (immutable).

### `pol_eco_board_comments`

Primary business table for comments on posts. Supports threaded
(single-level reply) discussion under each post. Authored by members.
Each comment is associated to a post (pol_eco_board_posts), and has
immutable author, timestamps, content, and moderation state. Edit and
audit history in pol_eco_board_comment_edits.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: Associated post's [pol_eco_board_posts.id](#pol_eco_board_posts).
- `author_member_id`: Authoring member's [pol_eco_board_members.id](#pol_eco_board_members).
- `parent_comment_id`
  > If reply-to is used, parent comment's [pol_eco_board_comments.id](#pol_eco_board_comments).
  > Null if top-level comment. Restricts to one reply level (no deep
  > threading).
- `body`
  > Comment body. 5-1000 chars, applies content rule validations, trimmed and
  > sanitized.
- `flagged`
  > True if comment is flagged for moderation. Triggers workflow for
  > moderator review.
- `created_at`
  > Creation time. Used for ordering and rate limits (e.g., member can't
  > comment repeatedly within short period).
- `updated_at`
  > Latest edit/update time for audit. Must be kept current for edit
  > workflows.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete marker. Null if active, otherwise holds time of deletion
  > (retained for audit/compliance duration).

### `pol_eco_board_comment_edits`

Edit history and audit trail for all edits to pol_eco_board_comments.
Stores each change as immutable row referencing comment and editor.
Permanent audit trail—no user deletions allowed. Used for rollback,
moderation, and review of edit history.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `comment_id`: Comment's [pol_eco_board_comments.id](#pol_eco_board_comments) being edited.
- `editor_member_id`: Member's [pol_eco_board_members.id](#pol_eco_board_members) who performed the edit.
- `edit_body`: Body of the comment at time of edit. Full snapshot for rollback/audit.
- `edit_reason`: Reason given for edit; may be user-entered or system-determined.
- `created_at`: When edit operation occurred.

### `pol_eco_board_votes`

Voting actions on posts/comments by eligible participants. Supports
upvote/downvote for post or comment (one per member per item). Immutable
business log of voting behavior for each content unit, with audit.
Member, post or comment, and value (up/down) strictly recorded.
Duplicate/invalid voting prevented by design. Used for both engagement
display and moderation/escalation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `voter_member_id`
  > Voter's [pol_eco_board_members.id](#pol_eco_board_members). Necessary for quota, abuse
  > detection, and audit.
- `post_id`
  > Voted post [pol_eco_board_posts.id](#pol_eco_board_posts), if applies. Null if vote is on
  > comment.
- `comment_id`
  > Voted comment [pol_eco_board_comments.id](#pol_eco_board_comments), if applies. Null if vote
  > is on post.
- `vote_value`
  > 1 for upvote, -1 for downvote. Used for efficient tally and abuse
  > detection. Value must be in set {1, -1}; min/max constraints at business
  > layer.
- `created_at`: When the vote occurred. Used for rate limits and duplicate prevention.

### `pol_eco_board_tags`

Tags available for categorizing posts. Used for search, filtering, and
analytics, subject to admin management. Tags must be unique, normalized
(slug), and cannot be deleted if in use (cascades managed at
business/application layer).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `name`
  > Tag display name (case-insensitive unique constraint, validated for
  > allowed chars/length 3-30).
- `slug`
  > Normalized slug for search/filter. Must be unique and lowercase
  > (URL-safe).
- `description`: Short human-friendly tag explanation (30-120 chars).
- `created_at`: Creation time for audit/history.

### `pol_eco_board_post_tags`

Junction table mapping posts to tags (M:N relationship). Each row
connects one post with one tag; together forms many-to-many mapping for
filtering/search. No duplicates by unique composite index. Must reference
only active posts/tags. No denormalized data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: Reference to post [pol_eco_board_posts.id](#pol_eco_board_posts).
- `tag_id`: Reference to tag [pol_eco_board_tags.id](#pol_eco_board_tags).
- `assigned_at`: Timestamp specifying when the tag was applied to the post.

### `pol_eco_board_reports`

User/member reports on posts or comments for abuse/inappropriateness.
Includes reason, type, and optional description supplied by the reporter.
Status of moderation report is managed in other domains (moderation can
reference this ID for action). Each report links to exactly one post or
comment (not both), and to the reporting member. Used for workflow
triggering, abuse management, and analytics. Immutable for audit
purposes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `reporter_member_id`
  > Member's [pol_eco_board_members.id](#pol_eco_board_members) who submitted the report.
  > Audited for abuse prevention.
- `post_id`
  > If reporting a post, reference [pol_eco_board_posts.id](#pol_eco_board_posts). Null if
  > report targets a comment.
- `comment_id`
  > If reporting a comment, reference [pol_eco_board_comments.id](#pol_eco_board_comments). Null
  > if report targets a post.
- `reason_code`
  > Report type (e.g., spam, hate, off-topic, abuse, other). Must match
  > business-validated admin codes.
- `reason_description`
  > User-supplied optional description/details. Max length enforced at
  > business layer (e.g., 250-400 chars).
- `created_at`: When report was submitted. Used for review queue and escalation SLAs.

### `pol_eco_board_attachments`

File attachments to posts. Each row represents a file uploaded and
attached to a specific post by a member (author). Attachments follow
business rules after post creation. File reference (uri) must be unique,
and only permitted types/size enforced at application layer. Null
deleted_at = active; soft delete for retention. Cascading deletion
follows business and legal hold rules.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `post_id`: Parent post's [pol_eco_board_posts.id](#pol_eco_board_posts). Must be active post.
- `author_member_id`
  > Uploader's [pol_eco_board_members.id](#pol_eco_board_members) (must match post author for
  > ordinary attachments).
- `uri`
  > Location/identifier for file in storage bucket. Immutable. Must be unique
  > per attachment.
- `file_name`: Original file name as supplied, used for display and audit.
- `file_size_bytes`
  > File size in bytes. Limits enforced at application level (business rules:
  > 10MB max/file, 20MB/post).
- `mime_type`
  > Detected MIME type (e.g., 'image/png'). Used for business acceptance and
  > audit.
- `created_at`: Time of upload/attachment.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete marker. Null if active.

### `pol_eco_board_moderation_actions`

Represents a single moderation action (decision, removal, warning, etc.)
taken on reported content. Each record captures the moderation activity,
its executor (moderator/admin), linked report/reference object, operating
context (post, comment, or user), action type, rationale, and
status/result. This model creates a traceable primary record for every
business or privilege-sensitive action, and serves as the authoritative
source of action events for compliance or audit purposes. Links to
pol_eco_board_reports for the underlying content or event. Also
references staff identity via moderator or admin ids from existing user
tables.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `report_id`: Moderated report's [pol_eco_board_reports.id](#pol_eco_board_reports).
- `operator_id`
  > Moderator or admin's [pol_eco_board_moderators.id](#pol_eco_board_moderators) or {@link
  > pol_eco_board_admins.id}. (References either role according to context;
  > use discriminator field in application logic).
- `action_type`: Type of moderation action (e.g., edit, remove, warn, suspend, escalate).
- `target_type`: Object of moderation (e.g., post, comment, user, attachment).
- `status`: Current status of this action (pending, completed, overruled, etc.).
- `rationale`
  > Business reason, operator justification or notes. Required for
  > auditability. Max 1000 chars.
- `outcome`: Result/outcome of action (accepted, rejected, escalated, appealed, etc.)
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the moderation action was created.
- `updated_at`: Last update time for this moderation action record.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp if this action was removed.

### `pol_eco_board_moderation_audits`

Captures comprehensive audit logs for all moderation actions, including
pre- and post-action state snapshots, actor identity, and audit metadata.
Enables historical tracing and compliance review of all sensitive
moderation processes. Every change to a moderation action (remove, edit,
escalate) is logged here for transparency and dispute resolution. Links
to both action and operator. Provides full visibility into the decision
lifecycle.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `moderation_action_id`: Related moderation action's [pol_eco_board_moderation_actions.id](#pol_eco_board_moderation_actions).
- `auditor_id`
  > Auditor (usually admin or lead moderator) identity, references {@link
  > pol_eco_board_admins.id} or [pol_eco_board_moderators.id](#pol_eco_board_moderators). Use
  > business logic to distinguish role.
- `pre_state_snapshot`
  > Serialized JSON/text snapshot of moderation action before change. Max
  > size 2000 chars.
- `post_state_snapshot`: Serialized JSON/text snapshot after action. Max size 2000 chars.
- `reason`: Reason for the audit/change. Max 1000 chars.
- `created_at`: Audit record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update time for this audit record.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp.

### `pol_eco_board_sanctions`

Formal record of sanctions (temporary or permanent) issued as a result of
moderation. Includes details about type, target (user/member/moderator),
status, rationale, and duration. Links directly to the action and
sanctioned entity for full audit trail. Used for account suspensions,
bans, and other participation restrictions. All sanctions must be
traceable to the initiating moderation action, with full compliance
support.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `moderation_action_id`
  > Underlying moderation action that produced the sanction. {@link
  > pol_eco_board_moderation_actions.id}.
- `sanctioned_user_id`
  > User/member account subject to sanctioning. References {@link
  > pol_eco_board_members.id}.
- `sanction_type`: Type of sanction (suspension, ban, warning, probation, cooldown).
- `status`: Sanction status (active, expired, revoked, appealed, overruled).
- `rationale`: Business reason or policy link for the sanction. Max 1000 chars.
- `start_at`: When the sanction takes effect.
- `end_at`: Scheduled end of sanction (null for permanent/indefinite).
- `created_at`: Record creation date/time.
- `updated_at`: Record last update date/time.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp, if sanction is removed or redacted.

### `pol_eco_board_escalations`

Tracks escalation events in the moderation process. Used when a case
requires review by higher authority (e.g., admin-level review, legal, or
risk escalation). Records triggering moderation action, escalation
initiator, recipient (target admin), reason, and status. Ensures every
escalated case has a controllable audit chain. Provides a paper trail for
disputes, legal compliance, and risk management.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `moderation_action_id`
  > The moderation action being escalated. {@link
  > pol_eco_board_moderation_actions.id}.
- `escalator_id`
  > User/Moderator initiating escalation. References {@link
  > pol_eco_board_moderators.id}.
- `recipient_admin_id`: Admin reviewing/escalated to. References [pol_eco_board_admins.id](#pol_eco_board_admins).
- `reason`: Reason/notes for escalating the action. Up to 1000 chars.
- `status`: Escalation status (pending, resolved, rejected).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp.

### `pol_eco_board_appeals`

Represents user or moderator appeals against moderation outcomes. Each
appeal is linked to the original action, includes the appellant (member
or moderator), appeal reason, status, reviewed-by field, and outcome
result. Supports full audit trail of business appeal and resolution logic
for compliance. Allows users to contest sanctions or actions taken
against them via properly controlled workflows.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `moderation_action_id`
  > The moderation action being appealed. {@link
  > pol_eco_board_moderation_actions.id}.
- `appellant_id`
  > The user or moderator submitting the appeal. References {@link
  > pol_eco_board_members.id} or [pol_eco_board_moderators.id](#pol_eco_board_moderators).
- `reviewer_admin_id`
  > Admin or authorized moderator reviewing the appeal. References {@link
  > pol_eco_board_admins.id}.
- `reason`: Appellant's rationale for requesting the appeal. Max 1000 chars.
- `status`: Appeal status (pending, in_review, resolved, rejected, upheld, overruled).
- `outcome`: Result of the appeal process. (approved, denied, modified, escalated)
- `created_at`: Appeal creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Appeal last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp.

### `pol_eco_board_notifications`

Stores every notification event generated for users, including delivery
status, event type, recipient linkage, and time stamps. Each record
represents a single notification instance requiring delivery and history
retention independent from participation or content actions. Links to the
intended user (member, moderator, or admin) via foreign key, and
optionally to the related provider and originating post/comment/report as
appropriate. Enables audit trail for notifications and supports
operational, compliance, and privacy purge requirements.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `recipient_member_id`
  > Recipient's [pol_eco_board_members.id](#pol_eco_board_members). References the user to whom
  > the notification is delivered (can be member, moderator, or admin).
- `provider_id`
  > Notification provider's [pol_eco_board_notification_providers.id](#pol_eco_board_notification_providers).
  > Identifies the provider/service used for this notification attempt.
- `event_type`
  > Business event type code or category, e.g., 'reply', 'moderation_action',
  > 'report_status', 'admin_notice'. Used for filtering and analytics.
- `related_object_id`
  > UUID of related business object (e.g., post, comment, report, etc.) for
  > audit and navigation. References the source event but is not a foreign
  > key to keep polymorphism. Can be null for global or system-wide
  > notifications.
- `status`
  > Current delivery status of the notification (e.g., 'pending',
  > 'delivered', 'failed'). Used for tracking and reporting.
- `attempt_count`
  > Number of delivery attempts made so far for this notification event. Used
  > for retry/backoff logic and audit.
- `last_attempted_at`
  > Timestamp of the most recent delivery attempt for this notification.
  > Updated on each send try, used for troubleshooting and audit.
- `delivered_at`
  > Timestamp when notification was successfully delivered. Set if and only
  > if status is 'delivered'. Null otherwise.
- `created_at`
  > Created timestamp for audit trail; when the notification was initially
  > generated.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp; reflects status/attempt count updates.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for privacy purge. Null if notification is active.

### `pol_eco_board_notification_preferences`

Holds explicit notification opt-in/out settings and channel preferences
for each member, separated from user profile for privacy and audit
clarity. Each row applies to a single user and event type/channel
combination, supporting granular user control and compliance evidence.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `member_id`
  > User's [pol_eco_board_members.id](#pol_eco_board_members). References the member whose
  > preference is being recorded.
- `event_type`
  > Type of event this preference relates to (e.g., 'reply',
  > 'moderation_action', 'admin_notice').
- `channel`
  > Delivery channel: 'email', 'push', 'in_app', or 'sms' (enumerate in
  > application logic, not DB constraint at this level).
- `opt_in`
  > Whether the member has explicitly opted in (true) or out (false) of this
  > notification type/channel combination. Used for privacy and regulatory
  > compliance.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp preference was first recorded. Supports opt-in/out consent
  > auditability.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last preference change or user update.

### `pol_eco_board_notification_failures`

Retains all failed notification delivery attempts, supporting technical
diagnostics, reporting, and compliance audits. Each row records a failure
for a specific notification, including provider, technical details, and
timestamps. Enables operational and privacy retention policies for
notification-specific failures.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `notification_id`
  > Associated notification's [pol_eco_board_notifications.id](#pol_eco_board_notifications). Each
  > failure is tied to an attempted notification event.
- `provider_id`
  > Provider involved in the failed delivery (references {@link
  > pol_eco_board_notification_providers.id}). May be null where failure is
  > internal to system and not a provider.
- `failure_code`
  > Provider- or system-assigned error code describing the reason for failure
  > (business-level string, not system enum).
- `failure_message`
  > Human-readable summary of the failure cause, suitable for diagnostics,
  > audit, and support.
- `occurred_at`
  > Timestamp when the failure was recorded or detected. Used for analytics
  > and time-slicing incident review.
- `resolution_status`
  > Resolution or status of the failure event: e.g., 'pending', 'resolved',
  > 'permanent_failure'. For operational reporting and closure.
- `created_at`
  > Created timestamp for record/audit. Indicates when the failure was
  > entered.
- `updated_at`: Updated timestamp to track changes in resolution/status.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp for compliance or privacy purge, may be null if
  > not yet deleted.

### `pol_eco_board_external_auth_providers`

Represents authorized external authentication providers (e.g., Google,
Facebook, Apple) integrated for polEcoBoard user sign-in flows. Used for
compliance, audit, and dynamic provider switching. Each record uniquely
identifies a provider, manages status (enabled/disabled), and stores
privacy/compliance settings relevant to integration. Does not contain
user authentication data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `provider_name`
  > The human-readable name of the authentication provider (e.g., Google,
  > Facebook, Apple).
- `provider_key`
  > Unique internal key or code identifying the provider integration (e.g.,
  > 'google', 'facebook'). Used for configuration and provider switching.
- `status`
  > Current status of the provider integration. Valid values: 'enabled',
  > 'disabled', 'maintenance'. Enforces which providers are available to the
  > system.
- `privacy_policy_uri`: The URI to the provider's privacy policy for compliance display to users.
- `data_residency_region`
  > Region/jurisdiction where user data processed by this provider is stored
  > or resides (ISO region/country code, e.g., 'US', 'EU').
- `consent_required`
  > Specifies whether explicit user consent is required for this provider
  > integration per privacy/compliance rules.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of provider record creation.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last record update.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp for soft deletion, or null if active.

### `pol_eco_board_third_party_audit_logs`

Tracks all events, actions, and error responses from external
integrations (e.g., authentication, analytics, anti-spam, notification
providers) for compliance/audit purposes. Each log entry records source
provider, event type, event payload (as JSON/string), timestamp, system
result code, and related correlation information, supporting
troubleshooting, legal hold, and system incident management.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `provider_key`
  > Internal code identifying which external provider generated the event
  > (e.g., 'google', 'analytics', 'anti_spam').
- `event_type`
  > Type or category of event logged (e.g., 'auth_flow_start',
  > 'auth_flow_error', 'api_call', 'token_refresh', 'notification_send',
  > 'fallback').
- `event_payload`
  > Serialized JSON string or encoded payload of the event as received from
  > or sent to the external provider.
- `result_code`
  > Internal result code or error indicator derived from processing the
  > provider event (e.g., 'success', 'failure', 'timeout', 'invalid_token').
- `correlation_id`
  > Optional provider, system, or business correlation/trace ID for boundary
  > tracking across systems (e.g., trace IDs for business audit).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the audit log entry was created.

### `pol_eco_board_analytics_events`

Stores anonymized, structured events transmitted to analytics platforms
(e.g., page view, post creation, vote action, login) for
operational/business intelligence and compliance. Each record supports
audit requirements, regional reporting, and opt-in/out model. Not linked
to user identities to preserve privacy. Data is purged or aggregated as
per retention rules.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `event_type`
  > Business-defined type of analytics event (e.g., 'page_view', 'login',
  > 'vote', 'moderation_action').
- `session_anon_id`
  > Anonymized session identifier (non-PII, no user linkage), used for
  > statistical correlation of analytics events by session or cohort.
- `user_role`
  > User role associated with the event (e.g., 'guest', 'member',
  > 'moderator', 'admin'). Used for business segmentation.
- `event_details`
  > JSON-encoded details or metadata specific to the analytics event (e.g.,
  > category, target_id, feature usage); varies by event_type.
- `region`
  > Region or jurisdiction associated with the event/session (data residency,
  > reporting compliance; ISO country/region code).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the analytics event was generated.

### `pol_eco_board_anti_spam_events`

Captures event records for all interactions with anti-spam/abuse
prevention integrations (inbound or outbound events). Stores provider,
operation, content hash, action outcome, score, and related metadata for
audit and investigation, supporting appeals, escalations, and incident
reviews. Does not store original user content (use hash/fingerprint
only).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `provider_key`
  > Unique internal code or key for the integrated anti-spam provider (e.g.,
  > 'akismet', 'custom_1').
- `operation`
  > Business or technical operation performed (e.g., 'content_submit',
  > 'abuse_check', 'appeal', 'score_retrieval').
- `content_hash`
  > Hash or digital fingerprint of content analyzed (never stores raw user
  > content; only hashed to protect privacy).
- `score`
  > Numeric risk or abuse probability score output from the provider (e.g.,
  > 0.00 to 1.00; higher is more risky).
- `action_taken`
  > Result of anti-spam event or system action (e.g., 'approved', 'blocked',
  > 'escalated', 'queued', 'error').
- `appeal_requested`
  > Indicates if appeal process (user- or moderator-initiated) was requested
  > for this event.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when anti-spam event was recorded.

### `pol_eco_board_consent_statuses`

Stores all explicit consent and opt-in/out statuses by provider, data
region, and integration use, supporting regulatory compliance for user
and session privacy. Tracks what was consented to, for which provider, by
which region/session/date, and manages enforcement of business/legal data
flows. No PII is stored (refer to session/user separately in other
domains for linkage).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `provider_key`
  > The unique key or code for the provider or integration to which consent
  > applies (e.g., 'analytics', 'auth', 'notification').
- `region`
  > Jurisdiction or regional code relevant to the consent (for data residency
  > and privacy enforcement, ISO format).
- `consent_type`
  > Type of consent (e.g., 'analytics', 'email_marketing', 'third_party',
  > 'profiling').
- `consent_status`
  > Status of the consent. Valid values: 'opt_in', 'opt_out', 'revoked',
  > 'pending'.
- `session_anon_id`
  > Anonymized session or cohort identifier related to this consent record
  > (no PII/user identity stored).
- `audit_trail`
  > JSON-encoded object/log with consent action metadata (e.g., time, source,
  > device, evidence), for compliance audit. No PII included.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the consent status was recorded.

### `pol_eco_board_notification_providers`

Catalogs all external notification providers (e.g., SendGrid, Twilio
Email, SMTP, SMS) integrated with the service. Each record defines
supported channels, endpoint URIs, operational status, provider region,
configuration metadata (non-secret), and business flags for
routing/fallback logic. Used for compliance transparency and operational
provider switching.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `provider_name`
  > Human-readable name of the notification provider (e.g., 'SendGrid',
  > 'Twilio').
- `provider_key`
  > Unique internal key/code representing notification integration (e.g.,
  > 'sendgrid', 'twilio_sms').
- `channels_supported`
  > Comma-separated string of notification channels supported by this
  > provider (e.g., 'email,sms,push').
- `endpoint_uri`
  > Integration endpoint URI for provider's main API/service (primary
  > endpoint, not credential/secret).
- `region`
  > Provider's service or business region, for data residency and routing
  > (ISO country/region code).
- `status`
  > Current operational status of the provider: 'active', 'inactive', or
  > 'maintenance'.
- `config_metadata`
  > JSON-encoded key/value mapping of non-secret configuration and
  > operational metadata (supported features, documentation links, etc.).
- `created_at`: Timestamp of provider record creation.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last provider config update.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp for soft deletion, or null if active.

### `pol_eco_board_operational_logs`

Centralized log of all system operations, events, and service activities
for the polEcoBoard platform. Captures timestamped records of API calls,
backend jobs, system notifications, performance events, and other
significant operational actions for audit and monitoring. Provides a
historical record to support incident investigation, compliance
verification, and operational analytics.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `log_level`
  > Severity or categorization of the operational event (e.g., INFO, WARNING,
  > ERROR, CRITICAL). Used for triaging and dashboard filtering.
- `logged_at`: Timestamp when the operational log entry was recorded.
- `message`
  > Human-readable description or summary of the operational event. Designed
  > for audit readability and system monitoring dashboards.
- `context`
  > Structured or serialized metadata providing extra context for the
  > operational event (e.g., job type, subsystem, trace ID, related resource
  > identifiers).
- `actor_id`
  > Optional reference to the involved admin, moderator, or automated system
  > actor. May be null if operation is system-initiated or anonymous.
- `event_code`
  > Internal code or short identifier for the event type, supporting analytic
  > and automation use-cases (e.g. 'SIGN_IN', 'BACKUP_START',
  > 'MAINTENANCE_NOTICE').
- `created_at`
  > Log record creation timestamp (for soft-deletion and audit lifecycle
  > control).
- `updated_at`: Log record last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp; null if log is active.

### `pol_eco_board_audit_trails`

Immutable, write-once audit trail storing high-sensitivity business and
system change records required for compliance reviews, security
monitoring, and regulatory audits. Includes detailed context for all
critical actions (e.g., config changes, access grants/revocations, data
retention actions, incident resolutions).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `action_type`
  > Type of audited action (e.g., CONFIG_CHANGE, ROLE_ASSIGN, DATA_ERASURE,
  > INCIDENT_RESOLVE).
- `performed_by_id`: ID of admin or privileged actor responsible for the action.
- `target_resource`
  > Unique or composite identifier of the resource subject to the action
  > (could be user id, config id, or resource URI).
- `audit_context`
  > Structured or serialized details about action, pre/post state, or
  > business justification.
- `recorded_at`: Timestamp when the audit trail entry was written (immutable once set).
- `created_at`
  > Audit entry creation timestamp (redundant for retention lifecycle and
  > index support).
- `updated_at`
  > Audit entry last update timestamp (in principle, should not change except
  > for retention lifecycle metadata changes).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp; null means audit entry is live and protected
  > from purge.

### `pol_eco_board_incidents`

Service incident management and business-impact event log for
polEcoBoard. Stores all critical or sustained operational incident
reports, including outages, degraded services, compliance issues, data
breaches, and legal events. Records allow for lifecycle tracking,
business review, and regulatory reporting.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `incident_code`
  > Unique, short string code for the business or operational incident (e.g.,
  > OUTAGE_2024_05, GDPR_BREACH_001).
- `category`
  > Classification of the incident (e.g., OUTAGE, BREACH, COMPLIANCE, LEGAL,
  > MAINTENANCE). Used for admin filtering and regulatory response.
- `status`
  > Current business status of the incident (e.g., OPEN, RESOLVED, ESCALATED,
  > UNDER_REVIEW, CLOSED).
- `description`: Summary of what happened, business impact, and affected services/users.
- `detected_at`
  > Timestamp when the incident was first detected (may be earlier than
  > creation for retroactive records).
- `resolved_at`
  > When the incident was resolved or marked as closed; null for
  > ongoing/outstanding incidents.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp for audit and operational lifecycle management.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp; null if still primary record.

### `pol_eco_board_maintenance_windows`

Scheduled and historical system maintenance windows, covering downtimes,
upgrades, migrations, and other planned/unplanned service interruptions.
Supports platform status dashboards, incident correlation, and regulatory
notifications. Used for compliance tracking and SLA verification.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `window_code`
  > Unique identifier for the maintenance window event (e.g., MAINT_2025Q1,
  > HOTFIX_20240615).
- `start_time`: Scheduled or actual maintenance window start timestamp.
- `end_time`
  > Scheduled or actual maintenance window end timestamp; null if still
  > ongoing or if unplanned duration.
- `expected_impact`
  > Human-readable summary of expected service impact; for admin and
  > compliance dashboarding.
- `actual_impact`: Recorded impact as determined post-event.
- `notified_at`
  > Time when admins/moderators were notified of the scheduled/unscheduled
  > maintenance event.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp, null if still in operational window history.

### `pol_eco_board_service_metrics`

Aggregated, time-bucketed service-level metrics supporting operational
dashboards, business KPI tracking, and SLA verification for polEcoBoard.
Metrics include post/comment/vote counts, user activity, moderation
actions, response times, operational error frequencies, and
retention/purge statistics. Only computed via backend aggregation; no
denormalized materialized view pattern needed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `metric_code`
  > Short string code identifying metric type (e.g., POST_COUNT,
  > COMMENT_COUNT, VOTE_VOLUME, API_LATENCY, INCIDENT_COUNT, PURGE_VOLUME).
- `metric_window_start`: Start of the aggregation time window (e.g., hour, day, week).
- `metric_window_end`: End of the aggregation window (exclusive).
- `value_int`
  > Integer-valued metric (e.g., count of events, users, incidents in the
  > window).
- `value_double`
  > Floating-point metric (e.g., average latency, percent completion, ratio).
  > Only one of value_int or value_double typically used per metric by code
  > convention.
- `notes`
  > Optional business note or free-form annotation to explain anomalies or
  > correlate business events with metric deviations.
- `created_at`: Timestamp for when the metric aggregation entry was created.
- `updated_at`
  > Last time metric was updated (e.g., for amended calculations or corrected
  > data).
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp, for retention/purge control. Null if active.

### `pol_eco_board_business_reports`

Business event report entry for admin dashboards, export/audit actions,
scheduled metrics, regulatory filings, or compliance reviews. Covers both
automatically and manually triggered reports, their configuration,
delivery status, and role in audit trail. Enables tracking, lifecycle
management, and historical analysis of all formal business report
objects.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `report_code`
  > Short string code or business key identifying the report (e.g.,
  > WEEKLY_METRICS_20240810, INCIDENT_EXPORT_20250515).
- `report_type`
  > Business categorization of the report (e.g., METRICS, AUDIT, INCIDENTS,
  > EXPORT, SLA, LEGAL, COMPLIANCE).
- `status`
  > Report status in the report lifecycle (e.g., PENDING, COMPLETED, FAILED,
  > DELIVERED).
- `requested_by_id`
  > Admin or system service account that initiated the business report
  > request or generation.
- `content_uri`
  > Location or reference (e.g., S3 URI) of the generated report document or
  > export file.
- `triggered_at`: Timestamp when the report generation/export was started.
- `delivered_at`
  > Timestamp when report was delivered or made available for download; null
  > for pending reports.
- `failure_reason`
  > If the report failed to complete or deliver, this provides the reason or
  > error context.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp on report object creation (for lifecycle and retention
  > tracking).
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp (for report lifecycle changes).
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp; null if report record is active.

operations.specification:
Retrieve a specific comment by its unique identifier belonging to a post. This operation consults the pol_eco_board_comments table, using the composite key of postId and commentId, which refers respectively to the parent post and the specific comment. Only comments not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null) are returned. The query delivers the full comment details including body, author_member_id, post_id, parent_comment_id, flagged status, created and updated timestamps, and other audit-related metadata.

Access is allowed for all roles above guest, as commenting is a core feature for members and higher. Guests can view only comments tied to public posts; members, moderators, and admins can view all comments for posts within their accessible boards and categories. Permission checks are layered by role based on the parent post access and category membership.

Security: Paths and identifiers are validated to be UUIDs. If the parent post is locked or archived, additional checks on comment accessibility apply. Comments that are flagged or moderated retain audit visibility for moderator/admin.

Related APIs: This endpoint is typically used after listing comments for a post (comments index endpoint) or after following a notification of a reply to the user. For moderation/audit, this data may be cross-referenced in report or sanction flows.
operations.description:
Retrieve the full details of a specific comment on a post using its unique identifier. The operation leverages the pol_eco_board_comments table, where each comment record contains authoring information (author_member_id), content (body), creation and update temporal fields, and moderation metadata such as flagged status and deleted_at for soft deletes.

Permission depends on role:
- Guest users may view comments only if the parent post is public and the comment is active (not soft deleted or flagged for abuse).
- Members and higher roles (moderators, admins) may access all comments on any visible or assigned content, including those flagged or deleted (subject to audit log access).

Each returned comment provides direct linkage for further business operations, such as editing (put), deletion (delete), or report/submission for moderation. Comments flagged or deleted are annotated accordingly in the API response, ensuring transparency and auditability.

If a comment is not found, deleted, or inaccessible due to business rules (locked post/category, sanction, or restricted membership), an appropriate business error is returned. Strong audit and error-handling mechanisms are employed to detect unauthorized or invalid parameter usage.

parameters.description: Unique identifier for the parent post containing the comment.

parameters.name: commentId
parameters.description: Unique identifier for the target comment under the given post.

responseBody.description: Full details of the comment including content, metadata, and audit state.

operations.specification:
Create a new comment under a specific post. This operation inserts a record into the pol_eco_board_comments table, using postId to associate the parent post. The request must include authoring member (authenticated from session), body (validated by business rules for length and prohibited content), and an optional parent_comment_id for reply comments. Enforces business logic: comment length, rate limiting, and prohibited expressions as outlined in participation rules. Parent post and authoring member must exist and be active. 

All submissions are automatically flagged for moderation if business logic is triggered (e.g., excessive rate, potential abusive content). The response includes the created comment or detailed error reasons for failed validation.

Related: Used after fetching post details and for participatory flows such as comment chains and reply notifications. Authenticates through member, moderator, or admin role.
operations.description:
Create a new comment under a given post. The handler checks postId validity and that the post is active and within a visible/accessible board/category. The request body contains the new comment's text (body, validated for length/content per IPolEcoBoardComment.ICreate schema), and an optional parent_comment_id to indicate replying to another comment (if supported). The persistent record includes creation and update timestamps and initial flagged status per content policy.

Authorship is recorded with the active member from the session/JWT. Guests cannot comment and attempting to do so causes an explicit business error and prompt to log in or register. All successful comments are immediately available for audit, moderation, and display (unless flagged by automatic business logic).

If the parent post is locked/archived or author is sanctioned, comment creation is blocked and a detailed error is returned. Comments may be further managed via update or delete endpoints.

The device_fingerprint is optional and supports improved unique visitor tracking where it is available. When called, this endpoint logs or refreshes a guest record for the current IP/device and returns a secure guest session object for analytics and abuse monitoring. There are no authentication headers required, and no posting/voting permissions are established. This operation aligns with business rules in the requirements documentation regarding guest to member flows, analytics event tracking, and consent status management for cookies/privacy law compliance.

operations.specification: Implements registration for the member role, allowing unregistered individuals to create a new member account in the polEcoBoard system. Registration requires providing a unique, verified email and password (password_hash), which are stored securely in the pol_eco_board_members table. The API issues initial JWT tokens and sets up authentication sessions (see pol_eco_board_auth_sessions) for the user. The process ensures all input validation rules from the schema are enforced, including email uniqueness and password strength. Upon successful registration, a session is created with associated tokens stored in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions; feedback is provided with an 'Authorization' header in response. The operation is essential for onboarding and enables subsequent login, posting, and participation across all board functionalities.
operations.description: This operation registers a new member using their email and password and creates corresponding records in both the pol_eco_board_members (for user info) and pol_eco_board_auth_sessions (for login session/tokens). Password is securely hashed. Email must be unique (the uniqueness constraint is enforced via a unique index on the email field in pol_eco_board_members). No additional personal information is required at registration, but the member's is_active flag defaults to true upon successful creation. Tokens are stored in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions for future validation and token refresh. If registration is successful, the response contains setHeaders with the issued JWT Authorization value for immediate authenticated usage. Error handling includes duplicate email rejection and validation on password complexity according to system policy. This is the only mechanism to create a new member account and must be called before any member login or session.
operations.summary: Register new member (pol_eco_board_members) and issue login JWT (Auth Session).

responseBody.description: Headers containing JWT Authorization issued after successful registration.

On successful authentication, generates and returns new JWT access/refresh tokens, creates a new session record in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions, and enforces all business logic for secure credential verification and session creation. The operation ensures members are only authenticated if the is_active flag is true and that the supplied password matches the stored password_hash. Implements all security rules and logs login attempts for audit and compliance purposes.
operations.description: This endpoint handles login for previously registered members, validating credentials against the pol_eco_board_members table (matching the unique email and hashed password). On success, creates a new auth session in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions, issues signed JWT tokens, and marks the last_login_at timestamp for audit. Login fails if the member is not active (is_active=false), banned, or if credentials are incorrect. Login actions are recorded for compliance. No sensitive data is returned; only tokens required for session management.

This operation enforces immediate invalidation of authorization credentials and is a critical security measure to prevent unauthorized continued access. No request body is necessary as the current session is derived from authentication context.
operations.description: This endpoint removes the authentication and token validity for the currently logged-in user's session in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions (identified via JWT/auth header). When called, the revoked_at timestamp for the corresponding session is set, banning further use of the issued tokens. This ensures session security and immediate logout effect. This operation is only available to authenticated users with the member role as determined by their JWT.

Does not issue new tokens or create new session records, but confirms validity and status of current credentials.

This operation helps maintain user session continuity and allows clients to test their authentication state. It is important for single-device or token-based transitions (such as client refreshes, SPA reloads, or verifying token integrity). This ensures maximum account security in accordance with user-initiated password change requests.
operations.description: Enables authenticated members to securely update their account password after submitting the current password for validation, following all secure practices and system password complexity requirements. The operation follows strict security control (revocation and validation of refresh_token hash). Business and audit rules from system specification apply. Errors arise from invalidated, expired, or compromised tokens, or member account status change.

The operation ensures that refreshes are only performed for non-revoked, valid sessions and actively enforces account eligibility and audit compliance. Designed as a backend-for-backend (not public) operation. The result includes setHeaders for client assignment. operations.specification: This operation registers a new moderator account in the polEcoBoard system. It creates a new record in the pol_eco_board_members table (for account identity, password, and email), and immediately creates a corresponding record in pol_eco_board_moderators to grant moderator rights. The registration requires a unique email, a secure password, consent status, and a display name. Account creation is only permitted if registration is enabled in pol_eco_board_service_settings. Upon successful creation, the system returns moderator account info and issues JWT tokens for immediate use; a setHeaders property in the response allows the client to apply an Authorization header for authenticated requests. The response does not include the raw password or secrets. If email already exists, rejects with a business error. Coordination between members and moderators ensures full traceability and audit. No invitation workflow is needed for moderators—all qualifying users must follow explicit registration, consent, and activation rules. No soft delete on creation; account is active upon successful onboarding.
operations.description:
This registration endpoint for moderator accounts supports secure, auditable onboarding to the polEcoBoard moderation staff. It references the pol_eco_board_members table for account identity (email, password_hash, consent_status, display_name) and immediately creates a subordinate pol_eco_board_moderators record linking the member to moderator privileges. All registration activity is governed by the polEcoBoard business rules: email and display_name must be unique, password_hash is securely stored (never plaintext), and consent_status must be present reflecting privacy law or platform policy.

JWT access and refresh tokens are issued on successful registration, using the account records in pol_eco_board_members and pol_eco_board_auth_sessions; response includes the setHeaders object with an Authorization bearer token, satisfying the high-security requirements for moderator onboarding. Moderators require traceable identity—anonymous or pseudonymous moderators are not permitted under audit requirements.

Integration is tightly coupled with current values in pol_eco_board_service_settings (registration_enabled); no new moderator can be registered if system-wide registration is disabled. Validation rules (email format, password strength, uniqueness) are enforced at the business logic layer with precise error handling for conflicts. 

Security context: registration is public but rate-limited for abuse prevention. All registration actions (success/failure) are logged in pol_eco_board_account_audits for compliance. Related operations include moderator signIn (for login), signOut (for logout), and changePassword (for security management). All issuance of JWT tokens after registration supports immediate access to moderator operations.

This flow integrates into the polEcoBoard authentication workflow as the entry-point for moderator capabilities. Errors (duplicate email, weak password, system policy limits) are returned in business format; no raw system exceptions or sensitive context are exposed.

operations.specification: This operation authenticates an existing moderator account and issues new JWT tokens for access. It checks credentials against the pol_eco_board_members email and password_hash fields, and confirms the account exists in pol_eco_board_moderators with is_active true. The endpoint is public (no prior auth needed) and on success returns an authorization JWT (and refresh token as per session logic) for immediate authenticated use. If credentials fail or account is not a currently active moderator, returns a business error. Login is audited for security and traceability.
operations.description:
This login endpoint enables moderators to securely authenticate using their registered email and password. It queries pol_eco_board_members for the account, confirms the password_hash matches, and ensures a pol_eco_board_moderators record exists and is is_active. On successful login, the operation issues JWT tokens according to polEcoBoard requirements (role, userId, session-token-id, permissions). No unverified or suspended accounts are permitted login.

Login and session issuance are logged in pol_eco_board_account_audits for security and compliance. Rate limiting is enforced for repeated failed attempts. The operation strictly follows privacy and security standards—no sensitive details are leaked on login failure, and all JWT payloads contain only required role and session info. This operation integrates with session tracking in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions for all login events.
operations.summary: Moderator login endpoint using email and password, returning JWT tokens upon success (pol_eco_board_members, pol_eco_board_moderators, pol_eco_board_auth_sessions).

requestBody.description: Moderator login credentials: email, password.

responseBody.description: Moderator login response, including JWT for Authorization if successful.

operations.name: signIn

operations.specification: Signs out the currently authenticated moderator, invalidates the active JWT session, and terminates the current record in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions for the session. Requires Authorization (JWT) of type moderator. This operation does not take a request body and only supports authenticated sign-out. Security logic assures session invalidation is immediate and full audit is updated. The account remains active and may re-sign-in. No impact to other active sessions.
operations.description: This operation securely logs out the moderator from the application by invalidating their current JWT token and associated auth session found in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions. Only accessible with a valid moderator Authorization header (JWT). Upon sign-out, the current pol_eco_board_auth_sessions record is updated with a revoke timestamp and all related audit trails are updated for compliance. This operation does not affect sessions on other devices. The system guarantees immediate removal of session access upon successful completion. No personal or credential IDs are returned. This endpoint is part of the session management flow for moderator accounts and integrates with security event logging in pol_eco_board_account_audits.
operations.summary: Log out the currently authenticated moderator and revoke the current JWT session (pol_eco_board_auth_sessions).

responseBody.description: Successful moderator logout confirmation. No sensitive details are returned.

operations.name: signOut

operations.specification: Verifies the validity and active status of a moderator's JWT token or Authorization header. Accepts an access token and checks signature, expiry, and that the moderator account (pol_eco_board_members/pol_eco_board_moderators) and corresponding JWT session are still valid and not revoked. Supports both pre-flight token validation and in-session security verification. Does not require authentication to call but validates provided JWT for business logic. On valid JWT, returns authentication context for the moderator role, otherwise returns error. Used by clients to check session expiry/validity (or for SSO/E2E flows).
operations.description: This operation enables client-side and backend verification of a JWT token or Authorization header intending to authenticate as a moderator. It decodes, verifies signature/expiry, and looks up the corresponding session in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions, validating that the member is still an active moderator. It does not require an authenticated session to call but expects a JWT (usually via header or payload). If successful, provides details about the authenticated context; otherwise, returns an unauthenticated result with an explanatory message. Works as part of token lifecycle management and may be used by proxies or SSO layers to check moderator authentication/validity before sensitive actions. No confidential credentials or secrets are exposed at any point. Full validation and audit chain are enforced for compliance.
operations.summary: Check validity of a given moderator JWT or token for authentication status (pol_eco_board_auth_sessions, pol_eco_board_members, pol_eco_board_moderators).

requestBody.description: Moderator JWT token or Authorization value to validate.

responseBody.description: Moderator token validation result, includes authentication context info or error.

operations.name: validateToken

operations.specification: Allows a logged-in moderator to change their password by supplying current password and a new password. Updates password_hash in pol_eco_board_members, forces invalidation of all active auth sessions for that member (pol_eco_board_auth_sessions are revoked). Requires moderator Authorization and is only available to currently authenticated, active moderators. Enforces all password policy rules (length, complexity match). Triggers business audit and updates account audit/compliance tables. No password hash or sensitive secrets are ever returned in response.
operations.description: This operation enables a moderator to change their account password using the current password for verification and a new desired password. It fetches the currently authenticated moderator's credentials (via JWT and pol_eco_board_members/pol_eco_board_moderators), validates the current password, and updates the password_hash with the new value on success. All auth sessions (pol_eco_board_auth_sessions) for this member are then revoked (including other devices/sessions), following business security policy. A business audit trail is added in pol_eco_board_account_audits. On success, no sensitive details or identifiers are returned. Password complexity and rotation policies are enforced as per polEcoBoard requirements.
operations.summary: Moderator password change endpoint. Requires old and new password; revokes all sessions on change (pol_eco_board_members, pol_eco_board_auth_sessions).

requestBody.description: Payload including current password and new password for moderator account.

responseBody.description: Moderator password change result. No account identities or secrets returned.

operations.name: changePassword

operations.specification: This endpoint enables JWT refresh for a moderator using a valid refresh token. The session is checked in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions for validity, not revoked, and matching the moderator's account (including is_active checks). If valid, new JWT access and refresh tokens are issued and the setHeaders property is returned in the response for client-side Authorization header assignment. The refresh logic updates issued_at, expires_at, and rotates session identifiers for improved security. Refresh tokens are securely hashed and stored; never returned raw in any response. This operation supports the sliding-session model and audits all token issuances in pol_eco_board_account_audits. Fails with a business error on invalid/expired/revoked tokens.
operations.description: This refresh token endpoint is available to moderators with a valid, unexpired refresh token created via previous authentication (see pol_eco_board_auth_sessions for session logic). The endpoint checks the refresh_token against existing sessions, validates that the member and moderator records are active, and, if valid, issues a new JWT access/refresh pair with setHeaders for Authorization. On failure (invalid or revoked refresh token), a business error is returned without exposing session or credential details. Token refreshes are logged in audit tables (pol_eco_board_account_audits) for compliance. Security: raw tokens are not leaked; token rotation is enforced on each use. Sliding-session and business rules are as per platform policy; session audit and revocation support prompt incident response. Related operations: signIn, signOut, and changePassword, which all update session state. Integrates into the full authentication workflow for moderator accounts.
operations.summary: Moderator JWT refresh endpoint: checks refresh_token, issues new tokens and setHeaders (pol_eco_board_auth_sessions, pol_eco_board_members, pol_eco_board_moderators).

requestBody.description: Moderator refresh token payload for JWT renewal process.

responseBody.description: New JWT (access/refresh) and setHeaders for moderator Authorization.

operations.name: refreshToken

operations.specification: Core JWT-based admin authentication/authorization. Required for 'admin' to access any protected resource. Tied to pol_eco_board_admins, pol_eco_board_members, and pol_eco_board_auth_sessions tables. Requires email (unique), password (hashed in 'password_hash') and sets up access/refresh tokens using session management table. Issues 'setHeaders' for Authorization header after registration. No admin-specific onboarding, but base member record must already exist or be created as part of workflow. Ensures all platform security principles for sensitive role.
operations.description: This endpoint allows a new admin account to be registered into the system. It requires unique email and password, which are validated and securely stored. Records are inserted both into the pol_eco_board_members (as a baseline account) and pol_eco_board_admins (for admin privileges). On completion, a JWT access token and refresh token are issued and a session is recorded in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions, with 'setHeaders' containing the new Authorization token for streamlined SDK/connection. All credential storage uses strong hashing per schema; error handling includes duplicate email, password weakness, or disabled registration in platform settings (refer pol_eco_board_service_settings). This operation creates the security root for all administrator actions and is only enabled if registration is allowed in service settings. It forms the main entry-point for system administrator onboarding and is required for any further admin or global management operations.
operations.summary: Register a new admin account (pol_eco_board_admins, pol_eco_board_members).

requestBody.description: Registration details for new admin, including email and password.

responseBody.description: Admin registration result, including JWT tokens and Authorization headers for subsequent SDK calls.

operations.name: signUp

operations.specification: JWT-based admin login endpoint. Validates credentials (email, password) against pol_eco_board_members (checks status, is_active, deleted_at) and pol_eco_board_admins (ensures admin privilege and is_active). On valid authentication, issues JWT access and refresh tokens and creates new pol_eco_board_auth_sessions record. Tokens in response; does not require prior registration validation as endpoint checks all data at login time. Handles all error states: invalid credentials, deactivated/banned, admin role revoked, etc. strictly via schema tables.
operations.description: This API logs in an existing admin user using validated email and password. Auth is checked against the member and admin tables (pol_eco_board_members, pol_eco_board_admins). If the user is active and has current admin privileges, their password_hash is checked and, on success, a new session is written to pol_eco_board_auth_sessions. JWT access and refresh tokens are returned for secure subsequent access. Accounts that are banned, deleted, or whose admin status is revoked will be rejected with a clear error. This endpoint is essential for all privileged system management and monitoring actions. No partial success is possible: both credential and status/role checks must pass.
operations.summary: Authenticate an admin and issue JWT for session (pol_eco_board_admins, pol_eco_board_members).

requestBody.description: Login credentials (email, password) for admin authentication.

responseBody.description: Admin login session and tokens for follow-up authorized requests.

operations.name: signIn

operations.specification: Admin logout (JWT/session invalidate) endpoint. Revokes the current admin user's active session, updating pol_eco_board_auth_sessions (by session id or token hash lookup) and ensuring subsequent actions require new authentication. Implements proper session termination flow as required by audit/tracking. Must be called with valid Authorization (JWT) identifying admin. This operation ensures global session hygiene and is crucial for secure device management and platform compliance.
operations.description: Allows a currently authenticated admin to log out by invalidating their current auth session token in the pol_eco_board_auth_sessions table. Session is identified using token hash or session id (presented via Authorization header). After processing, the session is marked revoked_at with a timestamp and no further actions are permitted with this token. Essential for security of all admin-level business: session revocation is required on role changes, password reset, or device deprovision. The endpoint is protected by admin-level JWT authentication and forms part of the mandatory audit/compliance flows.
operations.summary: Logout endpoint for admin, revoking current JWT session (pol_eco_board_auth_sessions).

responseBody.description: Logout confirmation and session status.

operations.name: signOut

operations.specification: Validate an admin JWT token for session continuation or client state check without requiring a protected operation. Accepts (possibly expired) token, verifies JWT structure, signature, expiry, and validity by cross-checking against pol_eco_board_auth_sessions, pol_eco_board_admins, and pol_eco_board_members. Used for client-side persistent login checks or SDK/connection re-establishment. No sensitive data is returned—only authenticated status, identity, and expiry/permissions info.
operations.description: Checks whether the supplied JWT access token is valid and the admin session is still authorized and active. Evaluates membership and admin privileges, session status (from pol_eco_board_auth_sessions), expiry, and revocation state. Used for client/SDK token renewal decisions or to power 'keep me signed in' UI patterns. Token is verified both for cryptographic signature and with live status in sessions table. Distinct from refresh/token issue (which requires refresh endpoint). Failure cases result in clear non-authenticated status.
operations.summary: Validate admin JWT token for session/auth status (pol_eco_board_admins, pol_eco_board_auth_sessions).

requestBody.description: Token to validate, usually in Authorization header.

responseBody.description: Token validity status, admin/user identity, expiry and permissions info.

operations.name: validateToken

operations.specification: Enables an authenticated admin to securely change the account password. Expected to require the current admin JWT plus a request body providing both the old password and new password, which must be business-validated and stored as a hash in pol_eco_board_members.password_hash. Also terminates (revokes_at) all existing pol_eco_board_auth_sessions for the admin to require complete re-authentication, enforcing strict security. Written to audit/account audit tables for compliance.
operations.description: This endpoint updates the admin's password after verifying the current one matches the stored hash in pol_eco_board_members. The new password is validated for business strength and updated securely (hashed, salted). On completion, all existing authentication sessions for the admin's member_id are revoked in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions (revoked_at). The operation is journaled in pol_eco_board_account_audits with type/password_change, satisfying all audit and compliance rules. Only logged-in admins may change their own passwords, and regular password rotation is expected for best practices. Any errors (incorrect old password, business validation) are communicated specifically. Partial updates are disallowed.
operations.summary: Change admin password, revoke existing sessions (pol_eco_board_members, pol_eco_board_auth_sessions).

requestBody.description: Current password and new password for admin update flow.

responseBody.description: Password update operation result and re-authentication requirement notice.

operations.name: changePassword

operations.specification: JWT refresh operation, conditional on storage of refresh_token in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions. Accepts valid (not expired or revoked) refresh token (usually from a secure httpOnly cookie or client SDK). On success, issues new access and refresh JWTs, updates session record, and returns 'setHeaders' for new Authorization value. Decouples session lifecycle from regular access token rotation, as required for long-lived admin/client sessions. Handles all error states, including revocation and expiry, with complete cross-table (pol_eco_board_auth_sessions) check.
operations.description: Allows an admin to obtain new JWT access and refresh tokens by submitting a valid refresh token. The endpoint locates the relevant session in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions, ensures the session has not been revoked/expired, and issues new tokens. Updates refresh_token field for session and responds with new 'setHeaders' structure encapsulating updated Authorization value for performant SDK use. Failure or tampering invalidates the session and requires full login. This supports enterprise session management patterns in admin UIs and service integration.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT for admin (secure rotation, session update, pol_eco_board_auth_sessions).

requestBody.description: Input refresh token for session renewal (pol_eco_board_auth_sessions.refresh_token used).

responseBody.description: New JWT tokens, session state and updated 'setHeaders' for Authorization header.

operations.name: refreshToken

operations.specification: List all active sessions for current admin (token/session management). Loads all unrevoked, unexpired records from pol_eco_board_auth_sessions for the given member_id linked to this admin. Allows global view of devices, IPs, times, and devices using session. Enables enterprise-level admin session hygiene, security, and audit. Must be filtered/paged for large installations. Does not allow modifying sessions (use revoke endpoints).
operations.description: Returns all active authentication sessions currently held by this admin user. Loads via member_id (from JWT) and returns a page of pol_eco_board_auth_sessions records where revoked_at is NULL and expires_at is in the future. Result includes times, ip addresses, device fingerprints, provider info, and session metadata. Used for admin self-management, device awareness, and security posture review. Only current admin may list their own sessions. For operations on other users, super-admin or different endpoints are required.
operations.summary: Enumerate current admin's active sessions (pol_eco_board_auth_sessions by member_id).

responseBody.description: Page of session state records for this admin, with security metadata.

operations.name: listActiveSessions

operations.specification: Revoke (terminate) a specific active session for this admin based on sessionId. Accessible only to the corresponding logged-in admin, not for global management (use other endpoints for cross-account). Looks up session in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions by provided sessionId (path parameter), validates ownership via member_id, and sets revoked_at, triggering session termination. Used for self-service logout-from-device flows and device hygiene enforcement.
operations.description: This endpoint allows the admin to revoke (log out) a specific session (typically for another device/browser) by providing its sessionId. The API checks that the sessionId exists, belongs to the current admin (via JWT), and is not already revoked/expired. If valid, it marks revoked_at and updates session status instantly, enforcing logout. Useful for admins managing their own cross-device presence and for handling device compromise or maintenance. Fails gracefully if session is not found, not owned, or already revoked. Operations are journaled in audit/service tables for compliance. Non-superusers cannot terminate sessions for other admins through this endpoint.
operations.summary: Revoke a specific session for current admin by sessionId (pol_eco_board_auth_sessions).

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique session record ID to revoke as found in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions.id (UUID).

responseBody.description: Success/failure for session termination, with before/after state.

operations.name: revokeSession

operations.specification: Revoke all active admin authentication sessions for the currently logged-in admin ('logout everywhere'). Scans all pol_eco_board_auth_sessions for this admin's member_id where revoked_at is NULL and sets revoked_at for each (hard log-out on every device). Also used after password changes for compliance. Self-service only (no admin-over-admin session management); super-admin tooling handled elsewhere.
operations.description: Invalidates ALL active authentication sessions (tokens) for the current admin account by setting revoked_at on each pol_eco_board_auth_sessions record for the admin's member_id. Effective for enterprise security or in response to device loss/compromise. After execution, all tokens for admin are rendered invalid, requiring total re-authentication. Can be called at any time by the admin on their own account. The operation is audit-journaled, with full accountability and notification recommended. No effect on other users—strictly self-directed. Used by security UIs for 'logout everywhere' and required after sensitive credential updates.
operations.summary: Logout of all sessions: revoke all admin tokens for own account (pol_eco_board_auth_sessions).

responseBody.description: All-session revocation confirmation with overall session count/status.

Business rules enforce valid transitions and full traceability per policy. Used for account restrictions, compliance audit, and operational lifecycle management.

Scheduled end time of the sanction, or null for indefinite/permanent. Required if a time-limited sanction, null if permanent/unspecified.

end_at.description: Scheduled end time of the sanction, or null for indefinite/permanent. Required if a time-limited sanction, null if permanent/unspecified.
