IMemberAuthenticationMemberValidateToken.description: Result of token validation. If valid, may include user info and expiry/role; otherwise nulls/false.

current_password.description: The member's current password for verification; required.

new_password.description: The desired new password; must meet complexity/length/etc policy.

IMemberAuthenticationMemberChangePasswor.description: Payload used by authenticated members to change their password. Requires current password and new password for full verification (per business/security requirements).

success.description: Indicates whether the password change operation was completed successfully. True if password was updated and all sessions revoked; false if operation failed due to incorrect old password, account state, or validation error.

message.description: Human-readable message explaining the outcome of the password change request. On success, summarizes session revocation and required re-login. On failure, provides actionable error (e.g., 'Incorrect current password', 'Password does not meet strength policy').

sessionsRevoked.description: Number of authentication sessions that were revoked as a result of the password change, typically >= 1 (including all device/browser sessions for this account).

reloginRequired.description: Returns true if the member must re-log-in to continue using the service (all sessions have been revoked).

timestamp.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601) when the password change operation was completed.

IMemberAuthenticationMemberChangePasswor.description: Password change result object for members. Indicates outcome, explanatory message, count of sessions revoked, and whether re-login is now mandatory. Used after password updates for audit and user feedback.

refreshToken.description: Refresh token (JWT or securely generated opaque value) issued at authentication and used to obtain new access tokens. Must be valid, non-expired, and match a session record for this member.

IMemberAuthenticationMemberRefreshToken.description: Request body for refreshing a member's authentication token/session. Contains the refresh token to validate and exchange for new access/refresh tokens.

accessToken.description: Newly generated JWT access token for member authentication. To be used in Authorization header for subsequent API requests.

refreshToken.description: Newly issued refresh token (rotated for security) for future session renewals. Provided for client-side secure storage.

tokenType.description: The OAuth2-compliant token type (always 'Bearer' in this system for API use).

expiresIn.description: Number of seconds until the new access token expires (e.g., 1800 for 30 minutes). Used for token refresh scheduling in clients.

Authorization.description: Header value for 'Authorization', typically in the format 'Bearer <accessToken>', to be set for future authenticated requests.

setHeaders.description: Key-value object containing headers the API consumer should set with the new token (usually Authorization), supporting SDKs and automation.

IMemberAuthenticationMemberRefreshTokenR.description: Result of member refresh token grant. Provides new access/refresh tokens, token type, expiry info, and headers for authenticated client usage.

email.description: Unique email address for new moderator registration. Must be validated and non-empty. Used as login credential and for communications.

password.description: Raw password supplied by registrant (will be hashed and not stored in plaintext). Must meet platform complexity and length requirements. Not returned in outputs.

display_name.description: Public display name (unique within platform, usually 2–30 chars) for the moderator. Used in UI, moderation logs, and public actions.

consent_status.description: Business/consent flag indicating privacy policy and terms acceptance for account creation. Must reflect current required consent string or version.

IPolEcoBoardModeratorRegistration.ICreat.description: Request to create/register a new moderator account. All required onboarding properties for moderation role registration. Password is input only (never output).

moderatorId.description: The UUID assigned to the newly created moderator account (usually matches the member record ID).

email.description: Moderator's unique email address (used for login and notifications).

display_name.description: Moderator's public display name for UI and audit.

Authorization.description: Header value for 'Authorization', e.g., 'Bearer <JWT>', for subsequent authenticated access post-registration.

setHeaders.description: Key-value object for headers to set after registration, with the JWT Bearer Authorization.

IPolEcoBoardModeratorRegistration.IRespo.description: Response after successful moderator registration. Contains moderator unique ID, identity fields, and Authorization header for immediate authenticated use. No secrets or passwords are returned.

email.description: Registered email address for moderator login. Must correspond to an existing, active moderator account.

password.description: The login credential (cleartext password for login; will be verified then discarded). Must match stored hash for account.

IPolEcoBoardModeratorAuthentication.ICre.description: Moderator login request: input email and password for credential verification and session issue. No outputs return password or raw hashes.

moderatorId.description: UUID for the authenticated moderator account.

email.description: Moderator's login email, returned for confirmation.

display_name.description: Moderator's display name, returned for session context and UI.

Authorization.description: Header to set for 'Authorization': 'Bearer <token>'. For immediate authentication post-login.

setHeaders.description: Header object: Authorization, for client-side usage with issued Bearer token.

IPolEcoBoardModeratorAuthentication.IRes.description: Moderator login response: basic identity confirmation and JWT Authorization header for authenticated session. Tokens are not returned raw; client sets the header from setHeaders.

success.description: True if logout operation completed successfully (session revoked and user signed out); false if already logged out or session was not valid.

message.description: Descriptive message explaining the logout outcome: successful sign out, session already revoked, or other info.

IPolEcoBoardModeratorSignOut.IResponse.description: Response from moderator sign-out operation. Indicates if logout/revocation was successful and provides explanatory text. Used for feedback on logout events in web/mobile interfaces.

token.description: JWT token string or value from Authorization header to validate. May be expired, revoked, or active. Used to verify the authenticity and status of a moderator or member session.

IJwtToken.IRequest.description: Request wrapper for JWT token validation. Accepts the token string to check for session, expiry, and privilege info.

isValid.description: Indicates if token is currently valid (true) or invalid/expired/revoked (false).

oneOf.description: Role granted to this token, as decoded from JWT. If token is invalid, field may be null.
Role granted to this token, as decoded from JWT. If token is invalid, field may be null.
Role granted to this token, as decoded from JWT. If token is invalid, field may be null.

role.description: Role granted to this token, as decoded from JWT. If token is invalid, field may be null.

memberId.description: The account/member UUID to which the token is linked (if present and valid).

moderatorId.description: Optional: present if token corresponds to a moderator session (UUID of pol_eco_board_moderators record).

adminId.description: Optional: present if admin role; UUID of pol_eco_board_admins record.

email.description: Email address associated with this account, if applicable and visible according to role.

expiresAt.description: Time (ISO 8601) when the token expires. If token is invalid, may be null.

issuedAt.description: Time (ISO 8601) when the token was issued (JWT 'iat' claim). May be null if token is invalid.

permissions.description: List of permission codes or capabilities granted by this token, as included in JWT or derived from account role. Empty array if none or invalid.

IJwtToken.IResponse.description: Result of JWT token validation. Indicates validity, decoded role info, and (if valid) account identifiers/permissions. Some fields may be omitted or null if invalid.

old_password.description: Current password for the moderator account, used for verification before password update. Must match stored hash for account; required for security.

new_password.description: New password to assign to the account. Must meet the platform's password complexity and security rules (e.g., min length, complexity, etc.). Not stored or returned raw.

IPolEcoBoardModeratorPasswordChange.IUpd.description: Request body to change a moderator's password. Requires old (current) password for verification and new password for update. Platform security/complexity rules enforced.

success.description: Indicates if the moderator password change operation succeeded and password was updated.

message.description: Actionable result message for the password change: explains outcome, policy, and further actions.

IPolEcoBoardModeratorPasswordChange.IRes.description: Response to moderator password update operation. Indicates result and includes explanatory feedback for user/audit.

IPolEcoBoardModeratorTokenRefresh.ICreat.description:
Moderator refresh token submission payload used to obtain new JWT access and refresh tokens. This type is used in the moderator authentication endpoint for token renewal. It requires only the moderator's refresh_token string, which must be valid, unexpired, and not revoked for a session in pol_eco_board_auth_sessions. No other authentication or personal information is included.

This is a security-sensitive operation and the token must be a non-empty string. Never include access token here.

refresh_token.description:
The refresh token string obtained from a previous authentication session. This token must be valid (not expired or revoked) and is cryptographically bound to a specific moderator's account and session.

On submission, the backend will validate the refresh_token and, if successful, issue a new set of JWT access/refresh tokens.

The refresh_token is typically stored in an httpOnly cookie or secure client store and is never shared with other parties.

IPolEcoBoardModeratorTokenRefresh.IRespo.description:
Response payload returned upon successful refresh of a moderator JWT. Contains newly issued access and refresh tokens (usually intended for assignment to httpOnly cookies or Authorization headers).

setHeaders is an object containing the exact HTTP headers (Authorization, Set-Cookie) the client must apply for follow-on authenticated requests with new tokens. Access token values are never shown directly in API or UI output after this operation, except as part of the setHeaders bundle. The client must respect all expiry and security constraints.

IJwtSetHeaders.description: Bundle of HTTP headers to be set by the client upon authentication or token refresh. Typically includes an Authorization header (as 'Bearer <token>') and may include Set-Cookie or other session-relevant headers. Used as a transport mechanism for token issuance in authentication endpoints. Values are sensitive and must be set exactly by the client after authentication workflows.

Authorization.description: The Authorization header value for authenticated requests. Typically this is a Bearer token string such as 'Bearer eyJhb...'. This value must be set by the client for every subsequent protected API call until expiration or revocation of the token. This field is always present for successful authentication.

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.SignUp.description:
Payload for registering a new admin (administrator) account in polEcoBoard. The properties required are the email address and password for the admin account. Both are required fields and must satisfy business and schema validation. The email must be unique platform-wide; the password must be submitted in plaintext and will be hashed server-side.

On successful registration, a member and admin record will be created, subject to registration policy.

email.description: Unique business email address for the admin. Must not be a duplicate of any existing member/admin email. Used for login, notifications, and as the admin's identity in all platform workflows. Must be RFC 5322 compliant and satisfy business email policy (use business domains, not public email if domain enforcement is enabled).

password.description: Initial password for admin registration in plaintext. Sent via secure channel and hashed server-side. Must satisfy platform password minimum length, complexity, and should not be reused from previous credentials. This password is never stored or returned in plaintext.

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.SignUpResponse.description:
Response payload for successful admin registration in polEcoBoard. Contains setHeaders with JWT Authorization and refresh tokens for follow-on authenticated requests. These headers must be set by clients to enable session use. The response does not include any other personal or sensitive account data.

If registration fails, use API errors as per platform convention.

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.SignIn.description:
Payload for admin login (sign-in) in polEcoBoard. Requires both email and password. Email must match an existing active admin account; password must match the stored hash value. Credentials must be provided in plaintext over secure channel. Only active (not deleted or banned) admins will successfully login.

Business and schema validation applies. Login failures must not indicate which field failed (for security).

email.description: The email address associated with the admin account to login. Must exist in the platform database for authentication to proceed.

password.description: The plaintext password for the admin account. This value must match the hash stored in pol_eco_board_members for the account with the specified email address.

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.SignInResponse.description:
Response for successful admin login. Contains setHeaders with newly issued JWT Authorization and refresh tokens (as HTTP header values to be set by the client SDK or frontend). Tokens are typically pushed as an Authorization header and (optional) httpOnly cookie for session management.

On login failure, no setHeaders property is present.

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.SignOutResponse.description: Response for admin sign-out (logout) operation. When successfully called, indicates the active session is revoked and all tokens are no longer valid. No payload is typically returned for logout success. This schema may be used as an empty object for documentation purposes or may be omitted.

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.ValidateToken.description: Request payload for validating an existing JWT token for admin session retention or state check. Accepts the token as a string. Invocation returns the ValidatedTokenResponse structure for success/failure (role, account, session expiry, etc).

token.description: The JWT (access token) to be validated for continued admin session activity. This should be the exact value previously issued at registration/login or refresh. Token validation includes signature, expiration, and role/session integrity checks.

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.ValidateTokenRespo.description: Response structure representing the validity and context of an admin JWT token. Indicates whether the token is valid, account ID (UUID), session expiry (ISO 8601), and role if valid. If not valid, isValid=false and reason explains failure. Used for persistent login UI logic or preflight auth checks.

isValid.description: Indicates whether the provided JWT is valid (signature, expiry, and session status checks pass). True for valid tokens, false otherwise.

accountId.description: The unique identifier of the admin's member account. Only returned when isValid is true.

role.description: Role of the authenticated account. Always 'admin' for this schema.

expiresAt.description: The expiration timestamp for the JWT token in ISO 8601 format. Only present for valid tokens.

reason.description: Human-readable message explaining the reason for validity or, if invalid, the specific failure (e.g., 'Session expired', 'Token revoked', 'Signature invalid'). Only present when isValid=false.

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.ChangePassword.description:
Request structure for updating admin account password. Requires current (old) password and new desired password (in plaintext, never hashed on client). The business logic must validate that the current password matches the stored password_hash, and the new password must meet platform complexity, length, and rotation (not reusing previous password if enforced).

After success, all active sessions are revoked and only the new password may be used for login going forward.

currentPassword.description: The current (old) password for the admin account, submitted to verify existing authentication before allowing update. Must match the password_hash in the stored pol_eco_board_members record.

newPassword.description: The new password (in plaintext) which will be used to replace the existing one after validation and successful update. Must fulfill all business and policy requirements for admin credentials.

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.ChangePasswordResp.description: Response after successfully changing admin password. Confirms password change and indicates that all active sessions have been revoked, requiring re-authentication. Returns only status info, never passwords or tokens.

status.description: Operation result code, always "password_changed" upon success.

message.description: Human-friendly confirmation message, e.g., "Password successfully updated. All sessions revoked; please sign in again with your new credentials."

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.RefreshToken.description:
Request body structure for admin JWT refresh. Contains the refresh_token issued at or after login. Enforces all business/session logic for validity, expiry, and revocation.

Only the exact refresh_token value as issued should be supplied. This operation is required for admin session rotation in secure environments.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token string previously issued in a session for this admin. Must be valid (not revoked or expired) for session rotation to succeed.

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.RefreshTokenRespon.description: Response for refreshing an admin's authentication JWT token in polEcoBoard. This DTO is returned by the admin JWT refresh endpoint (/auth/admin/refresh), which issues new JWT access and refresh tokens and provides them in setHeaders for the client to apply as the Authorization header. No sensitive credential data is exposed. This structure guarantees that after a successful refresh, the client immediately knows which authorization token to use for subsequent requests and can manage session state safely according to security requirements. Only the defined properties below are included in this response. The content is strictly for admin role session/token life-cycle.

setHeaders.description: Object containing new headers the client must set, typically including a valid Authorization header with the new JWT access token. This enables simple, SDK-friendly session continuation in the client post-refresh.

Authorization.description: New JWT access token issued for the admin. To be set in the HTTP Authorization header as 'Bearer <token>' for all subsequent SDK/API requests.

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.ActiveSessions.description: Response structure for an admin's current active authentication sessions. Returned by the endpoint /auth/admin/sessions, which lists all unexpired, unrevoked sessions for the requesting admin. Each session represents a device/browser login, with details for device hygiene, security, audit, and user awareness. This DTO is critical for security-conscious admin users to review all their valid authentication tokens and sessions across multiple devices. Sessions excluded here are those already revoked or expired. The returned property 'sessions' is a required array of session summaries for each active session, used for device management UIs and admin dashboards.

sessions.description: A list of all currently active (unrevoked, unexpired) sessions for the admin user. Each item is a session summary with essential metadata to support session management, device awareness, and audit. The exact structure is per IPolEcoBoardAuthSession.ISummary; see below.

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.RevokeSessionRespo.description: Response for the endpoint /auth/admin/sessions/{sessionId} DELETE, documenting the result of revoking (logging out) a specific admin authentication session. This structure returns information about the revocation event, confirming successful operation, with IDs and status reflecting the affected session. Used for audit trails, admin security dashboards, and client UIs to indicate result of remote session termination. If unsuccessful, an error is returned instead of this DTO. The included properties confirm which session was revoked, previous status, and the new state of the session.

sessionId.description: Unique identifier of the authentication session that was revoked.

revoked.description: True if the session was successfully revoked (invalidated). False if the session was already revoked or could not be revoked (error returned instead of this DTO in such cases).

revokedAt.description: Timestamp when the session was revoked (set to current UTC time of revocation).

IPolEcoBoardAdminAuth.RevokeAllSessionsR.description: Response for the endpoint /auth/admin/tokens/revoke-all POST, which logs out the admin from all devices by revoking (invalidating) all authentication sessions for the admin's member_id. This object confirms the number of sessions that were affected, their status, and provides a list of session IDs involved for verification and audit. Returned after a successful invocation of the 'logout everywhere' function for admins. Clients use this to confirm that no active tokens remain, as part of high-security workflows.

totalRevoked.description: Total number of sessions that were revoked/inactivated as part of this operation.

revokedSessionIds.description: Array of UUIDs listing each session that was revoked during the operation.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a new guest session. Initiate the POST /polEcoBoard/guests endpoint with valid IP address, device fingerprint, and initial consent status. Verify that a guest session record is created and a UUID is returned, and stored fields match the payload for analytics and compliance. Edge case: test with minimal required fields (e.g., IP address only, with device_fingerprint omitted) to validate optional schema. Ensure that privacy policy requirements are enforced, and that repeated calls from same IP/device combination are handled consistently.

Test failure scenario for guest session creation with invalid input. Attempt to create a guest session with improperly formatted IP address or missing required consent status in the payload. Verify the endpoint returns clear, actionable error messages indicating the specific business or validation failure. Ensure no guest session is actually created for invalid input.

Test successful soft deletion of a notification preference by an admin. First, register a new admin and log in to obtain privileges. Next, create a notification preference to have a target record. Then, call the DELETE /polEcoBoard/admin/notificationPreferences/{notificationPreferenceId} endpoint using the created ID and verify the response confirms successful deletion. Finally, confirm that a subsequent GET returns the deleted_at timestamp or that the item is not available in standard searches, ensuring compliance with retention and audit policy.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to gain 'admin' privileges required for this operation.
Login as admin to obtain a valid JWT for authenticating further API calls.
Create a new notification preference to be deleted in this test scenario.

scenario.draft: Test search of all notification failures as a moderator, confirming access to all user failures (not just own) is permitted as per role. Register and log in a moderator, create failures for multiple users (members), and issue a PATCH request to /polEcoBoard/moderator/notificationFailures with a broad filter. Assert that multiple users' failures are visible and that fields not accessible to regular members are shown. Security must ensure no leakage to unauthorized members while providing full results to moderators. Also, test edge cases for filters by failure_code or provider.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as a moderator.
Obtain JWT for a moderator session.
Create at least one member account to simulate other users with notification failures.
Create notification failure records for multiple users as admin, enabling moderator visibility and filter tests.

scenario.draft: Test full search and pagination of all notification failures as an admin. Register and log in as an admin, having several failure records for different members, including across multiple providers, codes, and delivery statuses. Submit a search request with advanced filters (failure_code, provider, status combinations) and verify the response contains failures across all users, full field visibility, correct sorting, and pagination controls for large result sets. Confirm security prevents access to non-admins/moderators. Also, check handling when filtering for non-existent codes or users (should return an empty result).

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as an admin user.
Acquire valid JWT as admin.
Create notification failure records for several different users and scenarios to ensure search realism.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a specific notification failure as a member. Register and log in as two different members. Create a notification failure for each. As member A, call GET on their own notificationFailureId and verify successful retrieval with complete details. Then, attempt to GET member B's notification failure as member A and confirm a permission error or not found is returned, demonstrating row-level security. Validate error responses and audit compliance for unauthorized access attempts.

dependencies.purpose: Register member A.
Log in as member A.
Register member B.
Log in as member B.
Create notification failure records for both member A and member B, referenced by their IDs.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of an anti-spam event record by an admin. First, register an admin and log in. Create a new anti-spam event via POST to obtain a valid antiSpamEventId. Then, update fields such as score, operation, or appeal status using this endpoint and verify that the record is correctly updated in the database. Ensure that business and audit constraints are enforced, and all changes are logged.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration to provide authorized access for updating anti-spam events.
Login as the registered admin to obtain credentials for authorized actions.
Create an anti-spam event entry and extract antiSpamEventId for the update test.

scenario.draft: Test updating an anti-spam event with a non-existent antiSpamEventId. After admin authentication, attempt to update an event using a random or deleted UUID. Confirm the system returns a not-found error and does not corrupt the database. Verify that error messages are precise and audit logging occurs for failed operations.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for permissions.
Login to act with admin credentials.

scenario.draft: Test hard deletion of an anti-spam event by an admin. Register and login as admin, create an anti-spam event, then delete it using this endpoint. Ensure that the event is permanently removed from the database and cannot be retrieved anymore. Confirm audit logs for compliance and that relationships or foreign keys do not cause issues on delete.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration to authorize deletion.
Login as admin to perform the action.
Create an anti-spam event to have a valid antiSpamEventId for deletion.

scenario.draft: Attempt to delete a non-existent anti-spam event by providing an invalid antiSpamEventId. System should return a not-found or similar error without affecting existing records. The test ensures business rules prevent deletion of non-existent records and that error messages are clear.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for proper authorization.
Login as admin to access the endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a paginated list of consent status records with various filter criteria. Register as admin and login. Create several consent status log entries through POST. Then, use this PATCH endpoint to search by provider_key, consent_type, status, region, session id, and time window. Verify responses include only expected records, pagination works, and sensitive information is not leaked. Edge cases: filters with empty result, invalid filter syntax, and searching large datasets.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for permission to query consent statuses.
Login as admin to access protected resources.
Create multiple consent status records for search/filter tests.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a single consent status record by its unique ID. Register and login as admin. Create a consent status log, then fetch it with GET using its returned consentStatusId. Confirm that all expected fields (provider, status, region, audit context) are present, permissions are enforced, and non-admins are denied access.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for sufficient permissions.
Login as admin to use the GET endpoint.
Create a consent status record and obtain consentStatusId.

scenario.draft: Test fetching a non-existent or already-deleted consent status record. After admin authentication, use a random or invalid consentStatusId in the GET request. Ensure system returns an appropriate error (not found), logs the attempt, and does not expose internal details.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for access.
Login as admin.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a user consent status by admin. Register and log in as admin. Use the POST endpoint with valid consent status input (provider_key, consent_type, region, status, session_anon_id, timestamps, audit context). Confirm the returned record is correctly stored, all compliance validations pass, and audit logs are created. Required fields must be present and business logic (such as uniqueness and schema validation) enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to gain write access for consent logs.
Login as the admin for authenticated requests.

scenario.draft: Test rejection and error messaging for attempts to create a consent status with invalid, missing, or inconsistent input data (e.g., unsupported provider_key, missing region or consent_type, schema violation). The system should return detailed validation errors without creating the record, and ensure audit logging for compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for endpoint access.
Login as admin before making invalid creation attempts.

scenario.draft: Test moderator login workflow with both valid and invalid credentials. Start by registering a new moderator account (email, password, display name), ensuring registration succeeds. Attempt to login with correct credentials and validate that JWT tokens are issued and the moderator session is established. Then attempt login with incorrect password, unregistered email, and using an inactive or banned account (where possible), verifying the API returns appropriate errors for each. Assess rate limiting on repeated failed attempts and ensure security information is not leaked in error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new moderator account to allow login with valid credentials.

scenario.draft: Test moderator logout operation, ensuring session tokens are invalidated and unauthorized API access is blocked after logout. Prerequisites include moderator registration and login to obtain JWT. Perform the logout call and ensure the API returns confirmation. Then attempt any protected moderator API with the same token to verify access is denied, confirming session revocation. Repeat with an already-logged-out token to check idempotency and proper error messaging.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator account which will be logged in.
Login as moderator to obtain valid JWT for the logout process.

scenario.draft: Test the token validation logic for moderators. After registering and logging in as a moderator, use the provided JWT to call the validation endpoint and confirm that the token is accepted and the context is correct. Then test this endpoint with expired, revoked (after logout), and clearly malformed JWTs to verify invalid tokens produce correct unauthorized or error responses. Covers both success and various edge failure scenarios.

dependencies.purpose: Create coordinator to obtain a valid JWT via normal onboarding.
Obtain valid moderator JWT for subsequent validation tests.

scenario.draft: Test moderator password change flow. Register and login as a moderator, then submit a valid password change request. After password is changed, verify all sessions are revoked and login is required. Attempt to change password with incorrect current password to validate error handling, and test weak/new password policy enforcement. Attempt protected API action with the old JWT after password change to ensure sessions are properly invalidated by this operation.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator account for password change testing.
Login as moderator to obtain the current JWT token used in password change.

scenario.draft: Test moderator token refresh by registering and logging in to obtain both access and refresh JWTs. Use the refresh token on this endpoint and confirm a new set of tokens is issued. Try using an already used (rotated out) or revoked refresh token to ensure the API returns an error and does not issue new tokens. Include testing of missing or malformed tokens in the request for correct failure handling.

dependencies.purpose: Create a moderator account to enable the login/refresh process.
Obtain refresh and access tokens to test the refresh workflow.

scenario.draft: Test member successful logout. Register a new member, log in to retrieve a valid authentication token, and use this token to log out. Confirm the session is revoked and that the token cannot be used for further authenticated actions (e.g., member validateToken).

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to get credentials for login and session creation.
Login as the registered member to create an authentication session and retrieve JWT token.

scenario.draft: Test member token validation for both success and failure cases. First, register and log in as a member to acquire a valid JWT token, then validate this token (should succeed). Next, after logout, re-validate the same token to confirm it is now invalid. Test validation with malformed or missing tokens to ensure proper error handling.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member to test authentication token flow.
Obtain a JWT token for validation.
Log out to simulate invalidated tokens and test validation failure after logout.

scenario.draft: Test that a member can successfully change their password and all sessions are revoked. Register and log in as a member, then change the password with the correct old password. After password change, confirm that previous tokens are no longer valid (validateToken should fail), and require a fresh login with the new password.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member for the password change flow.
Obtain JWT token required to perform password change.

scenario.draft: Test member password change failure due to incorrect current password. Attempt to change the password using an invalid existing password. The system should return a clear error with no change in account state. Authentication with both old and new passwords should reflect the proper status.

dependencies.purpose: Register a member account to initiate password change test.
Obtain JWT token for the password change attempt.

scenario.draft: Test issuance of a new JWT via refresh token. Register and log in to obtain initial access and refresh tokens. Use the refresh token to request new tokens and ensure the refresh is successful. After prior logout or password change (which revokes sessions), attempt refresh again and confirm correct error code for revoked/invalid refresh token.

dependencies.purpose: Register member account for refresh workflow.
Log in to generate access and refresh tokens.
Optional: Verify that refresh token cannot be used once session is revoked.

scenario.draft: Test successful registration of a new moderator. Provide unique email, valid password, display name, and required consent status. Validate that JWT tokens are issued upon registration and all moderator fields are populated. Follow up with moderator login using the registered credentials to confirm ability to authenticate and use moderator features.

dependencies.purpose: The scenario is for this endpoint; self-register and assert all fields and JWT returned.

scenario.draft: Test registration failure when attempting to register a moderator with an email that is already in use. scenario.draft: Test edge cases where admin tries fetching a report using invalid or non-existent postId or reportId, or with insufficient permissions. Start by registering an admin and ensuring valid login. Attempt to retrieve a report using malformed or random UUIDs for postId/reportId, and verify that appropriate 'not found', 'forbidden', or error messages are returned. This test ensures robust error handling for bad input or unauthorized access.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin for test actions.
Login as admin to get tokens for admin requests.

scenario.draft: As a member, submit a report about a post. Validate that reporting is only allowed for authenticated members and that duplicate reports by the same member for the same post are prevented. The scenario proceeds as follows: First, register and login as a member. Create a post as another member account to ensure the reporting member is not the author, then submit a report (reason code and description) for the post. Verify that the report is created. Try to submit a second report as the same member for the same post and confirm the API returns a duplicate error. This tests report creation flow and de-duplication logic.

dependencies.purpose: Register two members: one for creating the post, one for reporting.
Login as each member to perform actions.
First member creates a new post to allow another member to report it.

scenario.draft: Test post report submission fails for unauthenticated users and for invalid reason codes. Attempt to report a post without authentication and confirm a 401 or forbidden error occurs. Then, while authenticated, try submitting reports with invalid or missing reason codes/descriptions to cause schema validation errors, confirming proper error messaging and enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: A member creates a post beforehand to ensure a valid postId is available for reporting.

scenario.draft: Check moderator role attempting to submit a report with incomplete or invalid fields (e.g., missing reason, reporting own post). Attempt to report a post authored by the same moderator, or submit with missing data, and verify that validation errors or business rule errors are returned as expected.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator, who will create a post and then attempt to report it as self.
Login as moderator for all steps.
Moderator creates a post and then attempts to report it.

scenario.draft: As an admin, attempt to submit a new report for a post. Register as admin, login, and create a post via a member account. Submit a report for that post as the admin. Confirm the report is properly created and that all required fields are enforced. Attempt to submit another report for same post as the same admin and verify duplicate prevention is active. Also test with missing required fields or invalid post to verify business logic and error responses.

dependencies.purpose: Register and login as admin to obtain tokens.
Login as admin for subsequent actions.
Register member to create a post.
Login as member for post creation.
Member creates a post for admin to report.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can fetch the full editable and audit history for a specific post. Prerequisites include registering an admin account, logging in to obtain authorization, creating a member post, and generating several post edits (edits recorded in history). Scenario should ensure correct filtering and pagination behavior, return of all allowed audit metadata, and testing against a post with a rich history of edits. Includes checking empty result for posts with no edits and access denial if admin is unauthorized or improperly authenticated.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account with valid credentials to obtain admin privileges for subsequent operations.
Log in with the newly created admin to obtain valid JWT for authorized actions.
Register a member account, which is needed to create a post as a normal user.
Authenticate as the member in order to create a post in the system.
Create the original post to be used as the subject for edit history.
Generate one or more post edits to populate the edit history for the post. This must be performed after post creation and by an authorized user (the author, moderator, or admin).

scenario.draft: Validate that a post's author (member) can fetch the full detail of a single edit made to their post. Steps: member registration, login, post creation, post edit creation, then querying the postEditId as the member. Should ensure all historical edit content, rationale, actor, and timestamp fields are present, and that access control restricts viewing solely to permitted actors (author, moderator, admin).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member to act as post author.
Login as member to gain authorization.
Create the base post that will be used for subsequent edits.
Create one or more edits to the post to generate edit history, returning postEditId for use in detailed fetch.

scenario.draft: Ensure that a random member (not the post author and with no moderator/admin privileges) cannot access the edit history of another member's post edit via this endpoint (403 forbidden). Steps: register post author, register a second member, create post/edit as first member, then attempt to access post edit detail as the second member.

dependencies.purpose: Register the post author.
Login as the post author.
Create a post as the author.
Create an edit to the post as the author.
Register a second member that is unrelated to the post.
Log in as the second member before making access attempt.

scenario.draft: Verify that a moderator can access the detail of any post edit (including those not authored by themselves), regardless of post authorship, for audit and compliance purposes. Process: register a moderator, login as moderator, produce a member post and edit, then use the moderator endpoint to retrieve the edit detail and confirm full data access including actor, content, reason, and timestamps. Should validate permission enforcement and prohibit access to non-existent edit IDs.

dependencies.purpose: Register and onboard a new moderator account.
Authenticate the moderator to receive JWT.
Register a member for normal user actions.
Login as the member for post and edit creation.
Use the member account to create a post.
Member creates a post edit to supply postEditId for moderator inspection.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve complete details for any post edit, regardless of author or moderator, confirming full permission. Scenario: create an admin, login, produce a member post and post edit, then retrieve postEditId detail as admin to confirm access. Should also validate error response for non-existent or deleted postEditId.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin user for system-level access.
Admin login to obtain authorization.
Register a standard member to author the post to be edited.
Member login to write a post.
Create the post for editing and history.
Produce one or more edits for the post so that the admin has something to review.

scenario.draft: Ensure a member can create an edit record for a post they authored. Steps: member registration, login, post creation, post edit operation. Validate correct audit, editor ID match, and that the new edit is visible in post edit history. Also cover that creating multiple edits correctly appends history entries and increments version/revision counters where relevant.

dependencies.purpose: Register member account who will author the post.
Login as the member for authorization.
Author creates a post for subsequent editing.

scenario.draft: Verify a member cannot create an edit record for a post they do not own (permission denied scenario). Steps: two separate member accounts, first creates post, second attempts to create an edit for the other's post - should return forbidden error for second member.

dependencies.purpose: Register the post author.
Login as the post author.
Create the post as first member.
Register a second (non-author) member.
Login as the second member prior to attempting the unauthorized edit.

scenario.draft: Test updating a specific incident record by its unique ID as an admin. First, register an admin account and log in to acquire the necessary authorization. Create a new incident record to obtain a valid incidentId. Attempt a successful update by changing the description or status (e.g., set it to 'resolved') and verify the changes persist in the system. Also, attempt to update immutable properties such as the incident code or creation timestamp to verify that such operations are correctly rejected with validation errors. Additionally, check that only admins are permitted to perform updates, and attempts by other roles or unauthenticated users result in appropriate permission errors.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to acquire admin-level system access required to update an incident.
Log in as admin to acquire a valid JWT token for authorization.
Create a new incident to obtain a valid incidentId for the update operation.

scenario.draft: Test hard deletion of an incident record by its unique incidentId as a super-admin. Begin by registering and logging in as an admin. Create an incident to ensure there is at least one incident record to delete. Attempt to delete the incident and verify it is removed from the list of incidents. Check that all related compliance, auditing, and reporting rules are enforced (e.g., mandatory logging of deletion with rationale). Test error responses for attempts to delete non-existent, already deleted, or unauthorized record deletions; ensure such attempts yield clear error messages. Validate that only an admin can perform this deletion operation and that other user types receive a permission denied error.

dependencies.purpose: Register a super-admin/admin user to perform the incident deletion operation.
Authenticate as the admin to perform privileged operations.
Create a new incident entry, providing a valid incidentId for the deletion test.

scenario.draft: Test searching and retrieving maintenance window events using filtering, sorting, and pagination as an admin. Register and log in as an admin first. Create multiple maintenance window records with varying codes, impact types, and time windows. Perform a search query without filters, then with specific filters such as time range, status, and code to verify correct results. Validate the pagination and sorting behaviors. Also, test edge cases such as invalid filter syntax, empty results, and permission denial for unauthenticated users.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to ensure appropriate permissions to search maintenance windows.
Admin login to obtain JWT for authorization.
Create one or more maintenance window events for search and filtering tests.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of a single maintenance window record by its unique ID as an admin. First, register and log in as an admin. Create a new maintenance window and use its ID to fetch the record with the GET method, ensuring the returned details match exactly what was stored. Attempt retrieval of a non-existent or deleted maintenanceWindowId and confirm the system returns a not-found error. Finally, confirm access is restricted to admins and unauthorized requests are rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user for authorized access.
Log in as admin to gain authorization.
Create a new maintenance window to provide a valid maintenanceWindowId for the GET test.

scenario.draft: Test creating a new maintenance window via admin endpoint. Register and log in as an admin to obtain authorization. Submit valid creation data and verify the maintenance window is correctly stored with all specified details. Attempt to create another maintenance window with conflicting or invalid input (such as overlapping windows or invalid time range) and check that the API returns the expected validation errors. Also, confirm that only admins can perform creation and unauthenticated or unauthorized requests are denied.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin as prerequisite for maintenance window creation.
Log in as admin to obtain the JWT required for authorized creation requests.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving a filtered and paginated list of historical board change events as a moderator. Ensure realistic moderator authentication by registering and logging in as a moderator first. Create one or more boards (requires an admin to create categories and boards), perform board changes to generate board history records (such as moving a board to a different category or editing board metadata through the admin). Then, as an authenticated moderator, perform a PATCH request to fetch board history using various filters (by change type, actor, time range, board, category, etc.) and verify: (1) Board history returns only events moderator has access to; (2) Filters, sorting, and pagination operate as expected; (3) Edge cases such as no results, invalid filters, or forbidden access are handled with proper errors; (4) Audit compliance and operational constraints are present.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator for authentication context.
Log in as the registered moderator to perform authorized queries.
Register a new admin (needed to create board categories and boards for context data).
Admin login for authentication.
Create board categories for board creation and assignment (must precede board creation).
Create discussion boards linked to categories, so history records can exist.
Generate board history entries by performing board migration or category changes as admin.

scenario.draft: Verify admin's ability to search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of board change history events. Register and log in as admin, ensure several board changes to establish a meaningful audit log. Use a PATCH request to /polEcoBoard/admin/boardHistories with a variety of filters (change_type, actor, board, category, date interval), confirming: (1) Admin can view all relevant history entries; (2) Filtering and pagination work as specified; (3) Access is denied for unauthorized roles; (4) Robust input validation and error messaging for improper filter parameters or missing context.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for authentication context.
Admin login to obtain appropriate permissions.
Create board categories as prerequisites for board creation.
Create boards within categories so that history events can be generated.
Create board history records by performing valid structural changes as admin.

scenario.draft: Test fetching the full details of a board change history event by its ID as a moderator. Register a moderator and log in, ensure relevant board histories exist (created via admin actions), then as the moderator, call GET on /polEcoBoard/moderator/boardHistories/{boardHistoryId} using a valid history ID. Expect: (1) Moderator receives all permitted details and references (board, categories, actor, rationale); (2) Invalid or unauthorized history IDs return not found or permission error; (3) Edge case of non-existent or deleted IDs handled correctly; (4) Permission matrix is enforced – moderator only sees records according to business rules.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator to execute authenticated requests.
Login as moderator for auth context.
Register an admin for board and history creation.
Authenticate as admin.
Create categories needed for boards.
Create boards and assign categories.
Generate board history records that can be fetched by moderator.

scenario.draft: Test the ability for a moderator to soft-delete (archive) a board status record. Register and log in as a moderator, ensure a valid board and an associated status event exist (admin must create category and board, then a moderator status event is created). As the moderator, delete the existing board status event by its ID and verify: (1) The event is marked deleted (deleted_at set); (2) Deleted event is no longer visible in active listings but retained for audit; (3) Attempts to delete non-existent, already-deleted, or unauthorized IDs return correct error responses; (4) Proper compliance logging is performed for moderation action.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator for test authentication.
Moderator login for secure operations.
Admin registration for board/category creation.
Admin login for setup.
Create a category as the context for board.
Create board linked to category.
Moderator creates a board status event to set up for deletion.

scenario.draft: Verify as admin the ability to soft-delete a board status event. Register and log in as admin, ensure a board and a relevant status exist (by creating category, board, and a board status event via another admin or moderator). Then perform a DELETE on /polEcoBoard/admin/boardStatuses/{boardStatusId} to archive the status event. Validate: (1) Event is flagged with deleted_at, not physically deleted; (2) It becomes inaccessible from active board status queries; (3) Audit trail logs are updated for compliance; (4) Edge cases such as attempting to delete already-deleted or non-existent status IDs are handled safely with business-meaningful errors; (5) Action is denied for users without admin role.

dependencies.purpose: Admin registration for authentication context.
Admin login to establish permissions.
Create a category as prerequisite for boards.
Create discussion board used in status event.
Create a board status event as admin or by assigning a moderator, so that a status event exists for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can search and retrieve escalation records filtered by various attributes, such as status, actor, rationale, and date range. Verify that only escalations visible to the moderator (based on their role and board assignments) are returned. Ensure pagination and sorting work as intended. Test for no-result scenarios and input validation errors (e.g., invalid filter fields). Attempting to search with insufficient privileges should result in a permission error. Edge cases include very large result sets and filtering for deleted or restricted escalation records.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator account to provide authentication for escalation search.
Login as the moderator to obtain the JWT required for authenticated requests.
Create one or more escalation records as test data to validate search filters and pagination.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator can retrieve full details of a specific escalation record by its escalationId, provided the record is visible within their role scope. Attempt to fetch a non-existent escalationId and verify a not-found error is returned. Attempt to access an escalation outside the moderator's assignment or privilege scope and verify that a permission denied error is provided. Edge cases should include attempting to access deleted or finalized escalations and verifying appropriate error handling and audit logging.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator for authentication context.
Authenticate as the moderator.
Create escalation records by admin for association and access verification.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve the detail of an escalation record by escalationId. Validate that all business and relational fields are included in the response. Attempt to fetch an escalationId that does not exist and verify the system responds with a clear not-found error. Confirm access is denied if an invalid or non-admin token is used in the request. Edge cases include requests for deleted, closed, or escalations unrelated to the current admin.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to create and access escalation records.
Login as admin for authorized session/context.
Create escalation records for test case validation.

scenario.draft: Test that a moderator is able to create a new escalation event using valid data. Validations include: referencing an existing moderation action, specifying the correct escalatorId (current moderator), assigning a valid recipient admin, providing business rationale, and initializing status according to business logic. Verify rejection for non-existent target moderation actions, invalid adminId, missing rationale, or authentication failure. Duplicate or unauthorized escalation attempts (e.g., by a member or with locked moderation action) should be denied and yield appropriate error responses. Resulting record should reflect the submitted data and be available in search endpoints.

dependencies.purpose: Register the moderator who will perform the escalation.
Login the moderator for session authentication.
Register an admin to act as recipient of the escalation.
Login as the admin recipient (if required for association context).
Create a sample moderation action to reference during escalation creation.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully create a new escalation event, specifying a valid moderation action, rationale, escalatorId (admin or moderator), and recipient admin. Validate required fields and verify correct handling of input errors such as missing rationale, referencing non-existent moderation actions, or invalid assignment. Ensure proper error messages are presented for each case. Confirm that the escalation record is persisted, all required metadata and relationships are established, and the event appears in downstream search and detail APIs.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin, who will perform escalation creation.
Authenticate as admin for escalation creation and target association.
Register a moderator to supply as an escalator or as the subject of moderation action.
Create a suitable moderation action record for association with the escalation event.

scenario.draft: Test retrieving detailed information for a specific board status event as a moderator. The scenario begins with the registration and login of a moderator, then a board status event is created (using moderator privileges), and finally the status is retrieved by its boardStatusId. Key verifications include successful retrieval when the event exists and proper permissions, error response when the boardStatusId does not exist, and forbidden access for users with insufficient permissions (non-moderator, non-admin roles). Also test access to already deleted or soft-deleted status events.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator account for permission to create and access board status events.
Login as moderator to obtain necessary authentication token.
Create a new board status event and obtain the boardStatusId for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a new board status event as a moderator. The scenario should cover: 1) successful creation with valid data (after moderator registration and login), 2) creation attempt with missing or invalid required fields (such as missing boardId, invalid status type, or missing rationale), 3) creation with reference to a non-existent board, and 4) forbidden or unauthorized attempts by a non-moderator role. Also, ensure business rules such as status-type transitions are enforced, and error messages are descriptive.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator account to be able to create a board status event.
Login as moderator to obtain authentication for creating events.
Create a board as a prerequisite for a valid boardId reference when testing valid creation scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test the creation of a board status event as an admin user. This scenario includes: 1) successful creation after registering and logging in as admin, 2) input validation failure (e.g., missing rationale or invalid status type), 3) attempt to create status for a non-existent board, 4) verifying that admin-only events cannot be performed by users with lower roles, and 5) business rule errors such as status transition not allowed. Additionally, validate audit logging and rationale requirements are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account for privileged board status events.
Login as admin to allow creating board statuses.
Establish a valid board for status creation and boardId referencing.

scenario.draft: Test updating details of an existing board status event as a moderator. Scenarios include: 1) successful update when boardStatusId exists and the moderator is authorized, 2) attempt to update with invalid or missing fields, 3) attempt to update an event after allowed edit window (if applicable), 4) updating a deleted or non-existent status event, and 5) permission errors when performed by non-moderators. Ensure audit trail is updated accordingly and business rules for allowed updates are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register moderator for performing update operations.
Login as moderator to obtain authentication token.
Create a board status event and obtain boardStatusId that will be updated.

scenario.draft: Test the admin update of a board status event for compliance and operational changes. Begin by registering and logging in as admin, then create a board and associated board status. Test cases should include: 1) valid update by admin (e.g., correcting rationale or time), 2) validation errors for missing/invalid fields, 3) update attempts on soft-deleted or non-existent status events, 4) permission error for non-admin roles, and 5) verify that changes are correctly reflected in audit logs and business rules regarding editability are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin user to perform status updates.
Login as admin to get authentication token.
Create a board so a valid board status can be associated and created.
Create board status event using admin privileges to obtain boardStatusId.

scenario.draft: Test successful update of an existing maintenance window by admin. Start with admin registration and login to obtain credentials. Create a new maintenance window via POST to get a valid maintenanceWindowId. Execute PUT with modified fields (e.g., updated start/end time, updated impact description, notification timestamps). Verify the response contains updated fields, audit log is appended, and inference checks for time window and policy are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to obtain permissions for maintenance operations.
Authenticate as the registered admin to obtain a JWT for subsequent requests.
Create a new maintenance window to supply a valid maintenanceWindowId for update testing.

scenario.draft: Test update failure when start time is after end time, which violates business logic. Begin with admin registration, login, and creation of a maintenance window. Attempt to update the maintenance window by submitting a payload where the start time is after the end time. Check that the response returns a validation error, and that the record is not updated.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for API authentication.
Login as the admin to authorize requests.
Create a maintenance window in advance to retrieve a valid maintenanceWindowId.

scenario.draft: Test admin ability to soft-delete (archive) a maintenance window. Perform admin registration, login, and create a maintenance window. Then, call DELETE on the new maintenanceWindowId. Assert that the deleted_at field is set, the maintenance window is marked as deleted, and that subsequent retrievals or listings do not include the deleted window (unless filter includes deleted).

dependencies.purpose: Provision a new admin account for permissioned API access.
Authenticate as admin to enable authorized actions.
Establish a maintenance window to obtain a valid maintenanceWindowId for deletion test.

scenario.draft: Test admin ability to search and paginate service metrics with various combinations of filters and sorting. After registering and logging in as admin, create several service metrics records using POST. Use PATCH to search with different query parameters (e.g., filtering by metric_code, date range, or sorting by created date). Validate that the correct filtered subset and pagination structures are returned, including metadata about total records and pages.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user for permissions.
Obtain an authenticated session as admin.
Add multiple service metric records so the search endpoint returns non-empty results.

scenario.draft: Test the successful retrieval of a single service metric's full details by an admin. Perform admin registration, login, and create a service metric record, then make a GET request referencing its serviceMetricId. Confirm the returned object matches the created record, including all summary and detail fields. Verify proper error handling if a non-existent or deleted serviceMetricId is used.

dependencies.purpose: Ensure admin privileges for secure endpoints.
Ensure authenticated admin session.
Create a new service metric to generate and retrieve a valid serviceMetricId for detail testing.

scenario.draft: Test successful creation of a service metric by an authenticated admin. After admin registration and login, use POST with valid metric_code, value, window, and all required fields consistent with schema rules. Confirm that the record is saved and all validations (uniqueness per code/time, value type) are enforced.

dependencies.purpose: Create an admin user to enable metric record creation.
Login as admin to acquire JWT authentication context.

scenario.draft: Test the ability of an admin to search and retrieve a paginated list of discussion boards with advanced filters. Ensure filtering works by category ID, board code, display name, status, and display order. Verify sorting and pagination (page, limit) return correct data slices. Include edge case testing for empty results, non-existent filters (e.g., invalid category), invalid pagination values, and that only boards linked to existing categories are returned. Proper permission enforcement is expected, and non-admin access should be denied. Results must provide the expected board schema details and reflect current database state.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account. Only admins can access this search endpoint.
Log in as an admin to obtain credentials for subsequent requests.
Create at least one board category for use as a valid filter and to link boards to this category. This precedes board creation and search.
Create one or more boards, referencing the created categories, to test the filtering/search functionality.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve the full details of a specific discussion board by its unique boardId. Prepare a board via the creation endpoint, then request its detail using the GET endpoint. Verify that the response contains all business fields: id, category link, board name, code, description, visibility, archive status, display order, and timestamps. Negative scenarios: attempt retrieval with a non-existent boardId (should return not found error), use an invalid UUID format (should return validation error), and attempt access as non-admin (should return forbidden/permission-denied error).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin for authentication.
Admin login for permissioned access.
Create a category; required for board creation.
Create a board to provide a valid boardId for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test board creation by an admin with both valid and invalid input data. For success, provide a valid categoryId, board name (2–60 chars), unique code (2–30 chars, lowercase/underscored), description, visibility, archive state, and display order. Verify response matches the persisted DTO. For failure scenarios: supply non-existent categoryId (should return referential integrity error), duplicate board name or code (should return uniqueness error), missing/invalid required fields (should return validation errors), and attempt creation as non-admin (should return forbidden). Ensure business rules such as linkage to valid category and uniqueness are fully validated.

dependencies.purpose: Register admin account to gain board creation privileges.
Admin login to obtain authorization.
Create a category to use its categoryId when creating the board.

scenario.draft: Test updating a discussion board by id as an admin. Cover success scenario by changing fields such as category, board name/code, description, public/archive flags, and display order with valid data—confirm response reflects changes accurately. Test edge cases: updating with duplicate name or code (should return uniqueness conflict), invalid category id (should fail with referential integrity error), updating with missing required fields (should fail with descriptive error), and using non-existent boardId (should return not found). Also verify that permission is enforced (non-admins cannot update a board) and audit trail/logging is maintained.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account for update privileges.
Authenticate as admin for authorized requests.
Create at least two categories to allow board category changes in the update process.
Create a board instance to provide a target for the update.

scenario.draft: Test the soft delete (archive) of a board by boardId as an admin. On success, ensure the deleted_at field is set and the board is not shown in active listings but remains for audit and possible restoration. Edge cases include: deleting a non-existent or already deleted board (should return appropriate error), attempting delete with insufficient permissions (non-admins or unauthorized roles should fail), and verifying the business logic constraints (cannot delete a board that does not meet certain criteria, e.g., if referenced in a mandatory workflow, should be blocked). All delete actions must be fully audited.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin to access the delete endpoint.
Admin login for permissioned operations.
Create a category to allow board creation.
Create a board that will be targeted for deletion.

scenario.draft: Test viewing a notification as a moderator. First, register a new moderator and log in to obtain a JWT token. Next, create a notification assigned to that moderator using the admin API. Retrieve the notification using the moderator's token and verify all appropriate metadata is returned, access is allowed, and privacy protections are enforced. Also, attempt to access a notification with an invalid or unauthorized ID, and as a non-owner, confirming correct error handling for not-found and forbidden cases.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new moderator account with valid details. Required for any moderator-level operations.
Log in as the newly registered moderator to obtain JWT for authentication.
Register a new admin account for admin-level operations.
Log in as admin to obtain admin JWT for notification creation.
Create a notification event assigned to the moderator. Used as the target in view scenarios.

scenario.draft: Test admin access for notification records. Register and log in as admin. Create several notification events targeting different members and moderators. Fetch individual notifications by their IDs and confirm all metadata and business fields are present, including delivery and event status. Test access to both valid and invalid IDs, including attempting to retrieve a notification that does not belong to the admin or does not exist, ensuring appropriate error responses are given.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account, required for all admin role scenarios.
Log in as admin and obtain credentials for subsequent API calls.
Create notification records to test retrieval and permission boundaries.

scenario.draft: Test the creation of a notification event by an admin. Register and log in as an admin. Attempt to create notification records using valid data for event type, recipient, and status, and verify successful creation with correct returned fields. Next, attempt to create notifications with missing required fields, invalid event types, or non-existent recipient IDs, and check that validation errors are returned with descriptive messages as per business logic.

dependencies.purpose: Register an admin account so that notification creation is permitted.
Authenticate as admin to obtain required credentials for notification creation.

scenario.draft: Test updating a notification as a member. First, register a new member and log in to obtain credentials. Create a notification via the admin for this member. Attempt to update permissible fields in the notification and verify success, audit trail, and correct response structure. Test failure scenarios by trying to update a notification not belonging to the member, or supplying invalid values (unsupported event_type or status), and ensure the API enforces permissions and input validation.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new member account for use as the notification recipient.
Log in as the member to obtain authentication token for updates.
Register an admin to allow notification creation.
Admin login, required to create notifications for the member.
Create a notification for the member, which will be used in update and error scenarios.

scenario.draft: Validate notification update functionality for a moderator. Register and log in as a moderator. Admin creates a notification assigned to this moderator. Update allowed notification properties as moderator and verify all changes persist, status updates are reflected, and changes are properly audited. Also, attempt to update notifications that belong to other accounts or supply invalid updates (such as improper statuses or unsettable fields), and confirm proper error handling and access controls.

dependencies.purpose: Register a moderator, needed for moderator-authenticated API usage.
Obtain moderator JWT for authorization.
Set up an admin for notification event creation.
Log in as admin to create notifications for moderators.
Create one or more notifications for the moderator, as the target of update actions.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can successfully update allowed metadata fields (such as context or compliance note) for an existing account audit record. The scenario starts by registering a new admin, logging in, creating an account audit record for a target, and then issuing a PUT with updated compliance metadata. Confirm the returned object reflects the changed values and audit history is preserved. Required ordering: admin registration -> login -> create account audit -> update.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to allow account audit update operations.

The test validates the update is reflected in the response and that appropriate audit trails or status changes have occurred. Dependencies reflect the need for admin registration, authentication, and initial notification creation for update context.

Also, verify pagination (limit, page) is respected. Edge cases: no results for non-existing filter parameters. Validate that unauthorized (non-admin) requests are rejected, ensuring role-based access control functions correctly.

scenario.draft: Test creation of a valid sanction by a moderator. This requires proper privilege escalation through moderator registration and login, after which the moderator attempts to sanction a member with a valid moderation action reference. Ensure all business constraints, including that the moderator is active and the sanction does not conflict with existing ones. On success, validate sanction fields, correct linkage to moderation action, and compliance/audit trails.

The API should return an error specifying invalid or missing references, preserving system integrity. Validate error message clarity and that no sanction is created in the backend.

dependencies.purpose: Provision a moderator account for privilege-checked usage of moderator routes.

Then, update allowed fields, such as extending duration or editing rationale. Confirm that immutable fields (e.g., creation timestamp, original reference IDs) are preserved, audit trail records the update, and the sanction record reflects the new values.

This ensures compliance deletion flows work as expected.

Use PATCH to search by specific fields (status, reason, moderator, time range), verifying that pagination works correctly, only authorized records are returned, and filtering logic matches business rules. Validate correct total count, paging metadata, and that edge cases such as no matches and invalid filters are handled with business-friendly error messages.

The scenario should ensure access is limited to moderators and that correct report summaries are returned based on filter criteria. Edge cases such as no results, invalid filters, or high-volume data should be included. Failure cases must cover attempts by non-moderator users and use of invalid postId parameters, with appropriate error responses. The scenario should also verify that business rule boundaries are respected (e.g., only reports belonging to the specific post are included).

The test should verify successful retrieval, correct data structure, and correct pagination metadata. Edge cases should include empty result sets, non-existent or deleted posts, and excessive pagination limits. Failure scenarios include invalid admin authentication, insufficient permissions, and improper input data (e.g., invalid filters, malformed postId). Business logic must ensure only authorized admins access this sensitive report data.

Edge cases should include attempts to access a report not belonging to the specified post, requests for non-existent or deleted reports, and permission violations (e.g., regular member or unauthorized user attempting the request). Ensure error handling provides explicit responses for each failure case, and successful retrieval aligns with business transparency and privacy rules.

This ensures that only admins can update guest sessions as defined by compliance and privacy requirements.
